Careers that change lives start here. Medtronic is a global leader in healthcare technology with a Mission to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life. Our 95,000 employees work across more than 150 countries to put patients first — developing innovative medical technologies that improve the lives of 72+ million patients each year. Your unique talents will help shape the future of healthcare while building a career grounded in purpose, growth, and impact.

A Day in the Life

Medtronic, a global leader in medical technology, services, and solutions, is seeking an accomplished and experienced Quality Engineering Manager to join our innovative team at the Lafayette, CO site. This position will oversee the surgical operating unit’s new product development quality team. A primary responsibility within this role is people management, which includes mentoring, developing, and coaching staff to meet or exceed performance expectations and program commitments. The role also involves providing strategic leadership to prioritize departmental initiatives, setting performance goals and targets, conducting performance reviews, and holding one-on-one meetings to support performance management and employee development aligned with departmental objectives.

The preferred candidate will possess extensive leadership experience in Quality New Product Development, including expertise in reliability science, reliability planning and testing, hardware/software risk management, design controls, and regulatory compliance within the medical device industry. The successful applicant must demonstrate strong teamwork abilities, initiative, curiosity, and the capacity for rapid learning. This position is integral to the medical device development process, ensuring patient safety throughout the entire product lifecycle.

Job Description field

Primary Responsibilities

  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of engineering professionals, including performance management, career development, promotion recommendations, and compensation planning.
  • Guide project-level decisions by gathering technical input, evaluating risk, and resolving disagreements between Quality, Research and Development, and other cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Drive quality improvement initiatives and establish consistent risk management and reliability practices across supported programs.
  • Direct and guide employees in the design and development of medical device products or software systems.
  • Develops and improves objectives, policies, processes, and standards to support strategy and drive functional excellence through best practices.
  • Continuously assesses team member deliverables and documentation quality across all phases of product development.
  • Selects, hires, and develops personnel, aligning talent to programs to support efficient operations of the function
  • Collaborates across functions and businesses while balancing divergent objectives to gain cooperation of other parties
  • Management of departmental budget
  • Builds strong cross-functional partnerships and leads the team in developing and maintaining risk management files, including risk management plans and reports, while ensuring regular and effective risk reviews.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree and 7+ years of relevant experience, including 5+ years of managerial experience, OR an advanced degree and 5+ years of relevant experience, including 5+ years of managerial experience.
  • Experience leading and developing technical professionals, including performance management, career development, and resource allocation.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in product risk management, reliability engineering, or quality engineering.
  • Experience working within the medical device industry or another highly regulated industry, such as aerospace.
  • Experience leading cross-functional technical decisions involving Engineering, Quality, or product development stakeholders.
  • Experience supporting New Product Development within the medical device industry.
  • Experience applying product risk management practices throughout the design and development lifecycle.
  • Experience leading reliability engineering activities for complex products or systems.
  • Experience resolving technical or quality disagreements across Research and Development and Quality teams.
  • Experience developing and executing organizational strategy or quality improvement initiatives.
  • Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Six Sigma/DRM Green Belt or equivalent certification, AAMI design control certification is preferred

description:

Job Description:

Primary Purpose


Reporting to the Associate Director, Parking, Grounds and Transportation, the Supervisor, Grounds Services is accountable for the day-to-day operations of the Grounds section of the Plant Operations department. This includes planning, development, implementation, and coordination of overall maintenance of the turf, horticultural areas, naturalized areas, water courses and features, paved and other hard surfaces on the University’s Campus Grounds, Research and Technology Park and Satellite Campuses. These duties have to be carried out in an efficient, reliable, and safe manner in accordance with University policies and all applicable legislative requirements.

University of Waterloo infrastructure comprises of nearly 1200 acres of land with over eight million square feet of space powered by a 1st Class High Pressure Power plant feeding a sophisticated district energy system located on over a thousand acres of land.

Responsibilities will align with Plant Operations’ goal of contributing towards providing a safe and accessible, invitingly clean and comfortable, functionally-enriched and well-maintained campus environment through service excellence.

Key Accountabilities

Planning & Financial Management

  • Supports the Associate Director (AD) in the development of long-term planning efforts, addressing stewardship responsibilities, and long-term sustainability of the University’s campus, facilities, and infrastructure, maximizing opportunities for efficient delivery of campus services and optimal investments in University–wide infrastructure.
  • Participates in departmental budget preparation and review process including major repairs, material needs, equipment purchases, and staff allocation (focus on soft and hardscaping).

Operations Management

  • Coordinates, schedules, instructs, and supervises unionized staff in a manner that ensures proper maintenance of all University roads, walks, parking lots, turfed areas, water courses and features, trees, flowers, shrubs in the summer period and snow and ice control in the winter period.
  • Coordinates the assignment of available staff resources; providing clear instruction, tools, materials, training as required, evaluation of results and any corrective action, as necessary.
  • Enforces the use of safe operating procedures, adherence to applicable codes and standards, and creates new processes as needed.
  • Supports the AD in selection of outside contractors and consultants for projects and activities that cannot be completed with assigned staff.
  • Liaises with various University stakeholders providing support and services in a client-focused, service-oriented manner.
  • Ensures that comments, requests, or complaints are addressed professionally and in a timely manner.
  • Oversees delivery of area-specific grounds services at remote locations such as Aberfoyle, Pharmacy, Stratford, Cambridge, Rockwood, Spongy Lake, Research and Technology Park.
  • Provides technical support to the grounds summer operation identifying areas for repairs, upgrades or changes.
  • In coordination with the Supervisor Grounds and Fleet, ensures that grounds department responds to all weather-related events to provide safe access to campus (snow, ice, floods, wind related debris).
  • Oversees the maintenance of all University roads and pathways.

Management of green areas (softscape)

  • Oversees the maintenance of playing fields including field equipment acquisition and installation (excluding turf maintenance).
  • Provides support with ongoing rehabilitation and maintenance of the UW Environmental Reserve.
  • Supervises wildlife management initiatives on campus within the means and resources available as outlined by the Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources.
  • Coordinates environmental maintenance efforts to protect University lands ie. water level control, erosion control measures, and storm water pond maintenance. Supports the AD in coordination of efforts with the City of Waterloo and the region.
  • Supports the development, updates and implementation of the Region of Waterloo Smart on Salt program.
  • Oversee the use of pesticides, herbicides and fertilizers of campus.

Project Management

  • Manages special projects as assigned through the Work Order system or as requested by the Associate Director
  • Supports the AD consulting with departments to develop scope of work ensuring feasibility of requested work.
  • Prepares project plan, coordinates activities, and follows sound procurement processes when ordering materials and contracting services.
  • Provides input and technical advice regarding landscape design on large projects and campus wide initiatives.
  • Manages the development of programs for control of invasive species on all UW campuses.

HR & Staff Management

  • Fosters a client-focused, service-oriented, positive work environment, ensuring the wellbeing and workplace health and safety for all employees.
  • Coaches, trains, and manages the performance and productivity of assigned staff, issuing disciplinary measures in accordance with UW Policy and the CUPE Local 793 Collective Agreement if needed, escalating to the Associate Director if appropriate.
  • Responds to grievances when they arise, recommending resolutions in accordance with the collective agreement.
  • Provides recommendation on skill makeup and staffing requirements for recruitment of new fulltime, temporary, and seasonal employees.
  • Participates in talent acquisition for assigned division.
  • Ensures all staff are current with mandatory training as outlined by the Safety Office.

Health & Safety

  • Active in health and safety and incident prevention by establishing, adhering to, and ensuring assigned support staff are following departmental policy, procedures and safe work practices required by the University health, safety, and environmental management system (HSEMS), and in accordance with relevant health and safety legislation, developing and enhancing a safety culture among support staff.
  • Performs inspections of the workplace and the investigation of workplace accidents in accordance with UW Health & Safety programs.
  • Ensures that application of chemical use withing assigned group (pesticide, fertilizer, etc.) is in compliance with government regulations and the Pesticide Act.


Required Qualifications


  • Niagara Parks Diploma and/or equivalent horticultural certification
  • Extensive knowledge of hard and soft landscaping and maintenance required
  • Arborist trade certificate is preferable (MTCU, ISA)
  • Pesticide Land Exterminator’s license Class 1 and 3
  • 3-5 years of progressive experience in an organization with substantial grounds infrastructure
  • Experience supervising staff preferably in unionized environment
  • Knowledge of year-round grounds operations and procedures to assemble crews with the proper qualifications/ licenses/training to maintain the University campus and outlying areas in all weather conditions.
  • Sound technical knowledge to effectively and safety manage substantial grounds infrastructure
  • Excellent communication skills with a deep commitment to customer service
  • Demonstrated ability to take initiative and incorporate innovation
  • Exemplary organizational skills
  • Strong problem-solving skills is critical
  • Intermediate skill level in the following programs: MS Word, Excel, Outlook, ARCHIBUS

Equity Statement

The University of Waterloo acknowledges that much of our work takes place on the traditional territory of the Neutral, Anishinaabeg, and Haudenosaunee peoples. Our main campus is situated on the Haldimand Tract, the land granted to the Six Nations that includes six miles on each side of the Grand River. Our active work toward reconciliation takes place across our campuses through research, learning, teaching, and community building, and is coordinated within the Office of Indigenous Relations.

The University values the diverse and intersectional identities of its students, faculty, and staff. The University regards equity and diversity as an integral part of academic excellence and is committed to accessibility for all employees. The University of Waterloo seeks applicants who embrace our values of equity, anti-racism and inclusion. As such, we encourage applications from candidates who have been historically disadvantaged and marginalized, including applicants who identify as First Nations, Métis and/or Inuk (Inuit), Black, racialized, a person with a disability, women and/or 2SLGBTQ+.

Positions are open to qualified candidates who are legally entitled to work in Canada.

The University of Waterloo is committed to accessibility for persons with disabilities. If you have any application, interview, or workplace accommodation requests, please contact Human Resources at hrhelp@uwaterloo.ca or 519-888-4567, ext. 45935.

title: Therapeutic Area Specialist
description:

Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it.

To drive key products growth within priority accounts in order to achieve defined promotional target while meeting the needs of key customers (HCPs) through win-win partnership (Full Account Management).

Managing multi-portfolio.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Deliver value story to targeted customers (HCPs)

  • Deploy tailored multichannel activities
  • Share & learn customers insight with/from other peers

  • Environment integration (Competition, Spheres of Relationship, Decision Making Process & Networks) – Map out precise relationships between key customers (e.g. HCPs, Academic institutions) and also with competitors. Adapt his/her activity and able to share appropriately with X-Functional colleagues on demand.
  • Customer (HCPs) needs& wants (Customer Individual Style, Patients Profile, and Treatment Objectives) – Use questions, listen & interpret the accounts’ current needs, priorities, attitudes, challenges and drivers across clinical, financial or other parameters.

Develop and implement both long- and short-term business plans for all identified key customers and accounts in order to overcome barriers and maximize opportunities in line with brand strategy.   • Multi-channels plan
  • Systems & processes

Execution:

  • Action plan implementation – Ensure resources allocated to promotional and access activities are prioritized appropriately and deployed effectively in line with both brand plan and local business plan.

Continually monitor local situation and make timely recommendations to ensure plans remain optimal.
  • Relationship management – Identify & develop appropriate business relationships with key customers. Effectively implement both promotional and access elements of the business plan, including regular progress reviews and adherence to defined metrics. Constantly champion account management approach and behaviors, particularly collaboration both internally & externally.
  • Multi-channel execution
  • Compliance - All activities must be fully compliant with all BMS/CLG policies & the local law.

  • An in-depth knowledge of the health care system and customers’ needs
  • Account management skills
  • Project Management
  • Multi-channel expertise
  • Excellent matrix communication skills
  • Drive & “can do” attitude / entrepreneurial behavior
  • Passion & energy

title: Network Designer - 12-Month Fixed Term Contract
description:
Location: Irlam, Manchester
Salary: Up to £50,000 per annum, depending on experience
Contract: Full-time, fixed-term contract (up to 12 months)

Ready for your next challenge?

Are you an experienced Network Designer with a passion for fibre networks, technical excellence and finding better ways of working?

Do you enjoy taking ownership, solving complex challenges and making a real difference?

If so, we'd love to hear from you!

Freedom Fibre is looking for an experienced Network Designer to join our Design and Planning Team on a fixed-term contract of up to 12 months. This is a fantastic opportunity to play a key role in the development of our network, influence design standards and drive continuous improvement across the business.

Who We Are

Freedom Fibre is a UK full-fibre network provider with a mission to connect communities and bring fast, reliable broadband to homes and businesses.

We're an ambitious and growing business, passionate about innovation, quality and delivering excellent connectivity. Our people are at the heart of what we do, and we encourage everyone to share ideas, challenge the norm and make a difference.

The Role

Reporting to the Head of Design and Planning, you'll take ownership of network design activities, ensuring projects are delivered efficiently, accurately and to the highest standards.

Working closely with surveyors, Build Assurance Engineers, Build Coordinators, suppliers and other stakeholders, you'll help ensure our network designs are technically sound, commercially effective and meet all relevant quality and data requirements.

You'll also play an important role in improving processes, introducing new ideas and helping shape the future performance of our Design Team.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Ensuring network designs comply with relevant guidelines, industry standards and codes of practice.

  • Maintaining high levels of data quality across asset and customer management systems.

  • Driving consistency, quality and cost-effectiveness across network designs.

  • Working with suppliers and vendors to improve performance and efficiency.

  • Overseeing design acceptance and ensuring as-built information is received, checked and correctly recorded.

  • Identifying new technologies, systems and innovations that could benefit Freedom Fibre.

  • Supporting technical and commercial evaluations of new CPP innovations.

  • Helping to develop and improve design processes, standards and performance reporting.

  • Working with colleagues and partners to resolve issues and deliver successful outcomes.

  • Achieving departmental and individual KPIs.

What We're Looking For

You'll ideally bring:

  • A relevant qualification or extensive experience in UK civils and fibre network planning and design.

  • Thorough knowledge of Openreach PIA products and their practical application.

  • Expert knowledge of FTTH/P passive network architecture and components.

  • A good understanding of the Diversionary Works Code of Practice.

  • Qualifications or experience in recognised continuous improvement methodologies.

  • Good working knowledge of APX, DPCom, QGIS or similar systems.

A Little About You

We're looking for someone who is:

  • Experienced in delivering results in a fast-paced environment.

  • A confident communicator with excellent stakeholder management skills.

  • A natural team player who builds strong working relationships.

  • Commercially aware, proactive and solutions-focused.

  • A strong problem-solver with an eye for detail and quality.

  • Passionate about fibre networks, industry developments and continuous improvement.

  • Flexible and happy to travel to sites and partner locations when required.

Our Benefits Include

  • Competitive salary.

  • Bonus scheme.

  • Generous pension.

  • Private healthcare.

  • Hybrid working.

  • A supportive, collaborative working environment.

Interested?

If you're an experienced Network Designer ready to take ownership, bring fresh ideas and help us continue building a high-quality fibre network, we'd love to hear from you.

Come and help us connect the future at Freedom Fibre. Apply today!

title: Summer 2027 PhD Battery Research & Development Intern
location: Warren, Michigan, United States of America
description:
Job Description

The Advanced Materials & Chemistries group within GM Battery Research and Development (BRD) is seeking a highly motivated Ph.D. student to join our research team as an intern. In this role, you will plan and execute collaborative research that advances sodium ion battery materials, components, and electrochemical technologies for next-generation electric vehicles and energy storage systems.

Hybrid: This role is categorized as hybrid. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to the Research Administration Building at our Global Technical Center in Warren, MI three times per week, at minimum.

The Role

As a Summer Intern, you will work with scientists, engineers, laboratory personnel, operations teams, and external collaborators to develop new knowledge, evaluate technical concepts, and translate promising research into practical solutions. Depending on the assignment, your work may contribute to external publications and/or intellectual property.


Potential research areas

  • Development of high-performance, durable, and cost-effective anode materials for sodium ion batteries
  • Electrode materials synthesis, processing, and scale-up considerations
  • Materials and component optimization for high-energy and high-power battery systems
  • Electrochemical characterization and performance evaluation
  • Materials, interfaces, and degradation-mechanism studies
  • Advanced methods for battery testing, characterization, and data analysis
  • Cell design, integration, benchmarking, and failure analysis

What you’ll do

  • Conduct research and/or experiments to collect required data and validate research ideas
  • Document and present results. Depending on the assignment, results could lead to external publications and/or intellectual property
  • Assist lab management in identifying mega trends in technology and business strategies in the automotive sector
  • Develop and execute specific research plans, including concept generation, development, implementation, and validation
  • Collaborate effectively with peers, management, operations groups, and outside organizations

Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications)

  • Currently enrolled in a Ph.D. program in materials science, chemistry, chemical engineering, electrochemistry, physics, or a related science or engineering discipline.
  • Research experience in sodium ion battery materials (such as hard carbon, Sn, and other alloy-based anode materials), materials synthesis, electrochemical systems, or a closely related field.
  • Strong theoretical and experimental problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to design experiments, interpret results, and draw technically sound conclusions.
  • Ability to work independently while contributing effectively to a collaborative research team.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Demonstrated commitment to integrity, accountability, safety, and responsible research practices.

What will give you a competitive edge (Preferred Qualifications)

  • Prior internship experience in automotive, battery technology, or manufacturing
  • Knowledge of and hands-on experience with both advanced anode materials for sodium ion batteries and cell chemistry development
  • Experience with cell fabrication and testing
  • Outstanding interpersonal and relationship management skills to effectively collaborate with varying levels of organization as needed
  • Strong critical thinking and analytical skills, especially the ability to synthesize large amounts of data involving multiple variables into comprehensive, impactful insights
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to distill sophisticated subjects to a wider audience

title: Director of Special Education & Program Coordinator/Instructor for Deaf & Hard of Hearing Education
description:
SUMMARY OF POSITION: Converse University invites applications for a full-time Director of Special Education and Program Coordinator/Instructor for Deaf and Hard of Hearing Education. The position combines teaching, program leadership, student advising, and clinical supervision. The faculty member will teach seven courses each academic year, typically four in the fall semester and three in the spring. Teaching assignments may include undergraduate and graduate courses, as appropriate to the candidate's expertise and program needs, but will primarily consist of instruction in American Sign Language (ASL).

ESSENTIAL DUTIES/NON-ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Provide academic and program leadership for the DHH and Special Education-Multicategorical programs.

Advise students majoring in special education and support their progress toward degree and licensure requirements.

Teach assigned courses and maintain regular office hours for student consultation.

Supervise or support teacher candidates in clinical experiences and student teaching, as needed. Coordinate with school and community partners on clinical placements, student teaching, and recruitment.

Contribute to curriculum development, program assessment, continuous improvement, and compliance with applicable state licensure and accreditation requirements.

Participate in School of Education department meetings and University faculty meetings. Contribute to teaching and service to the University and community, consistent with the Converse University Faculty Handbook.

Complete other related duties as assigned by the department chair.

JOB QUALIFICATIONS:

Expertise in Deaf and Hard of Hearing education or Special Education-Multicategorical, with the ability to contribute to coursework and program leadership across both areas.

Knowledge of evidence-based practices, inclusive instruction, assessment, and the preparation of teacher candidates to serve students with disabilities.

Ability to advise students and supervise clinical or student-teaching experiences in collaboration with school partners.

Ability to coordinate curriculum, program assessment, continuous improvement, and compliance with applicable licensure and accreditation standards.

A record of, or potential for, effective university teaching.

Strong communication and collaboration skills, and a commitment to supporting students, colleagues, and school partners.

Commitment to service within the University, the profession, and the community.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

An earned doctorate (Ph.D. or Ed.D.) in Special Education, Deaf Education, or a closely related field by the position's start date. Applicants who are ABD may be considered if they complete the doctorate by the start date.

Demonstrated expertise in at least one of the following areas: Deaf and Hard of Hearing education or Special Education-Multicategorical.

Professional experience working with students with disabilities in a P-12 school or comparable clinical setting.

Evidence of the ability to teach and advise undergraduate and/or graduate teacher candidates; must possess credentials that will allow applicant to teach undergraduate ASL I - III.

Strong written, oral, and interpersonal communication skills

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

Three or more years of P-12 teaching or related clinical experience in special education.

Experience supervising teacher candidates in clinical placements or student teaching.

Experience coordinating a teacher-preparation program or contributing to accreditation, licensure review, or program assessment.

Familiarity with South Carolina educator licensure requirements.

Experience teaching undergraduate courses in American Sign Language

Experience with online or hybrid instruction, if those formats are part of the programs.

ASL proficiency or experience working with Deaf communities, as relevant to the DHH program's curriculum and student needs.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:

Knowledge of evidence-based practices in Deaf and Hard of Hearing education or Special Education-Multicategorical, and the ability to apply that knowledge to teacher preparation.

Knowledge of relevant educator licensure requirements, professional standards, and program- assessment practices.

Ability to teach and advise undergraduate and/or graduate students, and to support teacher candidates' progress toward degree and licensure requirements.

Ability to supervise clinical experiences and student teaching, and to work effectively with P- 12 school partners.

Ability to coordinate curriculum, program assessment, continuous improvement, and accreditation or licensure-review activities across the DHH and Multicategorical programs.

Skill in using assessment information to evaluate student learning and inform program improvement.

Ability to contribute to professional service consistent with a faculty appointment.

Strong written, oral, and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to collaborate with students, colleagues, school partners, and community members.

Ability to use instructional technology and, as needed, teach in face-to-face, online, or hybrid formats.

GUIDELINES AND SUPERVISION: This position will report to the chair of the Department of Education and will be evaluated annually in accordance with Converse University's faculty policies and procedures. The evaluation will consider teaching, service, and assigned program-director responsibilities. Teaching effectiveness may be assessed through course materials, student feedback, evidence of student learning, and classroom observations conducted in accordance with university and department practices. The faculty member will communicate regularly with the department chair about progress, goals, and support needed to fulfill the position's responsibilities. The Director will work collaboratively with School of Education colleagues, University faculty and staff, students, and P-12 school and community partners. Program decisions, curriculum changes, assessment activities, and clinical-placement arrangements will be coordinated with relevant colleagues and follow established University, School of Education, and licensure procedures. The Director is expected to communicate professionally, contribute constructively to shared work, and respond to feedback as part of ongoing program improvement.

SPECIAL CONSIDERATIONS: This position includes teaching American Sign Language (ASL) courses as part of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing program. Candidates must demonstrate advanced ASL proficiency and the ability to teach ASL I-III to undergraduate students.

Hours: Daily throughout academic terms; Office Hours at a minimum of three hours per week.

Licenses: Licensure at any level of K-12 Education with an emphasis in Deaf Education or Special Education.

DISCLAIMER: The preceding job description has been designed to indicate the general nature and essential duties and responsibilities of work performed by employees within this classification. It may not contain a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities, and qualifications required of employees to do this job.

We believe that a diverse faculty and staff are essential to achieving academic excellence; thus, we strongly encourage applications from candidates from all racial, ethnic, and cultural backgrounds.

title: Unik möjlighet för erfaren kirurg – Capio i Göteborg
description:
Om oss

Capio Gastro Center Göteborg startade 2022 och bedriver mottagnings- och operationsverksamhet inom allmänkirurgi, urologi, gastroenterologi och endoskopi. Kliniken har två operationssalar, övernattningsmöjligheter och ett team på ca 15 engagerade medarbetare. Vi präglas av en nybyggaranda och strävar efter att erbjuda högkvalitativ vård i en dynamisk och framåtblickande miljö, med patientens välmående och medicinsk kvalitet i fokus. Hittills i år har vi utfört ca 600 operationer och vi bedriver vård på uppdrag av både regioner och försäkringsbolag.

Capio Lundby Specialistsjukhus är centralt beläget i Göteborg och erbjuder högspecialiserad poliklinisk vård samt dagkirurgiska ingrepp på uppdrag av Västra Götalandsregionen. Vi har ett starkt fokus på samarbete, trygghet och hög kompetens. Hos oss arbetar erfarna kollegor inom bland annat bråckkirurgi, gallkirurgi, hemorrojder och varicer. Vi är en stabil och etablerad arbetsplats med långsiktiga relationer, låg personalomsättning och tydliga utvecklingsmöjligheter.

Din roll

Vi söker en erfaren specialistläkare inom kirurgi till våra verksamheter på både Capio Gastro Center Göteborg och Capio Lundby sjukhus. Du arbetar självständigt med bedömning, operation och perioperativa ställningstaganden inom verksamheternas uppdrag. Du kommer att arbeta nära anestesi, omvårdnadspersonal och övriga kollegor.

Du har specialistkompetens inom relevant kirurgisk specialitet och dokumenterad, aktuell erfarenhet av självständigt kirurgiskt arbete. Du är trygg i patienturval, perioperativa bedömningar och effektiva vårdflöden samt har ett tydligt fokus på patientsäkerhet, kvalitet och gott patientbemötande.

Vi söker dig som är legitimerad läkare med relevant specialistkompetens, har goda kunskaper i svenska i tal och skrift samt trivs bäst när du arbetar i högpresterande team i gott samarbetsklimat. Du arbetar strukturerat, tar ansvar och uppskattar multiprofessionella team.

Erfarenhet av förbättringsarbete och handledning är meriterande.

Vi erbjuder dig

En spännande och utmanande roll på två kliniker med stora möjligheter att påverka och forma verksamheten. Engagerade- och kompetenta team som arbetar tillsammans för att nå gemensamma mål.

En arbetsmiljö som präglas av nytänkande och innovation. Möjligheter att delta i forum med kirurgkollegor från liknande verksamheter i landet. Mandat och frihet under ansvar. Tryggheten i att ha en stor organisation i bakgrunden som stöd.

  • Tillsvidareanställning med möjlighet till heltid eller deltid

  • Dagtid, helgfria vardagar

  • Effektiva patientflöden och god arbetsmiljö

  • Kollegiala och stabila team

  • Kompetensutveckling och utvecklingsdagar

  • Centrala lägen i Göteborg med närhet till kommunikationer

  • Kollektivavtal, friskvårdsbidrag, förmånscykel

  • Möjlighet att för rätt person utvecklas inom handledning, kvalitetsutveckling eller medicinskt ledningsansvar

Om dig

Du är erfaren specialistläkare inom kirurgi. Du är prestigelös, har förmågan att kavla upp ärmarna och trivs i en miljö där förändring är en del av vardagen. Du är nytänkande och har en förmåga att se möjligheter. Din stil är inkluderande och du har en förmåga att inspirera och engagera människor omkring dig. Viktigast av allt är att du har ett starkt engagemang för att erbjuda patienter vård av högsta kvalitet.

Vi har en kultur med hög kvalitet, patientsäkerhet, effektivitet, patientfokus och starkt medarbetarengagemang. Vi vill att du förstår vad som driver resultatet – både det medicinska och det ekonomiska.

Ansökan och kontakt

Varmt välkommen med din ansökan till två ledande kirurgiska kliniker i Göteborg, en möjlighet till både yrkesmässig utveckling och en bättre balans mellan arbete och privatliv!

Intervjuer sker löpande och tjänsten kan komma att tillsättas innan sista ansökningsdag. Annonsen kan därför tas bort tidigare än planerat, så vänta inte utan skicka in din ansökan redan idag.

I samband med anställning kan bakgrundskontroll och utdrag ur belastningsregistret komma att begäras.

Anställningsform: Tillsvidare med provanställning
Omfattning: Heltid eller deltid
Start: Enligt överenskommelse

Publicerat: 2026-11-18

Sista ansökningsdag: 27-01-31

Vi undanber oss vänligt men bestämt all direktkontakt med bemannings- och rekryteringsföretag samt försäljare av jobbannonser.

title: Associate Director, Product Owner - Workday Integrations
description:
About the Team:

Enterprise Systems is the backbone of GSK’s internal operations in Digital & Tech, enabling GSK Global Functions teams such as Finance, Procurement, HR, Legal, Compliance, WREF, CGA and Corporate Secretariat to run seamlessly. This team designs and delivers cutting-edge digital platforms that power critical processes, ensuring efficiency, compliance, and scalability across the enterprise.

Our HR Digital & Tech team transforms how GSK attracts, develops, and retains talent through innovative technology solutions. From managing global HR platforms to delivering data-driven insights, this function ensures our people have the tools and experiences they need to thrive. Partnering closely with HR business teams, we create solutions that simplify processes, enhance employee engagement, and enable strategic workforce planning. If you’re passionate about technology that empowers people, this is where you can make an impact.

Job Purpose:

The Associate Director, Product Owner - Workday Integrations is responsible for maximising the value of their product (Workday Integrations) by translating business needs into a prioritised backlog and leading delivery across the HR product lifecycle, within strategic and financial guardrails set by the SD People Services and Reward and VP of HR Digital & Tech. They work closely with business stakeholders to define outcomes and ensure delivered functionality is usable, secure, compliant, supportable, and aligned to product strategy. The Workday Integrations Product Owner guides delivery teams to ensure requirements are clear, value-driven, and data-informed, while overseeing iterative delivery that improves product performance, adoption, and operational readiness.

This role operates under GSK's "Performance with Choice" hybrid working approach, typically expecting 2–3 days per week in the office, with the specific pattern agreed between the successful candidate and their manager based on role and team needs.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Partner with business stakeholders to understand functional needs, refine requirements, and define product outcomes that support business priorities, within guardrails set by the SD People Services and Reward and VP of HR Digital & Tech.
  • Own and manage the Product backlog (e.g. Jira, ADO etc), ensuring requirements (e.g., epics, features, user stories) are well-defined and supported by minimum data inputs (e.g., cost drivers, user volumes, risk/sensitivity, process impact, dependencies).
  • Make prioritisation decisions for the Product backlog based on value, cost, risk, business continuity, and resource capacity, escalating only where strategic trade-offs are required by the SD People Services and Reward and VP of HR Digital & Tech.
  • Lead the Product team’s delivery activities, guiding Associate Product Owners and working with Engineers, Architects, and Testers to ensure solutions are fit-for-purpose, secure, compliant, supportable, and aligned to architectural standards.
  • Drive operational readiness by applying a delivery readiness checklist covering support model requirements, training needs, continuity planning, configuration/runbook documentation, release notes, and user onboarding.
  • Define and maintain the Product performance dashboard, tracking adoption, cycle time/throughput, stability/defects, UX signals (e.g., CSAT, SUS, completion rates), and support effort; use performance insights to drive continuous improvement.
  • Ensure product changes follow required security controls, risk assessments, data handling policies, and regulated change processes, obtaining approvals from relevant SMEs where required.
  • Support Solution Architects to assess design options and manage cross-Product dependencies, contract/interface impacts, and sequencing needs to support interoperability and consistent business outcomes.
  • Act as an escalation point for the HR Product team and business users on functional product issues, guiding decisions within agreed financial, risk, and architectural guardrails set by the SD People Services and Reward and the VP of HR Digital & Tech.
  • Contribute to the improvement of delivery practices within the Product, promoting agile (i.e. SaFe, Scrum etc), iterative, value-driven, and data-led ways of working, including meaningful measurement of benefits and operational impact.
  • Lead your team in using approved AI tools to improve productivity and ways of working, role-modelling responsible use and follow GSK’s Responsible AI, privacy and security requirements.

Required Skills & Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in a relevant field (e.g., Computer Science, Information Technology, or Engineering), or equivalent experience.
  • 15 to 19 years of experience working in product delivery, digital solutions, business systems, or process-led technology roles.
  • Knowledge of functional domains within Workday and broader HR technology ecosystem.
  • Deep technical expertise over Workday Integrations.
  • Proven experience defining and prioritising functional requirements (e.g., epics, features, user stories) and managing a product backlog.
  • Experience working directly with business stakeholders to translate needs into feasible, value-led technology changes.
  • Demonstrated ability to make prioritisation decisions based on business value, process impact, risk, cost, and technology constraints.
  • Experience leading delivery teams or analysts through the product lifecycle, from refinement and design through testing, release, and adoption.
  • Familiarity with enterprise governance requirements such as change control, security, data protection, and regulatory/compliance considerations.
  • Exposure to continuous improvement approaches (e.g., automation, process simplification, user-centred enhancements) that uplift product adoption, stability, or user experience.
  • Experience working within agile delivery environments and using iterative planning, delivery, and release practices.
  • Industry certifications highly desirable (e.g. Agile Methodologies, CPM).

Preferred Skills:

  • Strong communication and influencing skills, able to explain technology constraints clearly and support stakeholders in making informed product decisions.
  • Skilled in coaching and guiding Associate Product Owners and delivery team members to ensure requirements, documentation, and solutions meet business needs and compliance expectations.
  • Able to interpret business processes, user feedback, and operational data to identify opportunities for process simplification, automation, and improved user experience.
  • Comfortable working within structured governance, security, and data protection requirements, ensuring product changes remain controlled, supportable, and compliant.
  • Strong analytical mindset, able to weigh value, risk, complexity, and cost to make prioritisation decisions and sequence backlog items appropriately.
  • Ability to work in a very fast-paced and fluid environment
  • Comfortable with ambiguity and change.


Skills

Agile Methodology, Cross-Functional Teamwork, DevOps, Digital Solutions, Product Delivery, Product Strategies, Software Development, User Experience (UX), User Story, Web Services, Workday EIB, Workday Integration, Workday Studio

Why GSK?

Uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together.

GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. We aim to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade, as a successful, growing company where people can thrive. We get ahead of disease by preventing and treating it with innovation in specialty medicines and vaccines. We focus on four therapeutic areas: respiratory, immunology and inflammation; oncology; HIV; and infectious diseases – to impact health at scale.

People and patients around the world count on the medicines and vaccines we make, so we’re committed to creating an environment where our people can thrive and focus on what matters most. Our culture of being ambitious for patients, accountable for impact and doing the right thing is the foundation for how, together, we deliver for patients, shareholders and our people.

title: Affiliate Nutrition Fellow
location: Papillion, NE, US; Davenport, IA, US; Columbia, SC, US; Springdale, AR, US
description:
JOB TITLE: Affiliate Nutrition Fellow

JOB SUMMARY: Join the Kansas City Royals sports nutrition team and help bring performance nutrition to life in professional baseball. The Affiliate Nutrition Fellow is an on-site member of the Performance Nutrition staff who supports minor league players through practical fueling strategies, individualized education, and collaboration with coaches, clubhouse staff, medical providers, and strength and conditioning professionals. This hands-on opportunity emphasizes helping athletes develop the knowledge, confidence, and habits to independently fuel for training, recovery, and competition. We have 2 openings across our affiliate locations: Omaha, NE (AAA); Springdale, AR (AA); Davenport, IA (High-A); and Columbia, SC (Low-A).

Apply online with resume, cover letter, and 3 professional references.

POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES:
The percentages below represent an estimated distribution of responsibilities; priorities may shift with home stands, road trips, athlete needs, and the phase of the season.
FOOD SERVICE, INVENTORY & SUPPLEMENT OPERATIONS (40%)

Coordinate daily meal and snack service with home and visiting clubhouse managers, caterers, and/or chefs, ensuring accessible fueling options at home and on the road.
Monitor food quality, food safety, athlete feedback, ordering, inventory, and spending within assigned budgets and department procedures.
Assist with approved supplement inventory, distribution, and athlete education; promote NSF Certified for Sport products while following Club and MLB functional-food and supplement requirements.

APPLIED PERFORMANCE NUTRITION & ATHLETE CARE (25%)

Implement the Kansas City Royals Nutrition System through athlete interactions, dietary assessments, individualized fueling recommendations, and ongoing behavior-change support.
Collaborate with Nutrition leadership and strength and conditioning staff on energy needs, bodyweight/body composition priorities, recovery, and fatigue management.
Help athletes translate nutrition guidance into realistic, repeatable habits they can manage independently, escalating higher-priority needs when appropriate.

NUTRITION EDUCATION & BEHAVIOR CHANGE (15%)

Identify relevant team and individual nutrition needs; deliver practical education through conversations, small-group sessions, handouts, presentations, and digital content.
Teach applied skills such as meal planning, travel fueling, recovery, hydration, and informed supplement choices to support athlete autonomy.
Collaborate with Nutrition leadership to refine and develop resources for the Royals Performance Nutrition system.

CLINICAL SPORTS NUTRITION & INJURY RECOVERY (5%)

Coordinate with Nutrition leadership, athletic trainers, physicians, and other medical staff on nutrition considerations for illness, injury, rehabilitation, and return to play.
Support medical nutrition therapy and monitoring within applicable credentialing, licensure, and supervision requirements; refer or escalate needs as appropriate.
Apply current clinical and sports nutrition research to evidence-informed, athlete-centered care.

DOCUMENTATION, COMMUNICATION & SYSTEMS IMPROVEMENT (15%)

Complete timely and accurate nutrition documentation, share relevant athlete updates with authorized staff, and protect confidentiality.
Contribute to interdisciplinary meetings, operational feedback, education projects, and improvements to workflows, resources, and standard operating procedures.
Perform additional duties as assigned by the Director of Sports Nutrition or Minor League Nutrition Coordinator.

Typical Work Rhythm:

Daily / Home Games: Coordinate or verify meals and fueling stations; communicate with clubhouse and food-service partners; connect with athletes and identify immediate nutrition needs.
Weekly: Review athlete follow-ups, monitor inventory and supplement records, assess spending and food-service feedback, and keep documentation and team updates current.
Throughout the Season: Deliver targeted education, support higher-priority clinical or rehabilitation cases, and contribute to resource or workflow improvements as assigned.

Position Qualifications, Skills, and Experience Required:

Bachelor's degree in nutrition or dietetics; Registered Dietitian (RD) credential, or on track to obtain it.
Minimum 1 year of experience within a professional, private, or collegiate sports program.
Knowledge of performance and clinical nutrition, food-service operations, quality control, food safety, ergogenic aids, supplementation, and body-composition assessment.
Excellent communication, presentation, counseling, and relationship-building skills.
Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Adobe Acrobat; strong organizational, time-management, and recordkeeping abilities.
Self-motivated, with the ability to work independently and collaboratively, exercise sound judgment, and maintain confidentiality.
Ability to work non-traditional hours, including nights, weekends, and holidays.
Master's degree in nutrition, food science, or exercise physiology, preferred.
Bilingual (Spanish), preferred.

Physical Requirements:

Ability to lift items weighing as much as 50 pounds.
Must be able to work in a standing position for the majority of the workday.
Must be able to work productively using a computer keyboard and telephone.
Must be able to work productively in an environment where the noise level can be high at times.
Must be comfortable walking throughout the facility to access offices, the concourse, and other areas.
Must be able to work extended hours and/or weekends as required by deadlines and event scheduling.

Additional Details:

Housing (stipend or provided pending availability)
Monthly Stipend
Duration: March through end of affiliate season (may include post-season coverage)
Benefits: Not Included
Meals: Provided when onsite, at least 2/day
Gear and Computer provided
Travel: Some road trips as deemed necessary and with approval

The employee frequently is required to sit for long periods of time; walk; use hands, handle, or feel.

title: Group Risk Director (GRD001)
description:
Job Description:

Foreground is partnering with a diversified investment holding group in Kuwait to appoint a governance-oriented and enterprise-mindedGroup Risk Director, based in Kuwait City. With a portfolio spanning financial services, real estate, education, and healthcare, the group seeks to institutionalize its risk management framework to better align with regulatory expectations, shareholder governance, and sustainable growth priorities.



Role Purpose



To design, implement, and oversee a comprehensive enterprise risk management (ERM) framework across all business units and subsidiaries, enabling proactive identification, assessment, and mitigation of operational, strategic, regulatory, and financial risks.



Key Responsibilities




  • Lead the design and institutionalization of the groups risk management framework, ensuring alignment with board governance structures and Kuwait Capital Markets Authority (CMA) requirements.

  • Oversee enterprise risk assessment activities across all subsidiaries and asset classes, identifying emerging risks and defining acceptable thresholds of exposure.

  • Establish internal policies and tools for risk identification, escalation, and mitigation, including scenario planning, stress testing, and incident response procedures.

  • Act as the primary advisor to the Group CEO and Board Risk Committee, preparing quarterly risk dashboards, internal audit follow-ups, and board-level reporting.

  • Collaborate closely with compliance, internal audit, and legal teams to ensure alignment on governance, financial controls, and regulatory obligations.

  • Build and lead a cross-portfolio risk management team, embedding risk awareness across operational, project, and investment functions.

  • Lead risk training sessions and awareness programs across the group to strengthen decision-making and accountability at all levels.

  • Oversee risk management technology adoption, including risk registers, control libraries, and reporting systems.


Ideal Candidate Profile




  • 15+ years of progressive experience in enterprise risk, internal controls, or audit leadership roles within diversified groups, investment firms, or regulated entities.

  • Strong working knowledge of Kuwait CMA governance guidelines and GCC regulatory standards for group-level risk management.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional risk functions with exposure to varied industries and jurisdictions.

  • Bachelors degree in Finance, Accounting, Risk Management, or related field; CIA, CPA, or IRM/FRM certification strongly preferred.

  • Excellent stakeholder management skills with fluency in English; Arabic proficiency is preferred.

  • Strategic mindset with the discipline and structure to embed risk controls into high-growth and founder-led environments.

title: Assay Scientist
description:
When joining PerkinElmer, you select an experienced and trusted leader in scientific solutions, with the support of a global service network and distribution centers, providing the right solution, at the right time, to meet critical customer needs. With over an 80+ year legacy of advancing science and a mission of innovating for a healthier world, our dedicated team collaborates closely with commercial, government, academic and healthcare customers to deliver our broad portfolio of analytical solutions, and OneSource services.

Job Title

Assay Scientist


Location(s)

GSK Stevenage (UK) – Customer Site

Job Description


We are looking for highly motivated candidate for the role of Flow Cytometry Technician to build their career and support the PerkinElmer OneSource Scientific Services at one of our customer sites in Stevenage.


The successful candidate will be working within the PerkinElmer Extracellular Targeted Cancer Therapies team, who will be responsible for supplying routine flow cytometry maintenance, assays and basic cell culture support. The customer department is in the Oncology sector of R&D which is at the forefront of developing innovative and life-changing medicines for cancer patients.


The role will provide opportunity to develop skills associated with flow cytometry support and cell culture as well as the opportunity to collaborate with numerous biological groups across the site and service lines to improve the TLS Analytical Section operations.


The candidate will work within a collaborative team environment across diverse biotherapeutic portfolio within the company and have the opportunity to develop in PerkinElmer’s scientific arena.

This role will report into the PerkinElmer ETCT Team Leader and will work within GSK biological groups within the Stevenage Campus.



Job Responsibilities

  • Perform routine laboratory research activities including but not limited to cell culture, sample preparation and assay reagent and media supply.
  • Perform various biological assays as determined by the specific departmental work project or package and using both manual and automated techniques.
  • Analysis and reporting Of data using corporate tools; application Of QC rules to show acceptability.
  • Track assay performance metrics and communicate issues and suggest improvements to current assay methodology, supporting evaluation of new technologies where applicable.
  • Be an active member of the scientific teams — contribute at team meetings by presenting data and looking for opportunities for innovation.
  • Maintain training and compliance in areas of health and safety, security, environmental and operational aspects of daily activities in the working environment.
  • Actively seek opportunities to develop the service by discussion with the team leader and customer or by sharing the best practice(s) with other groups.
  • Operate to approved quality standards.
  • Work independently and flexibly depending on team priorities and set realistic work schedules to support requirements.

Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities of this job at any time.


Critical Skills

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, both written and verbal.
  • Self-motivated and able to work under pressure to prioritize conflicting deadlines.
  • An ability to meet timelines successfully with the utmost attention to detail while setting high performance standards.
  • Service orientated attitude combined with innovative thinking.
  • Strong interpersonal skills; strong team player with customer satisfaction focus
  • Ability to execute new and established methods and protocols.
  • Ability to understand, interpret, and communicate complex scientific data.
  • Understanding of standard software packages (i.e. Microsoft Office).
  • Ability to operate within company and/or customer site safety codes of practice.

Basic Qualifications

  • BSc or equivalent in a relevant scientific subject (e.g. Biology, Biotechnology or Biomedical Sciences), with relevant laboratory experience.
  • 1-2 years of demonstrated work in a laboratory environment following defined protocols and SOPS, performing cell culture and several laboratory bioassays using manual and automated techniques.
  • Demonstrable experience working with advanced cell techniques such as organoid cell cultures.
  • Working experience with several skilled techniques including flow cytometry, cellular imaging, and meso-scale discovery.
  • Knowledgeable in good laboratory practices (GLP) and good laboratory safety practices.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Masters or Doctorate qualification in a relevant scientific subject (e.g. Biology, Biotechnology or Biomedical Sciences).
  • A proven background of training staff in laboratory techniques.
  • Computational skills preferred for enabling automated data acquisition and analysis, and familiarity with related data analysis applications.
  • Knowledge of GCP, GCLP and GMP principles in the pharmaceutical environment.
  • Knowledge of 5S and/or 6 sigma principles is a plus

Working Environment

  • Employees will be provided with PerkinElmer polo shirts to be worn when on site.
  • Must be able to work in a laboratory and controlled environments requiring personal protective equipment (e.g., lab coat, safety glasses, etc.).
  • Work with biohazards upon completion Of blood borne pathogen surveillance.
  • Hepatitis B vaccination may be required, vaccination programme in place for successful candidates who are not already vaccinated or require updated boosters. Opt out optional.
  • Job pace may be fast and job completion demands may be high.
  • Must be able to remain in a stationary position more than 25% of the time
  • The person needs to occasionally move between laboratories, corridors, adjoining rooms, and buildings onsite.
  • Occasional travel to other customer sites may be needed.
  • Frequently Operate on instruments, objects, tools or controls, which will require regularly bending, squatting, stretching and reaching to perform in a service function.
  • Occasionally move or lift up to 25 pounds (potential for occasional lifting of up to 50 pounds).
  • Specific vision abilities required by this position include without limitation, the ability to observe details at close range distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus to perform the essential service functions of this position.
  • Operation of a computer and other office machinery, such as a calculator, copy machine, and computer printer.
  • The employee may be required to manage hazardous waste in compliance with company procedures and local and national hazardous waste regulations.
  • Duties may include identifying, handling, generating, accumulating, storing, labelling.
  • Potential risk to lab-based hazards including but not limited to extreme temperature, biological materials, and hazardous chemicals.
  • May be required to complete Medical Clearance, Respiratory Protection Training, and Fit Testing to wear a respirator as protection against hazards present in the laboratory environment

title: Lead Radiological Tech
description:
SUMMARY: Under the general supervision of Manager, Medical Imaging, following established policies and procedures, oversees and coordinates the work of Radiologic Technologists and support personnel in the performance of a variety of technical radiologic procedures. Provides guidance and supervision to technologist and students on imaging procedures. Assures efficient scheduling of patients and room availability; develops appropriate work schedules for staff to support anticipated needs. Maintains appropriate inventories of medical and radiology supplies, assures operating integrity of equipment and performs clerical and administrative functions as necessary. Regularly performs all functions of a Radiologic Technologist. Maintains highest level of compliance by meeting regulatory needs of but not limited to American College of Radiology and The Joint Commission. All essential functions performed in the position reflect age specific needs of the geriatric, adult, and pediatric patients. Fosters patient and family centered care and nursing services in accordance with the Brown University Health and Rhode Island Hospital mission, vision, and values, with consideration of the life span, including all developmental stages as well as cultural patterns. Brown University Health employees are expected to successfully role model the organization's values of Compassion, Accountability, Respect, and Excellence as these values guide our everyday actions with patients, customers and one another. In addition to our values, all employees are expected to demonstrate the core Success Factors which tell us how we work together and how we get things done. The core Success Factors include: Instill Trust and Value Differences Patient and Community Focus and Collaborate RESPONSIBILITIES: Schedules work time, holidays, sick time and vacation coverage of employees within unit which provides diagnostic radiographs to physicians for use in diagnosis and treatment of patients. Provides assistance with problems, and communicates new or changed policies and procedures to unit personnel. Counsels, guides, and evaluates the performance of employees regularly assigned to the unit. May provide input on hiring or disciplinary action. Responsible for the efficient patient flow by scheduling patient examinations, and coordinating work assignment of employees while giving consideration to the current volume of examination orders, type of radiography required, and the availability of equipment and facilities. Provides for the clinical experience of radiologic Technology students, instructing and guiding students through radiological procedures in the area of responsibility. May review performance of student with instructor. Regularly checks radiographs performed by technologists in the unit for quality control purposes. Performs clerical and/or administrative tasks such as conducting inventory and ordering supplies; compiling statistics; checking equipment for proper operating condition, and arranging for repair when needed; providing input for budgetary needs. Assumes charge-duty responsibility during weekends in the absence of regularly scheduled supervisory personnel on a routine basis. Understands and practices ALARA principles of radiation Protection including the use and exchange of personal dosimeters. Regularly performs all functions of a Radiologic Technologist. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: BASIC KNOWLEDGE: Registration through the American Registry for radiologic technologists as well as two years formal training in an accredited School of radiologic Technology required. Current and valid license from the Department of Health to practice in the State of Rhode Island. Must hold a current CPR certification from AHA, BLS for Healthcare Providers. Ability to operate all types of radiographic and related equipment, push portable radiographic equipment, and transfer and position patients. Conceptual ability to determine means of providing the requested radiographs of acceptable diagnostic quality based on the specifics of each case. Interpersonal skills to interact effectively with patients who may be under physical and/or emotional stress, to instruct students and employees in radiologic technique, and provides leadership to other employees. Ability to organize and coordinate the operation of a unit. Analytical skills to compile and interpret routine data. Demonstrated knowledge and skills necessary to provide care patients with consideration of aging processes, human development stages and cultural patterns in each step of the care process. EXPERIENCE: One to two years of increasing responsibility and experience in a hospital Radiology Department. WORK ENVIRONMENT AND PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: Work location is in Main Radiology Department or in smaller satellite operation where there is little discomfort due to noise, dust, or temperature. Exposure to radiation, but with little chance of illness or injury when established safety precautions are followed. Continuous standing, walking, pushing of portable radiographic equipment, and lifting and positioning patients is required. Some exposure to odors from human waste and chemicals from automatic film processing equipment.

title: Project Coordinator (IT) Temp
description:
Position Summary
The Temporary Project Coordinator plays a key role in successful planning, execution, and delivery of projects that support municipal operations and services. Reporting to the Supervisor, Business Solutions Delivery, the Temporary Project Coordinator works closely with the existing Project Coordinator to support the delivery of larger, more complex projects and coordinated project activities. The position also has independent management and accountability for assigned existing and new projects, ensuring outcomes align with organizational goals and are delivered on time, within budget, and to the required standard. This role supports organizational change initiatives and identifies opportunities for process improvement to enhance service delivery.
Core Accountabilities
Project Planning, Coordination and Delivery

Work collaboratively with other project delivery resources to support larger and more complex projects by coordinating assigned workstreams, activities, deliverables, and project documentation.
Independently manage and be accountable for assigned existing and new projects from initiation through close-out, including scope, schedules, budgets, risks, issues, decisions, and reporting.
Develop and maintain detailed project plans, schedules, budgets, and implementation approaches, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and approved project direction.
Coordinate with vendors and contractors to secure services, support procurement and contract activities, and ensure deliverables meet quality standards.
Monitor and track project progress, identify and escalate risks and issues, and implement appropriate mitigation strategies in collaboration with the Supervisor, Business Solutions Delivery and project stakeholders.
Prepare and maintain project documentation, including charters, status reports, RAID logs, meeting records, change requests, and post-project reviews.

Stakeholder Engagement

Serve as a central point of contact for assigned project communications and coordinate communications for assigned workstreams on larger projects.
Build and maintain effective relationships with internal departments, external partners, and contractors.
Facilitate timely communication among team members, leadership, stakeholders, and vendors to maintain alignment, resolve dependencies, and provide transparent progress reporting.

Execution and Delivery:

Lead the day-to-day delivery of assigned projects and coordinate assigned activities on larger projects, ensuring adherence to approved scope, timelines, budget constraints, and quality expectations.
Identify, assess, mitigate, and escalate project risks and issues; make recommendations and coordinate resolution with appropriate stakeholders.
Coordinate user acceptance testing, system deployments, data migration activities, and transition-to-operations requirements to support successful project delivery.
Ensure assigned project solutions meet applicable security, privacy, compliance, and operational standards as part of project execution.

Business Analysis Support

Collaborate with stakeholders to gather, document, and analyze business requirements for assigned IT and operational projects.
Create and maintain process flows, use cases, and requirement specifications to support project execution.
Work closely with the existing Project Coordinator, technical teams, and business stakeholders to ensure business needs are effectively translated into sustainable system solutions.
Assist in evaluating and recommending technology solutions that align with organizational goals.

Change Management and Training

Support organizational change management (OCM) initiatives by developing training materials and communication plans.
Facilitate workshops, training sessions, and feedback mechanisms to drive project adoption and success.

Collaboration and Continuous Improvement

Share project information, tools, lessons learned, and capacity across the project coordination function to support consistent delivery practices and successful portfolio outcomes.
Identify and implement opportunities to enhance project management, business analysis, and organizational change practices.

Other

Act in a professional and responsible manner to protect the integrity of employees and the business of Rocky View County. Maintain confidentiality and security as per administrative policy.
Always Adhere to Health and Safety Legislation and Rocky View safe work policies and procedures, ensuring the protection and safety of self, co-workers, the public and environment.
Perform other duties and special projects as assigned.

Position Qualifications

Minimum 5-7 years of experience in project coordination or project management, preferably including accountability for independently managing projects; public-sector experience is an asset.
Experience supporting larger or more complex projects and coordinating cross-functional teams, vendors, and stakeholders is an asset.

Skills and Knowledge

Strong understanding of project management methodologies and tools (e.g., PMBOK, Agile).
Familiarity with business analysis techniques and tools (e.g., process mapping, requirements gathering).
Excellent organizational, time management, and problem-solving skills.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, project management software (e.g., TeamDynamix), and other relevant tools.
Knowledge of municipal government operations and legislative frameworks is an asset.
Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage diverse stakeholders.

Certifications

PMP, CAPM, or equivalent certification is preferred.
Change management certification (e.g., Prosci) is an asset.
Business analysis certification (e.g., CBAP, CCBA) is an asset.

The Custom Project Coordinator I - Commercial Rugs Coordinator independently manages a high-volume portfolio of complex commercial custom rug projects supporting a business currently managing approximately $19 million in annual gross orders. Projects are managed from initial request and specification review through quoting, order entry, fabrication, delivery, and final resolution.

The role requires the coordinator to manage multiple projects at different stages, reconcile detailed and sometimes conflicting documentation, make time-sensitive decisions, and maintain accuracy in a deadline-driven environment. The coordinator serves as the single point of contact for assigned rug orders and is accountable for translating customer requirements into accurate production, fabrication, financial, freight, and delivery instructions.

  • Manage a high-volume portfolio of commercial rug projects with different requirements, priorities, production stages, and customer commitments, maintaining ownership through delivery and final resolution.
  • Reconcile requests, quotes, rug forms, purchase orders, specifications, layouts, dimensions, quantities, pricing, backing, edging, pattern direction, and shipping requirements; resolve discrepancies before they result in production, financial, or delivery errors.
  • Prepare or coordinate rug quotes, customer styles, product specifications, order entry, modifications, cancellations, and supporting documentation.

  • Build and retain positive business relationships, emulate Shaw core values of Honesty, Integrity, and Passion, and collaborate with team members to ensure continuous order coverage.
  • Own custom rug order commission management in Mainframe, including validating, entering, maintaining, and resolving commission requirements to ensure accurate order and financial processing.

High-value business + substantial transaction volume + constant communication + technical custom work + end-to-end ownership

title: Senior Commercial RM IV
description:
Make banking a Fifth Third better®
We connect great people to great opportunities. Are you ready to take the next step? Discover a career in banking at Fifth Third Bank.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

The Sr Commercial Relationship Manager-Emerging Middle Market (EMM) is a senior, expert relationship manager responsible for profitable business development and relationship management of the Bank’s largest and most complex Emerging Middle Market clients, defined as companies with annual revenues of at least $10MM and up to $50MM, within an assigned geographic market.

Serving as the primary relationship owner within the One Bank operating model, this role develops deep trusted‑advisor relationships with senior executives (e.g., CEO, CFO, COO), leads sophisticated relationship strategies, and coordinates integrated solutions across credit, treasury management, capital markets, and other internal partners. The Sr Commercial Relationship Manager-EMM maintains full accountability for relationship strategy, client experience, credit outcomes, and long‑term franchise value.

Please see below for specific responsibilities and requirements for this role.

YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES:

Business Development & Franchise Growth:
Independently originate, develop, and expand profitable Emerging Middle Market relationships through centers of influence, referrals, and existing client networks, while working in partnership with Business Development Officers (BDOs) on new client acquisition. Build long‑term, high‑value relationships that deliver sustained revenue growth, profitability, and increased share of wallet.

Relationship Ownership & One Bank Execution:
Serve as the sole relationship owner and One Bank relationship quarterback for assigned clients and prospects; lead and coordinate internal partners (e.g., Treasury Management, Capital Markets, Wealth) to deliver integrated, client‑centric solutions aligned to client strategy and lifecycle needs.

Client Advisory & Experience:
Maintain frequent, proactive engagement with senior executives to understand business strategy, capital needs, and risk considerations; deliver consultative, insight‑driven advice on financing alternatives, liquidity management, and strategic initiatives; lead all client‑facing activities to ensure a seamless, high‑quality client experience.

Credit Leadership & Risk Management:
Lead complex credit structuring and underwriting discussions, including bilateral and syndicated transactions where applicable; partner with Portfolio Managers and Credit Officers to structure, underwrite, and manage credit exposure in accordance with policy and portfolio guidelines.

Portfolio Management:
Monitor client financial performance, industry trends, and portfolio risk to ensure acceptable credit quality, appropriate pricing, and long‑term franchise value.

Sales Discipline & CRM Execution:
Utilize the Bank’s Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system to manage pipeline, call activity, and relationship planning; reinforce disciplined sales execution and data integrity.

Market & Community Engagement:
Represent Fifth Third in the market through active participation in community, industry, and professional organizations.

Risk Management & Accountability:
Identify, assess, manage, and escalate risks appropriately while operating within the Bank’s risk appetite and adhering to policies and procedures.

Other Duties:
Performing other duties as assigned, adapting to new tasks or shifts in priorities as necessary to support your team’s and the company’s mission.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, or a related field (or equivalent work experience)
  • Minimum of 7 years of commercial banking experience, including senior‑level relationship management
  • Formal commercial credit training or equivalent credit experience
  • Demonstrated experience managing complex Emerging Middle Market client relationships

Key note on Minimum vs. Preferred Requirements:
This section reflects only the base requirements necessary to qualify for the role. Preferred skills and differentiating capabilities are captured in the Skills for Success section.

REQUIRED SKILLS:

Qualified candidates will possess an advanced to expert degree of proficiency (typically from 7+ years of work or practical experience), in:

  • Commercial Credit & Risk Management: Structuring and managing complex credit solutions
  • Relationship Management: Owning and leading sophisticated client relationships
  • Financial Analysis: Interpreting complex financial statements and cash‑flow dynamics
  • One Bank Partner Leadership: Coordinating cross‑line‑of‑business execution
  • Executive Communication: Communicating with impact at the C‑suite level

Please refer to the “Skills for Success” section to learn how to stand out as an applicant.

SKILLS FOR SUCCESS:

Qualified candidates will possess an advanced to expert degree of proficiency (typically from 7+ years of work or practical experience), across a suite of skills including, but not limited to:

  • Trusted Advisor Mindset: Delivering strategic, insight‑driven advice to senior executives
  • Strategic Judgment: Balancing growth, risk, and client outcomes
  • Franchise Leadership: Building sustainable, long‑term client relationships
  • Influence & Negotiation: Driving outcomes in complex environments
  • Enterprise Collaboration: Partnering effectively across the One Bank ecosystem

DOING THE RIGHT THING:

Our employees take pride in doing the right thing for customers and colleagues as well as being accountable for risk by openly exchanging ideas and opinions, elevating concerns, and following policies and procedures that protect all our valuable assets — including you.
