title: Vice President, Membership & Communities
description:
Summary
The Vice President, Membership & Communities provides strategic and operational leadership for SHRM's Membership business, driving growth, retention, engagement, and long-term member lifetime value (LTV) across the full Membership Community.

This role combines strategic business leadership, commercial acumen, and financial discipline to lead a significant business portfolio. The Vice President is responsible for understanding the evolving needs of SHRM's membership community and translating market insights into differentiated member value, sustainable revenue growth, and competitive advantage.

With full P&L accountability for the Membership business, the Vice President establishes multi-year growth and financial objectives, directs investment across the membership lifecycle, and leads the teams responsible for acquisition, retention, engagement, and community development. The role requires a results-oriented executive with demonstrated success navigating organizational transformation, market disruption, and competitive pressures while strengthening business performance.

Operating in close partnership with SHRM's executive leadership, the Vice President brings a strategic, commercially focused perspective to business decisions. This leader serves as the senior voice for the Membership business with the Executive Team and Board of Directors, ensuring membership strategy advances SHRM's mission while delivering measurable business results.

Responsibilities
Membership Strategy & Business Growth

Establish and execute the strategy for membership growth, engagement, retention, and lifetime value (LTV) across the full Membership Community, including dues-paying and non-dues-paying members.
Lead the Membership business with full P&L accountability, including revenue growth, budgeting, forecasting, investment decisions, and financial performance.
Identify opportunities to strengthen SHRM's competitive position, differentiate member value, and expand revenue through innovative offerings and business models.
Translate strategic priorities into measurable business objectives, operational plans, and results.

HR Practitioner Insight & Member Value

Leverage senior HR practitioner experience and industry relationships to anticipate the evolving needs of HR professionals and inform membership strategy.
Strengthen member value across the lifecycle, including acquisition, onboarding, engagement, renewal, and upsell/upgrade opportunities.
Direct community platforms, peer networks, and engagement initiatives that build meaningful professional connections and long-term member loyalty.
Apply market intelligence, member insights, and performance data to improve experiences, retention, and lifetime value.

Executive Leadership & Operational Excellence

Lead and develop directors and multidisciplinary teams, establishing clear priorities, performance expectations, and accountability for results.
Navigate organizational transformation, competitive pressures, and changing market conditions while sustaining operational and financial performance.
Partner closely with the EVP, Membership and Strategic Partnerships to align membership priorities, operating decisions, and enterprise objectives.
Collaborate across Marketing, Product, Technology, Finance, and other functions to optimize resources, strengthen execution, and achieve shared business outcomes.

Executive Engagement & Governance

Represent the Membership business in executive-level strategic planning, financial reviews, and organizational decision-making.
Present business performance, growth opportunities, competitive risks, and strategic recommendations to the Executive Team and Board of Directors.
Build relationships with senior HR executives, volunteer leaders, and external stakeholders to strengthen SHRM's market relevance, influence, and member value.

Education & Experience Requirements
Education

Bachelor's degree in human resources, business administration, or a related field, or relevant, equivalent experience in lieu of degree.
Master's degree preferred.

Experience

Fifteen (15) or more years of progressive leadership experience, including current or former experience as a Chief Human Resources Officer (CHRO), Chief People Officer (CPO), or equivalent senior HR executive with direct HR practitioner experience required.
Demonstrated experience navigating complex HR challenges at the executive level, with firsthand knowledge of the evolving needs of HR professionals and organizations.
Demonstrated P&L accountability, including financial planning, revenue growth, resource allocation, and delivery of measurable business results.
Proven success leading organizations through significant transformation, competitive pressures, and evolving business conditions.
Experience developing and executing growth strategies, leading multidisciplinary teams, and influencing C-suite executives and Boards.
Experience in membership, subscription-based, professional services, or comparable business models preferred.

Certifications - NA

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Business and Financial Acumen: Strong commercial judgment, financial discipline, and ability to translate strategy into measurable business outcomes.
HR Industry Expertise: Deep understanding of the HR profession, practitioner challenges, workforce trends, and evolving market needs, with the ability to apply senior-level HR leadership experience to membership strategy and business decisions.
Strategic Growth: Ability to drive acquisition, engagement, retention, and lifetime value through differentiated offerings and member experiences.
Transformation Leadership: Ability to navigate complexity, organizational change, and competitive disruption while maintaining business performance.
Executive Influence: Strong executive presence, communication, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to align stakeholders and influence enterprise decisions.
Operational Execution: Results-oriented leadership style with a demonstrated ability to establish priorities, develop teams, and drive accountability.
Data & Technology Fluency: Ability to leverage analytics, AI, and emerging technologies to improve decision-making, operational efficiency, and business results.

Physical Requirements
This position operates in a typical office environment (which includes a home office setting) and requires the ability to perform essential job functions with or without reasonable accommodation. Physical requirements may include:

Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
Frequent use of hands and fingers for typing, handling documents, and using office equipment.
Occasional standing, walking, bending, and reaching.
Ability to lift and carry up to 30 pounds as needed.
Clear verbal and written communication skills for effective interaction with colleagues and stakeholders.

Work Environment
Hybrid Schedule (3 Days In-Office/2 Days Remote)
This position follows a hybrid work schedule, with Tuesday through Thursday in office and Monday and Friday remote. Employees must be available during standard business hours, with core hours beginning between 8:00–9:00 a.m. and concluding between 5:00–6:00 p.m. local time.
Travel: Moderate 20 – 30%
#LI
The hiring range for this position is $190,000 to $240,000 per year. This range is an estimate, and the actual salary may vary based on the candidate's experience, skills, and qualifications. SHRM offers a competitive and comprehensive total rewards package. The benefits for this position include professional growth and development, health, dental, vision, well-being, health savings, flexible spending, retirement, open leave, and annual discretionary bonus and incentives.

title: Cell Therapy Commercial Admin Project Coordinator
description:
At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it.



Position Summary:

The Executive Associate, US Cell Therapy, will support several Executive Directors (US Abecma brand lead and US Breyanzi brand lead) and their direct reports in the US Cell Therapy Franchise. We are seeking a dynamic, performance driven, well organized and flexible individual who thrives in a fast-paced environment which is dedicated to bringing important medicines to patients. This individual must be able to work independently and collaboratively within a highly matrixed commercial environment, comprised of partner functional across Account Management, Medical, Business Analytics, Value Access & Payment, Global Cell Therapy, both internally at BMS as well as externally with Alliance partners. On occasion, she/he will make appropriate decisions on behalf of manager in regard to calendar and travel events.


The successful candidate should be a self-motivated, efficient team player with strong oral and written communication skills. Candidate should also have a demonstrated capacity to develop new skills and learn new software applications. He/she will be responsible for supporting multiple priorities that support the US Commercial Cell Therapy Organization in addition to executive level calendars, travel requirements and meeting logistics.


Candidate must be capable of multi-tasking, prioritizing and have the ability to work with other members of the BMS Cell Therapy Organization. Independent judgment is required to plan, prioritize and organize a diversified workload, and meet applicable deadlines on a timely basis. Candidate will interact with a diverse group of team members at all levels of the Company. Exhibit a positive work attitude, high productivity and a collaborative approach with other employees across the organization.


The candidate must demonstrate superior personal integrity and ethics, including an exceptional sense of discretion; strong interpersonal skills; excellent organizational skills and attention to detail are required. Respect for confidentiality and ability to manage confidential information with discretion is of critical importance.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Perform a variety of administrative responsibilities on behalf of the practice area with minimal supervision
  • Manage calendars, as well as schedules, and organize complex activities such as executives & department calendars, meetings (including material preparation & archival), travel, expenses, conferences and related activities across numerous BMS sites
  • May support additional high level executives for temporary periods based on needs (e.g., vacation backup) and may be required to be working on site for specific days based on needs
  • Support opportunities for miscellaneous organizational activities (e.g., Site relocation, Restacking) and KPI monitoring (etc., training metrics) across department
  • Creation and maintenance of SharePoint site, Teams Channel, knowledge management activities, able to work with IT and other key stakeholders to make functional changes & improvement to such collaborative platforms
  • Continuously identify improvements to functional processes and support the change management to implement
  • Assist with onboarding of new colleagues
  • Assist with budget management and P.O. creation & processing, as needed
  • Responds to regularly occurring requests for information
  • Work independently and serve as a key team contributor for special nonrecurring and ongoing tasks, assignments and projects including time sensitive and high-profile meetings

Key Qualifications and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s Degree preferred, high school degree required
  • 5+ years experience in administration, pharmaceutical experience preferred
  • 2 years of Project Management experience preferred, 1 year required
  • Exceptional communication skills – written and verbal
  • Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to work on teams cross-functionally
  • Experience with data analytics
  • Strong problem solving skills
  • Candidate also should have a demonstrated capacity to develop new skills and learn new software applications.
  • Preferably advanced knowledge in Microsoft Office, Outlook, Concur and SharePoint

We hire for skills and capabilities, not just credentials – if this role excites you, but doesn’t perfectly match your resume, we encourage you to apply anyway.

Compensation Overview:

Madison - Giralda - NJ - US: $74,630 - $90,434
Princeton - NJ - US: $74,630 - $90,434 


The starting pay range(s) listed above is for full-time employees (FTE). You may also be eligible for additional discretionary incentive cash and stock opportunities. We determine starting pay thoughtfully – carefully considering the nature of the role, required skills, work location, schedule and the knowledge and experience you bring. Final compensation is guided by pay equity principles and applicable employment laws. Compensation programs are reviewed on an ongoing basis and may be adjusted over time to reflect evolving market factors, and individual, team or Company performance.


Benefits:


Subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable plans then in effect, you may be eligible to participate in our comprehensive benefit plans – including wellbeing support, retirement and financial protection benefits, and insurance offerings (medical, dental, vision, life and disability).


U.S.-based exempt employees are eligible for Flexible Time Off (FTO), which provides paid time off without a set accrual limit, subject to manager approval, along with 11 paid company holidays each year.


Non-exempt employees, RayzeBio employees, and employees located in Puerto Rico receive 160 hours of paid vacation annually for new hires (subject to manager approval), 11 paid company holidays, and 3 optional holidays.


Depending on eligibility, employees may also have access to additional time-off benefits, including paid sick leave, up to two paid volunteer days per year, summer hours flexibility, and leaves of absence for medical, personal, parental, caregiver, bereavement, or military needs. Eligible employees also enjoy an annual Global Shutdown between Christmas Day and New Year's Day.


U.S.-based job seekers can explore full benefit offerings at

title: Senior Product Specialist
description:
When joining PerkinElmer, you select an experienced and trusted leader in scientific solutions, with the support of a global service network and distribution centers, providing the right solution, at the right time, to meet critical customer needs. With over an 80+ year legacy of advancing science and a mission of innovating for a healthier world, our dedicated team collaborates closely with commercial, government, academic and healthcare customers to deliver our broad portfolio of analytical solutions, and OneSource services.

Job Title

Senior Product Specialist


Location(s)

Singapore

Job Description

Senior Product Specialist – Analytical Instruments

Bring your expertise in one technology. Grow it across three.

In the analytical instruments industry, product specialists usually build their careers around a single technology. Here, you don’t have to stop there. Join us as a subject matter expert in one area, and you’ll have the opportunity to gain exposure across all three of our major product categories: Chromatography, Inorganic Analysis and Materials Characterization. Few roles in the industry offer that breadth.

If you’re a hands-on analytical expert who wants to broaden your skills and grow beyond one specialism, this is your opportunity.

About the role

You’ll be the technical partner to our sales team and customers across the full sales cycle, from the first technical discussion and demo to installation, training and ongoing application support. You’ll lead in your area of expertise while having the opportunity to build knowledge across our wider portfolio, helping customers get the most out of our instruments and helping the business grow.

What you’ll do

Pre-sales: win the customer’s confidence

  • Understand customer needs and lead technical discussions to propose the right total solution
  • Run solution-focused demos, application testing and method development, and present the results clearly
  • Lead the creation of application notes and marketing materials for customers and sales colleagues
  • Partner with Sales Leaders to develop new prospects, enter competitive accounts, and meet or exceed annual targets

After-sales: make the solution succeed

  • Deliver hands-on hardware and software training, including technology presentations before hands-on sessions
  • Provide on-site application support, method development and troubleshooting for instruments, applications and software
  • Be the main contact for customer enquiries, working closely with service engineers to resolve issues quickly
  • Maintain strong satisfaction across our installed base
  • Deliver scheduled training to overseas customers

Market and team

  • Track market trends, customer requirements and competitor products, and share insights with the sales team
  • Generate sales leads through your customer engagement
  • Support user meetings, workshops and seminars on new products, technology and applications
  • Manage the demo lab, including chemical inventory

What you’ll bring

  • At least 3–5 years of hands-on experience with analytical instruments, with deep expertise in at least one of: chromatography, inorganic analysis (spectroscopy), or materials characterization
  • Curiosity and willingness to learn new technologies beyond your core area
  • Knowledge of analytical instrument operation, theory and industrial applications
  • Strong data analysis and problem-solving skills in analytical applications
  • Clear, confident presentation and communication skills, both verbal and written
  • A team player who works well with sales and service colleagues
  • Customer-focused and willing to travel in Singapore
  • Proficient in MS Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint)
  • Degree in Chemistry or a related science field. Equivalent hands-on experience will also be considered.

Why join us

  • One expertise, opportunities across three technologies. Build on your core strength, with the opportunity to gain exposure to chromatography, inorganic analysis and materials characterization.
  • Opportunity to learn on the job. Work alongside experienced specialists, with opportunities to get hands-on with technologies beyond your current area.
  • End-to-end impact. See your work go from first demo to a solution running in the customer’s lab.
  • Career growth. Broad application knowledge makes you a stronger technical advisor and can open more career paths.
  • Variety every week. Different customers, industries and analytical challenges, plus regional exposure through overseas training.

title: Associate Director, Product Owner - Learning Experience & Content
description:

The Associate Director, Product Owner - Learning Experience & Content is responsible for maximising the value of their HR Product Portfolio (including Degreed and Learning Content Providers) by translating business needs into a prioritised backlog and leading delivery across the HR product lifecycle, within strategic and financial guardrails set by the SD, Head of Talent + L&D Digital & Tech and VP of HR Digital & Tech. The Learning Experience & Content Product Owner guides delivery teams to ensure requirements are clear, value-driven, and data-informed, while overseeing iterative delivery that improves product performance, adoption, and operational readiness.

This role operates under GSK's "Performance with Choice" hybrid working approach, typically expecting 2–3 days per week in the office, with the specific pattern agreed between the successful candidate and their manager based on role and team needs.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Partner with business stakeholders to understand functional needs, refine requirements, and define product outcomes that support business priorities, within guardrails set by the SD, Head of Talent + L&D Digital & Tech and VP of HR Digital & Tech.

  • 15 to 19 years of experience working in product delivery, digital solutions, business systems, or process-led technology roles.
  • Proven experience defining and prioritising functional requirements (e.g., epics, features, user stories) and managing a product backlog.

  • Experience leading delivery teams or analysts through the product lifecycle, from refinement and design through testing, release, and adoption.
  • Familiarity with enterprise governance requirements such as change control, security, data protection, and regulatory/compliance considerations.
  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in a relevant field (e.g., Computer Science, Information Technology, or Engineering), or equivalent experience.

Preferred skills:

  • Strong communication and influencing skills, able to explain technology constraints clearly and support stakeholders in making informed product decisions.
  • Skilled in coaching and guiding Associate Product Owners and delivery team members to ensure requirements, documentation, and solutions meet business needs and compliance expectations.
  • Able to interpret business processes, user feedback, and operational data to identify opportunities for process simplification, automation, and improved user experience.

  • Strong analytical mindset, able to weigh value, risk, complexity, and cost to make prioritisation decisions and sequence backlog items appropriately.
  • Ability to work in a very fast-paced and fluid environment
  • Comfortable with ambiguity and change


Skills

Agile Methodology, Automation, Degreed (Platform), Design Thinking, DevOps, Digital Solutions, Learning Content Design, Learning Experience Platform (LXP), Phenom (Platform), Product Delivery, SAP SuccessFactors, User Experience (UX)

description:
Job Description:

Job Title: Technology Data Architect

Location: Bangalore, India

Corporate Title: AVP

Role Description

  • The Service Assurance Reporting and Analytics function is responsible for generating production technology performance and risk automated reports, conducting analytics on the output, and providing insights & commentary into these (monthly) reports which are built against different portfolios of applications (Legal Entities, CIO owned, Regional, etc.).
  • The Service Assurance Governance Function supports TDI wide forums, using the above reporting and analytical information as the basis for identifying and agreeing corrective action with our CIO colleagues to mitigate risk, prevent disruption to production stability and assure path to green is established where CIO areas are outside of risk appetite for KPIs.
  • The Data Architect will be responsible for designing and governing the data architecture required to support enterprise Patch and Vulnerability Management reporting, analytics, compliance monitoring and remediation governance. The role will provide the technical and architectural foundation for reliable, scalable and audit-ready data products that enable daily, weekly and monthly visibility of patch compliance, vulnerability exposure, remediation progress, data quality and risk trends across the technology estate.
  • The Data Architect will help establish a controlled and future-ready data platform for Patch and Vulnerability Management by consolidating data from multiple sources, defining trusted data models, improving lineage and quality controls, and enabling reporting consumers to access consistent, timely and actionable insights. The Data Architect will work closely with Patch Management, Cyber Hygiene, Service Assurance, Technology Owners, Engineering, Operations, ITSM platform teams and reporting teams to ensure that data capabilities meet operational, governance, regulatory and executive reporting needs.
  • The Data Architect must be able to work effectively across technical, operational, cyber security, governance and executive stakeholder groups. The role requires strong communication skills, the ability to simplify complex data architecture topics, and the ability to challenge inconsistent data definitions or reporting assumptions in a constructive and evidence-based manner

What we’ll offer you

As part of our flexible scheme, here are just some of the benefits that you’ll enjoy

  • Best in class leave policy
  • Gender neutral parental leaves
  • 100% reimbursement under childcare assistance benefit (gender neutral)
  • Sponsorship for Industry relevant certifications and education
  • Employee Assistance Program for you and your family members
  • Comprehensive Hospitalization Insurance for you and your dependents
  • Accident and Term life Insurance
  • Complementary Health screening for 35 yrs. and above

Your key responsibilities

  • Design the target-state data architecture for Patch and Vulnerability Management, including ingestion, transformation, storage, semantic layers, reporting marts and consumption patterns.
  • Define logical and physical data models for patch compliance, vulnerability exposure, asset inventory, application ownership, technology ownership, risk acceptance, remediation status, change records and governance workflows.
  • Assess and rationalise current data flows across systems such as ServiceNow or dbServiceNow, dbIB, dbART, dbRIB, CMDB, asset inventory, vulnerability scanning tools, patch reporting feeds and downstream dashboards.
  • Establish robust data lineage, source-to-target mappings, data dictionaries, metadata standards and ownership models for all critical Patch and Vulnerability data domains.
  • Design data quality and completeness controls to identify missing, stale, duplicate, inconsistent or unrecognised patch and vulnerability data.
  • Support the creation of trusted reporting datasets for operational reporting, KPI/KRI reporting, executive dashboards, audit evidence, consequence management and regulatory reporting.
  • Partner with process owners and reporting teams to enable analytics such as average time to patch, ageing analysis, breach thresholds, significantly non-compliant assets, overdue vulnerabilities, remediation trends and daily compliance movements.Define architecture patterns for scalable analytics, including structured relational models, big data platforms, NoSQL options, APIs and self-service data access where appropriate.Ensure data architecture aligns with enterprise data governance, security, access control, retention, change management and auditability standards.Provide architectural input into migration and transformation initiatives, including movement from legacy reporting platforms to modern ITSM and data lake capabilities.Collaborate with engineering and platform teams to ensure the data architecture is performant, resilient, reusable and maintainable.Translate business and control requirements into data architecture deliverables, implementation roadmaps, backlog items and technical specifications.

Your skills and experience

Experience | Exposure (Recommended):

  • Experience in data architecture, data engineering, data modelling or enterprise reporting architecture within a complex technology environment.
  • Experience working with cyber security, vulnerability management, patch management, IT risk, IT service management or infrastructure operations data.
  • Proven ability to design governed data platforms supporting management information, operational reporting, compliance reporting and audit requirements.
  • Hands-on experience with relational databases, data warehouses, data lakes, ETL/ELT pipelines, SQL, data marts, APIs and reporting semantic layers.
  • Good understanding of asset inventory, CMDB, application hierarchy, ownership structures, change management, incident management and remediation workflows.
  • Experience with reporting and analytics platforms such as Tableau, Power BI, BusinessObjects, dbRIB or comparable enterprise BI tools.
  • Ability to work across multiple source systems and reconcile conflicting data definitions, ownership models and reporting interpretations.
  • Experience defining data quality rules, validation controls, reconciliation methods and exception management processes.

Education | Certification (Recommended):

  • Degree in mathematics, statistics, computer science, engineering, economics, business management or related field

Proven ability to leverage AI tools to enhance productivity, optimise workflows to solve business problems, while applying critical judgment to ensure responsible and ethical use of data and AI outputs.

How we’ll support you

  • Training and development to help you excel in your career
  • Coaching and support from experts in your team
  • A culture of continuous learning to aid progression
  • A range of flexible benefits that you can tailor to suit your needs

About us and our teams

Please visit our company website for further information:


We strive for a culture in which we are empowered to excel together every day. This includes acting responsibly, thinking commercially, taking initiative and working collaboratively.

Together we share and celebrate the successes of our people. Together we are Deutsche Bank Group.

We welcome applications from all people and promote a positive, fair and inclusive work environment.

As a 24/7 veterinary teaching hospital, staffing needs exist across day, evening, and overnight hours. Specific schedules and shift assignments are based on hospital needs and will be discussed during the hiring process. Weekend and holiday coverage may be required.

Why You'll Love This Position:

  • Meaningful Work: Help clients navigate their pet's care journey and play a vital role in their health and happiness.
  • Team Atmosphere: Collaborate with skilled doctors, students, and support staff in a positive and supportive environment.
  • Exciting Responsibilities: Take on important tasks such as client communication, administrative duties, and service coordination to keep every day engaging.
  • Fast-Paced Environment: Stay active and focused in a role that supports exceptional client service and patient care in a dynamic hospital setting.

Key Job Duties:

Customer Service/Client Communication

  • Welcome clients and update patient information in the hospital database.
  • Schedule appointments, handle emergencies, and provide detailed instructions for visits.
  • Explain hospital policies, payment procedures, and consent requirements.
  • Manage high call volumes, transfer calls to appropriate departments, and address client inquiries.
  • Collect deposits for inpatient care and explain credit and billing policies.

Administrative Tasks

  • Manage communications for faculty, students, and staff.
  • Train and supervise students in office procedures and medical record handling.
  • Support doctors and students by providing access to client records, contact details, and visit history.

Service Coordination

  • Organize and maintain medical records.
  • Deliver food, supplies, and lab samples.
  • Prepare and send billing statements and other client communications.
  • Maintain the reception area with necessary forms and supplies.
  • Sort and distribute mail and assist with database updates.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Prior receptionist or front desk experience, preferably in a veterinary clinic, animal hospital, or animal healthcare setting.
  • Experience handling a multi-line phone system and coordinating appointments, client inquiries, and incoming communications.
  • Experience processing payments, preparing invoices, reconciling transactions, or maintaining financial records.
  • Experience using scheduling, electronic medical record, or client management software such as Avimark, Cornerstone, Workday, or similar systems.
  • Associate degree or coursework in veterinary technology, animal science, business, office administration, or a related field.

Join us and be part of a team that makes a real difference in the lives of animals and their families. Apply today to become a Veterinary Teaching Hospital Assistant and start a career you’ll be proud of!


Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. on an on-going basis without sponsorship. Immigration sponsorship is not available for this position.

Characteristic Duties and Responsibilities

• Schedule appointments using client and patient software to record the appointment.

• Determine if it is an emergency situation and which services to schedule.

• Relay information and requirements for the appointment to client or referring veterinarian.

• Provide special instructions for dermatology, ophthalmology, specialized radiological procedures, surgery, eye certification and proper usage of medication.

• Provide information to clients regarding Hospital policy on admitting animals; consent form for treatment; payment procedures, credit policy and billing procedures; types of services available and prices of hospital services.

• Receive and register clients.

• Collect information from client and establish or update client and patient information using the client and patient software program.

• Establish account.

• Enter exam fee and medical record fee.

• Compile charges on the account according to hospital policy.

• Collect deposits from clients for inpatient care.

• Enter payments and adjustments to client’s accounts.

• Prepare paperwork for patients visit.

• Assist veterinarian in pulling medical records or locating patient history.

• File client information in permanent files.

• Take prescription and food orders and deliver to appropriate veterinarian or pharmacy or customer as appropriate.

• Deliver prescribed medication and supplies to clients.



Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

• Ability to communicate by phone and in person with individuals in a variety of situations in a positive and helpful manner.

• Ability to maintain confidentiality of medical records.

• Ability to multi-task and deal with multiple priorities.

• Knowledge of veterinary hospital routines and functions.

• Ability to assess emergencies and refer to appropriate hospital staff.

• Knowledge of medical terminology.

• Knowledge of animal disease symptoms.

• Ability to come in contact with animals.

• Ability to work in an environment that houses and heals sick animals.

• Ability to work in an environment with animal noise, animal odors, animal dander and hair, and animal excrement and blood.

• Ability to utilize veterinary client and patient registration system.

• Ability to enter data with speed and accuracy.

• Ability to provide assistance to veterinary students who are learning office systems and processes.

• Ability to work as part of a team.

• Ability to retrieve files and pet supplies.

• Ability to carry/hold/restrain animals.

title: Planning Process System Expert
description:
Planning Process System Expert

Description -

Job Description for Planning Process System Expert and IBP Consultant

Business Environment

HP creates new possibilities for technology to have a meaningful impact on people, businesses, governments and society. The world’s largest technology company and ranked 10 on the Fortune 500 list for 2012, HP brings together a portfolio that spans printing, personal computing, software, services and IT infrastructure to serve more than 1 billion customers in over 170 countries on six continents. HP invents, engineers, and delivers technology solutions that drive business value, create social value, and improve the lives of our clients.

About the Engagement

The Print Planning Excellence (PPE) team is responsible for managing and executing production planning systems, data, and processes supporting global and regional Print and Personal Systems businesses within HP. The team focuses on ensuring that demand and supply plans are complete, reliable, accurate, and available on time to support effective business planning and execution.

The Planning Process System Expert and IBP Consultant would work closely with business planning teams, IT, and cross-functional stakeholders to support the execution of demand and supply planning processes. The consultant would monitor daily and weekly planning activities, analyse planning data, identify process and system issues, and coordinate with relevant teams to drive timely resolution.

The role would also support master data accuracy, planning metrics and reporting, business-user queries, and planning cycle readiness. The consultant would act as a key connection point between the planning community and IT, supporting issue resolution, process improvements, testing, and implementation of planning system enhancements.

The objective of the role is to ensure stable and timely planning execution, high-quality planning data, effective issue resolution, and continuous improvement of planning processes.

Planning Process System Expert and IBP Consultant
Execute → Monitor → Analyse → Resolve → Support

Key Roles & Responsibilities

ü Support and manage end-to-end Demand and Supply Planning activities across Print, S&G, and Personal Systems businesses.

ü Execute daily, weekly, and periodic planning processes, ensuring planning activities are completed accurately and on time.

ü Analyse planning data and reports to identify demand, supply, forecast, and planning-system issues and highlight potential business impacts.

ü Monitor key supply chain and planning KPIs, including forecast accuracy, demand-supply alignment, and other operational planning indicators.

ü Identify planning gaps and operational risks, perform initial root-cause analysis, escalate critical issues, and coordinate actions toward resolution.

ü Partner closely with Business SMEs, IT, and cross-functional teams to troubleshoot planning issues and ensure demand and supply alignment.

ü Communicate planning issues, business impact, corrective actions, and resolutions to relevant stakeholders and support/lead regular SME discussions.

ü Identify opportunities for process improvement, standardization, automation, and cost reduction across demand and supply planning processes.

ü Participate in cross-functional projects and planning transformation initiatives, including business requirements, testing, validation, and implementation activities.

ü Support the implementation, stabilization, and continuous improvement of planning tools and systems, while maintaining process documentation, controls, and planning best practices.

Planning Process System Expert and IBP Consultant – Skills Required

ü Demand & Supply Planning Fundamentals
Good understanding of demand planning, supply planning, forecasting, inventory, and demand-supply balancing.

ü Planning Systems Knowledge
Working knowledge of SAP IBP, SAP HANA, ARIBA, Enterprises Business Wearhouse or similar supply-chain planning systems.

ü Data Analysis
Strong analytical skills with the ability to review planning data, identify exceptions, trends, gaps, and potential issues.

ü Planning KPI & Performance Monitoring
Understanding of planning metrics such as forecast accuracy, demand-supply match, inventory, backlog, and service-level indicators.

ü Problem Solving & Root-Cause Analysis
Ability to investigate day-to-day process, data, and system issues and support root-cause identification and resolution.

ü Excel & Reporting Skills
Strong knowledge of Microsoft Excel; exposure to Power BI or other reporting/analytics tools is preferred.

ü Master Data & Data Quality
Basic understanding of master-data dependencies and the importance of data quality within planning processes.

ü Stakeholder Collaboration
Ability to coordinate effectively with planners, Business SMEs, IT/support teams, and other cross-functional stakeholders.

ü Communication Skills
Ability to clearly communicate planning issues, business impact, risks, corrective actions, and resolution status.

ü Testing & Implementation Support
Ability to support requirements gathering, UAT, validation, implementation, go-live, and stabilization activities.

Education & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, master’s in supply chain, or a related discipline. BTech, BE, MCA, or equivalent qualification preferred.
  • 1–3 years of overall experience, preferably with exposure to Supply Chain, Demand Planning, Supply Planning, or Planning Operations.
  • Working knowledge or hands-on exposure to SAP APO and/or SAP IBP modules.
  • Basic understanding of end-to-end Demand and Supply Planning processes.
  • Exposure to SAP S/4HANA, SAP Ariba, or related supply-chain applications is an added advantage.
  • Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word for analysis, reporting, and business presentations.
  • Knowledge of SQL, MS Access, Excel Macros/VBA, Power BI, or other data/automation technologies is an added advantage.
  • Willingness and flexibility to work across different time zones based on business requirements.

Soft Skills

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work effectively with Business, IT, and cross-functional teams.
  • Strong attention to detail, particularly when working with planning and master data.
  • Ability to learn new processes, systems, and technologies quickly.
  • Good time management and prioritization skills.
  • Proactive approach toward issue identification and resolution.
  • Strong teamwork and collaboration skills.
  • Customer and business-oriented mindset.
  • Willingness to take ownership and accountability for assigned activities.

Job -

Supply Chain & Operations

Full time

Shift -

No shift premium (India)

Relocation -

title: Principal Developer (Aspen)
description:
Job Purpose:

The Principal Developer – Aspen designs, develops, tests, and supports (Manufacturing Execution System) MES solutions using Aspen Manufacturing Suite. The role translates business and manufacturing requirements into reliable, secure, and compliant system solutions, including configurations, databases, integrations, and custom applications. The role supports troubleshooting of complex technical issues, uses approved AI-assisted development tools to improve efficiency, and ensures all solutions meet quality, security, data integrity, and (Good Practice) GxP requirements. The Principal Developer - Aspen also promotes standardization, reusable solutions, and best practices across MES platforms and teams.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Design, configure, develop, and implement MES solutions using Aspen Manufacturing Suite.
  • Translate business and manufacturing requirements into technical solutions by developing and maintaining system integrations, database objects, and custom applications to support business needs.
  • Perform testing, deployment, and validation activities to ensure system reliability and compliance.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve MES application issues and provide production support.
  • Use approved development and AI-assisted tools to improve productivity and solution quality.
  • Ensure compliance with GxP, data integrity, cybersecurity, and company standards.
  • Create and maintain technical documentation, design specifications, and support materials.
  • Contribute to standardization, best practices, and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Collaborate with business users, project teams, and vendors to successfully deliver MES projects while providing technical guidance, mentoring, and knowledge sharing to team members.
  • Participate in system upgrades, enhancements, and lifecycle management activities
  • Develop expertise across MES platforms, software technologies, and AI tools to effectively support and deliver solutions across multiple MES systems
  • Use AI-assisted development as the default way of coding, testing, reviewing and documenting, and validate all AI-generated output for quality, security, data integrity and GxP before release.
  • Implement version control and automated build, test, and deployment practices where supported, achieving improved release quality and deployment efficiency. Monitor production performance, proactively identify and eliminate root causes of issues, reducing recurring incidents and improving system reliability and availability.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s or master’s degree in engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, Automation, Data, Life Sciences or a relevant technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Relevant technical, AI, cloud, integration, automation, data, validation, cyber security or engineering certifications.
  • Minimum 7+ years of hands-on technical engineering experience in complex enterprise or operational technology environments.
  • Experience in Aspen Manufacturing Suite MES and the ability to work across multiple MES platforms.
  • Experience in leading MES solution delivery across products, platforms and sites.
  • Experience in software development, database technologies and system integrations within manufacturing or enterprise environments.
  • Experience in industrial connectivity technologies such as OPC UA (Unified Architecture)/OPC HDA (Historical Data Access) and manufacturing system integrations.
  • Experience in technical review, troubleshooting and root-cause analysis.
  • Experience in coordinating cross-functional teams and vendors to deliver compliant solutions that can be operated and scaled.
  • Experience in managing technical risk, ensuring data integrity, GxP compliance and supporting audits and inspections.
  • Experience in mentoring engineers and supporting technical best practices and standardisation.
  • Experience in using AI-assisted development tools and applying software quality, security, compliance and maintainability controls.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in problem-solving, technical leadership and communication.
  • Experience in developing solution designs, managing technical documentation and supporting compliant system delivery.
  • Experience in integrations, data management, security, quality and change control processes.
  • Experience in collaborating across teams, mentoring engineers and supporting standardisation, automation and continuous improvement.

#AGTech

#GSK-LI


Skills

Agile Methodology, API Management, CI/CD, Cloud Based Services, Computer Programming, Configuration Management (CM), Containerization, Database Management, High Availability (Inactive), Infrastructure As Code (IaC), Microservices Architecture, Network Security, Operating Systems (OS), System Monitors, Version Control System

Why GSK?

Uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together.

GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. We aim to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade, as a successful, growing company where people can thrive. We get ahead of disease by preventing and treating it with innovation in specialty medicines and vaccines. People and patients around the world count on the medicines and vaccines we make, so we’re committed to creating an environment where our people can thrive and focus on what matters most. title: Environmental Specialist I, II & III
description:
This posting will end on:

12/18/2026

At Williams, we’re powering a cleaner, more connected future, and that starts with you. Here, your work fuels communities, drives innovation, and helps deliver reliable energy the world depends on. Join a Fortune 500 team that invests in your growth, values your contributions, and challenges you to make a lasting impact every day.


Day in the Life of an Environmental Specialist:

As an Environmental Specialist I, II, or III on the Mid Atlantic field environmental team, you will apply technical expertise in air, water, chemical management, and/or waste. You will manage moderately complex projects and compliance programs that call for specialized, wide-ranging knowledge. Your day includes collecting operational data, submitting regulatory reports, conducting environmental sampling and testing, and participating in management of change processes to identify regulatory requirements. You will also serve as the point of contact for incident reporting, covering both event response and communication with regulatory agencies. You will track evolving regulations, such as updates to the Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, Resource Conservation and Recovery Act, Toxic Substance Control Act, Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act and guide operational changes to maintain compliance. The role also includes field engagements, training field staff, handling permit renewals and improvements, and working with engineering and operations teams on broader environmental initiatives.


Environmental Specialist I

  • Bachelor’s degree and 1+ year of related experience
  • Developing technical knowledge; routine permitting and compliance support
  • Works with guidance; gathers data, maintains records, researches requirements, prepares routine submittals, and supports senior staff

Environmental Specialist II

  • Bachelor’s degree and 2+ years of environmental experience
  • Functional knowledge across one or more environmental media; straightforward risk and compliance matters
  • Works with increasing independence; provides guidance and training, coordinates routine permits, and prepares compliance reports and plans

  • Bachelor’s degree and 4+ years of environmental experience
  • Technical expertise; moderate-complexity projects, programs, permits, audits, and risk matters

title: Water Treatment Operations Supervisor
description:
Water Operations Supervisor
Jasper GA
Are you an experienced water professional ready to take the next step in leadership? We are seeking a Water Operations Supervisor to oversee the day-to-day operation, maintenance, and regulatory compliance of our water treatment and distribution systems. In this role, you'll lead a skilled team, ensure safe and efficient plant operations, and play a critical role in delivering high-quality drinking water to the communities we serve.
This is an excellent opportunity for a licensed water treatment professional who thrives in a hands-on leadership role and is passionate about operational excellence, team development, and public service.
What You'll Do
As the Water Operations Supervisor, you will:

Lead the continuous operation of water treatment plants, wells, standpipes, distribution systems, and related infrastructure.
Supervise and support operations staff, ensuring work is completed safely, efficiently, and in compliance with all regulatory requirements.
Monitor plant performance and operational processes, making adjustments as needed to maintain system reliability and water quality.
Prepare and review internal, regulatory, and client reports.
Verify staff compliance with operational procedures, maintenance programs, laboratory protocols, QA/QC standards, and safety requirements.
Conduct regular meetings with department leaders to review performance metrics, operational goals, and continuous improvement opportunities.
Assist in establishing facility objectives, operational strategies, and workforce planning initiatives.
Respond effectively to emergency situations and implement corrective actions when necessary.
Champion a strong safety culture by overseeing and enforcing company safety programs and standards.
Participate in hiring, interviewing, onboarding, coaching, performance evaluations, and disciplinary processes.
Develop and approve staff schedules to ensure adequate operational coverage.
Support budgeting, planning, and administrative functions.
Serve as acting Project Manager when needed.
Build positive relationships with customers, clients, municipal officials, and community stakeholders.

What We're Looking For
Required Qualifications

High school diploma or GED required.
Additional college coursework or vocational training in chemistry, environmental science, water technology, or a related field preferred.
Minimum of five (5) years of experience in water treatment, water distribution, system maintenance, construction, or related utility operations.
Class I Water Treatment Plant Operator License (or equivalent license required by the state of employment).
Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record.

Knowledge & Experience
Successful candidates will have knowledge of:

Surface water treatment processes and groundwater operations.
Water quality regulations, permits, and compliance requirements.
Pumps, motors, valves, engines, and related mechanical equipment.
Backflow prevention devices and cross-connection control practices.
Supervising, mentoring, and developing employees.
Utility operations, maintenance planning, and emergency response procedures.

Skills for Success

Strong leadership and team development capabilities.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Ability to evaluate operating parameters and optimize treatment processes.
Experience operating process control systems and laboratory equipment.
Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and decision-making abilities.

Work Environment
This role combines office responsibilities with field and plant operations. You will work in both indoor and outdoor environments and may be exposed to changing weather conditions, mechanical equipment, chemicals, noise, dust, and other industrial settings. Appropriate safety procedures and personal protective equipment are required.
Physical Requirements

Ability to stand, walk, climb, bend, kneel, crouch, and work around operational equipment for extended periods.
Frequently lift, carry, push, or pull up to 50 pounds.
Ability to work in confined spaces and elevated areas when required.
Must be able to distinguish between different shades of color for operational and safety purposes.
Available to work overtime and respond to emergency situations outside normal business hours, including weekends and holidays when necessary

title: Materials Lead
description:
Flex is the diversified manufacturing partner of choice that helps market-leading brands design, build and deliver innovative products that improve the world.

A career at Flex offers the opportunity to make a difference and invest in your growth in a respectful, inclusive, and collaborative environment. If you are excited about a role but don't meet every bullet point, we encourage you to apply and join us to create the extraordinary.

Job Summary





Flex is hiring for Materials Lead in Pflugerville, TX.

Summary

The Materials Lead is responsible for leading day-to-day warehouse and material handling operations to ensure materials are delivered accurately and on time in support of production. This position combines hands-on warehouse responsibilities with team leadership, coordinating daily activities, monitoring material flow, preventing production disruptions, and supporting a safe, efficient, and customer-focused operation.

The Materials Lead serves as a key resource for the warehouse team, helping drive safety, inventory accuracy, productivity, and continuous improvement initiatives while ensuring uninterrupted support of manufacturing operations.

Shift: 7AM - 3:30PM | Mon to Fri

Location: Pflugerville, TX

What a Typical Day Looks Like

  • Coordinate daily warehouse and material handling activities to support production requirements and customer commitments.
  • Ensure materials are delivered accurately and on time to production areas, with a strong focus on preventing line-down situations and maintaining operational continuity.
  • Monitor material flow, inventory levels, and warehouse operations to proactively identify and resolve potential issues before they impact production.
  • Escalate staffing, material shortages, equipment issues, inventory discrepancies, and process concerns to the supervisor in a timely manner.
  • Lead by example in promoting Flex's Ways of Working while maintaining a respectful, professional, and inclusive environment.
  • Hold team members accountable for safety, quality, productivity, attendance, and compliance with standard operating procedures.
  • Support employee training and cross-training efforts to ensure workforce flexibility and operational effectiveness.
  • Assist with onboarding new team members and provide daily coaching, guidance, and support.
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives focused on warehouse efficiency, inventory accuracy, material flow, and productivity improvements.
  • Partner with Production, Planning, Inventory Control, Shipping, and Receiving teams to ensure seamless material movement throughout the facility.
  • Monitor key performance indicators and help drive achievement of operational goals.
  • Ensure compliance with company policies, safety standards, quality requirements, and warehouse best practices.
  • Operate material handling equipment such as forklifts, reach trucks, pallet jacks, and RF scanning devices as required.
  • Support inventory transactions, cycle counts, material audits, and inventory accuracy initiatives.
  • Assist with shipping, receiving, stocking, replenishment, and inventory control activities as business needs require.

The Experience We're Looking to Add to Our Team

title: Development Specialist
description:
What We Can Achieve Together:


The Development Program Specialist I will work as part of a functional team of organizational priority within a development program. The team will be responsible for providing resources such as research, gift processing, prospect tracking, stewardship, etc.


The Development Program Specialist I will work towards meeting the strategic priorities of the team by implementing tactics for approved plans and completing and organizing varied tasks and activities. They will identify day-to-day priorities based on needs of the program. They will manage, track, and report on key data related to the team scope and priorities. The Specialist will perform independent analysis on key program data, which may include donor or gift information. They will be responsible for processing gifts. They will provide support and targeted training related to the functional area of the team. The Specialist I must maintain advanced skills with the systems and resources utilized by the team in order to execute tasks. They will implement processes and practices in order to improve effectiveness based on their in-depth understanding of related policies and procedures. The Specialist I will effectively communicate or distribute information to assist staff in making decisions, solving problems, and improving workflow. The position will require occasional travel. The work environment may involve infrequent exposure to disagreeable elements and minor physical exertion and/or strain.


We’re Looking for You:


Want to help save the planet? The Nature Conservancy's mission is to protect the lands and waters on which all life depends. From the mountains to the sea, the Maryland/DC and Florida Chapters are dedicated to conserving the natural resources that make these places unique. Relationship building, project coordination, data entry and management, and creativity are key in this role. Come join TNC and apply today!


This is a fully remote role, open to candidates based in the state of Florida.


Responsibilities & Scope:

  • Enter gifts and commitments into constituent management system (CRMS) consistent with donor intent and TNC’s best practices. Manage/track revenue, including but not limited to:
    • Analyze gift related documentation (agreements, commitment forms, donor interactions; internal SOPs and best practices) to determine and code revenue based on donor requirements.
    • Monitor conditional gifts / commitments and work with Conservation and Finance colleagues to adjust as conditions are met.
    • Manage Master Donor File (MDF). Keep all information related to gifts and commitments securely stored in MDF and collaborate with team to ensure donor related information is up to date in MDF.
    • Process adjustments to revenue as needed and in a timely manner
  • Participate in recurring development operations calls and monitor other operations communications to maintain knowledge of TNC contribution revenue management and accounting best practices.
  • Produce donor reports and provide key revenue data to staff and collaboratively work towards identifying opportunities and gaps.
  • Manage commitment payments reminders and report requirements and track key data on CRMS.
  • Participate in the quarterly Commitments Review and Certification process with Finance teams and follow up on action items on the philanthropy operations side.
  • Assist staff in reviewing proposals and commitment documentation for coding and compliance with TNC gift recording policy.
  • Produce weekly gift and commitment reports and actively participate as needed in the stewardship process.
  • Provide interim revenue processing for other business units with manager approval.
  • Produce accurate mailing lists and invitation lists as requested and according to established parameters and deadlines.
  • Provide operational support including printing, mailing, data entry, and responding to or redirecting constituent outreach.
  • Act independently on assigned tasks and exercise independent judgment based on analysis and experience.
  • Coordinate revenue-related projects with several variables, work within a defined timeline and budget.
  • Does not supervise any staff, but may supervise interns, volunteers, and/or temporary staff.
  • Ensure compliance with TNC policies and procedures, and external (donor/legal/IRS) requirements. Maintain confidentiality of highly sensitive data.
  • Provide input through project teams for the improvement of existing and new processes and programs.
  • Some travel required to include BU off-site meetings and team retreats; flexible hours.
  • Work environment involves only infrequent exposure to disagreeable elements and minor physical exertion and/or strain.
  • Work is diversified and may not always fall under established practices and guidelines.

What You’ll Bring:

  • Bachelor’s degree and 2 years’ experience or equivalent combination.
  • Experience building relationships with staff, customers or similar.
  • Experience generating reports and interpreting data.
  • Experience in business writing, editing, and proofreading.
  • Experience working across teams.
  • Experience, coursework, or other training in principles and practices of relevant field.

Desired Qualifications:

  • Ability to analyze information for the purpose of coordinating and planning activities and solving problems.
  • Ability to use existing technology to achieve desired results.
  • Ability to work under pressure and perform repetitive data entry tasks.
  • Experience interpreting guidelines to achieve desired results.
  • Experience with databases and spreadsheet software.
  • Strong organization skills, accuracy, and attention to detail.
  • Multi-lingual skills and multi-cultural or cross-cultural experience are appreciated.

Salary Information:


The starting pay range for a candidate selected for this position is generally within the range of $29.49 - $34.84 per hour. This range only applies to candidates whose country of employment is the USA. Where a successful candidate’s actual pay will fall within this range will be based on a variety of factors, including, for example, the candidate's location, qualifications, specific skills, and experience. Please note countries outside the USA would have a different pay range in the local currency based on the local labor market, and not tied to USA pay or ranges. Your geographic location will be confirmed during the recruitment.


Who We Are:

The Nature Conservancy’s mission is to protect the lands and waters upon which all life depends. As a science-based organization, we create innovative, on-the-ground solutions to our world’s toughest challenges so that we can create a world in which people and nature thrive. We’re rooted in our mission and guided by our values, which include respect for all people, communities, and cultures. Whether it’s career development, flexible schedules, or a rewarding mission, there’s many reasons to love life inside TNC. Want a better insight to TNC? Check out our TNC Talent playlist on YouTube to hear stories from staff or visit Glassdoor.

One goal is to cultivate an inclusive work environment so that all our colleagues around the globe feel a sense of belonging and that their unique contributions to our mission are valued. In addition to the requirements in our job postings, we recognize that people come with talent and experiences outside of a job and consider each applicant’s unique experience. Please apply – we’d love to hear from you. To quote a popular saying at TNC, “you’ll join for the mission, and stay for the people.”

What We Bring:


Since 1951, TNC has been doing work you can believe in. Through grassroots action, we have grown from a small non-profit into one of the most effective and wide-reaching environmental organizations in the world. Thanks to more than 1 million members, over 400 scientists, and the dedicated efforts of our diverse staff and partners, we impact conservation around the world!

TNC offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package including health care benefits, flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) plan with an 8% employer match, parental leave, accrued paid time off, life insurance, disability coverage, employee assistance program, other life and work well-being benefits. Learn more about our Benefits and Perks here.

We’re proud to offer a flexible work environment that supports of the health and well-being of the people we employ.

Our recruiting process includes a rolling interview process to ensure we engage applicants in a timely manner. This means we may review applications in the order in which they are received. Once a strong candidate pool is identified, the role will be unposted. The timeline may vary depending on the expressed interest in the role, so we highly encourage candidates to apply as soon as possible.

Employees must submit their application by logging into Workday and applying via the Jobs Hub.

The Nature Conservancy is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Our commitment to equal employment opportunity includes the recognition that our conservation mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people of all backgrounds, beliefs, and culture. Recruiting and mentoring staff to create an inclusive organization is a priority, and we encourage applicants from all cultures, races, colors, religions, sexes, national or regional origins, ages, disability status, sexual orientation, gender identity, military, protected veteran status or other status protected by law.


The successful applicant must meet the requirements of The Nature Conservancy's background screening process.

Do you have military experience? Visit our U.S. Military Skills Translator to match your military experience with our current job openings!

TNC is committed to offering accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application process. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please send a note to applyhelp@tnc.org with Request for Accommodation in the subject line.

title: Associate Director, Content Approval
description:
As an Associate Director – Content Approval, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring the global promotional and non-promotional content meets the highest standards of quality, scientific accuracy, balance, and compliance. This includes adherence to internal GSK standards and applicable external regulations, including a robust understanding of the ABPI code of practice. This role will involve the fostering of robust relationships and collaborations within a highly matrixed environment which includes but is not limited to Commercial, Legal, Medical Affairs, Regulatory Affairs, Clinical Development, and third-party suppliers at a Global level.

Key Responsibilities:

This role will provide you the opportunity to utilize your expertise in the scientific area, understanding of the internal business strategies, applicable GSK processes/policies, and the external regulations including the ABPI code of practice to ensure global content is compliant, accurate, up-to-date, and fit for purpose for external engagement. These responsibilities include the following:

· Primary medical reviewer and/or approver who is accountable for the thorough, timely review and approval of Global promotional and non-promotional materials.

· Ensure content is scientifically accurate, meets the scientific rigor (i.e., levels of evidence); is fair-balanced and meets the GSK requirements/standards/processes as well as complies with applicable external regulations (incl. ABPI Code where relevant)

· Maintain deep scientific and therapeutic expertise on assigned products and therapy areas

· Maintain a deep understanding of ABPI Code of practice (as an AQP/Appropriately Qualified Person) and the GSK interpretation/position to ensure consistent application while reviewing and/or approving global medical or commercial content in scope of ABPI.

· Strong understanding of the business strategies/unmet needs to ensure the content is aligned with current medical practices/guidelines, and the content is fit for purpose to the targeted audience.

· Work alongside various business partners to align, validate, and identify solutions to ensure content is of the highest quality and relevant to the audience

· Provide timely feedback and recommendations for content created and/or reviewed by third-party vendors and escalate when third-party vendors do not meet the quality standards

· Address and/or escalate to appropriate leadership when content may result in a risk to the business

· Stay up to date with evolving regulatory requirements, industry standards, and best practices to ensure continuous compliance

· Identify issues, themes and/or opportunities for continuous improvement that enhance the quality and compliance of materials and activities

· Serve as a key point of contact for regulatory and legal teams during audits and inspections, providing documentation and insights as needed

· Actively participate in workstreams to develop best practices, ways of working and continuous improvement for promotional and non-promotional content approval process

· Actively contribute and provide input to content creation plans to ensure content deliverables and timelines are realistic and achievable

· Support other GMI&CA team activities (e.g. MI content creation, US medical review), when required and in onboarding new content approval team members.


Basic Qualifications:

We are looking for professionals with these required skills to achieve our goals:

  • Graduate Degree in Life Sciences or Healthcare (e.g. master’s level, PharmD, PhD)
  • 4+ years of pharmaceutical industry experience
  • 3+ years of Medical Affairs experience as a reviewer of content used in promotional and non-promotional settings
  • Strong organizational and planning skills
  • Understanding of the typical commercial and medical activities from a global perspective in the pharmaceutical industry (e.g., promotion, medical education, external partnerships, advisory boards)
  • Strong clinical literature evaluation skills
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills
  • Ability to work independently and manage/prioritize multiple projects simultaneously
  • Ability to accurately evaluate and summarize complex scientific literature, real-world evidence, and other observational research studies for scientific evaluation needs by various customer types
  • Ability to clearly communicate complex scientific data in a concise and accurate manner
  • Demonstrated customer-focus, problem solving abilities and strong conflict resolution skills

Preferred Qualifications:

If you have the following characteristics, it would be a plus:

  • Strong understanding of content approval requirements incl. external regulations (e.g. ABPI Code)
  • Strong understanding of international Codes of Practice FDA, IFPMA, EFIPIA, IPHA, ABPI etc
  • Capable to cope with pressure and meet tight timelines
  • Experience of working at both global and local country level
  • Experience working with global teams in a matrix environment
  • Ability to work effectively with others, delegate appropriately and foster a strong culture of teamwork

Skills

Cross-Functional Leadership, Digital Fluency, Enterprise Thinking, High Impact Communication, Launch Excellence, Patient Impact

Why GSK?

Uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together.

GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. We aim to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade, as a successful, growing company where people can thrive. We get ahead of disease by preventing and treating it with innovation in specialty medicines and vaccines. We focus on four therapeutic areas: respiratory, immunology and inflammation; oncology; HIV; and infectious diseases – to impact health at scale.

People and patients around the world count on the medicines and vaccines we make, so we’re committed to creating an environment where our people can thrive and focus on what matters most. Our culture of being ambitious for patients, accountable for impact and doing the right thing is the foundation for how, together, we deliver for patients, shareholders and our people.

GSK is an Equal Opportunity Employer. This ensures that all qualified applicants will receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, gender identity, and sexual orientation), parental status, national origin, age, disability, genetic information (including family medical history), military service or any basis prohibited under federal, state or local law.

We believe in an agile working culture for all our roles. If flexibility is important to you, we encourage you to explore with our hiring team what the opportunities are.

Please note should your enquiry not relate to adjustments, we will not be able to support you through these channels. However, we have created a Recruitment FAQ guide. Click the link where you will find answers to multiple questions we receive
