title: Manager Workplace Safety and Workers Compensation
description:
Are you a person who believes in providing great care? Do you believe in having a positive impact on other people's lives? Are you a team player, quick-thinker, and ready to be a part of an organization that supports your growth?


WHAT WE'RE ABOUT

We believe care goes beyond a medical chart. With kindness and integrity as our guide, we strive for excellence in every interaction.


Requirements:

  • You care
  • Clinical/Healthcare experience
  • Workers Comp and OSHA Experience

POSITION SUMMARY

The Manager Workplace Safety and Workers Compensation provides strategic leadership and oversight of workplace safety, occupational risk, workers' compensation, loss preventiona nd claims management programs across multiple skilled nursing and long-term care facilities throughout Colorado.

The position is responsible for developing, implementing, and continuously improving an organization-wide safety and risk management program designed to protect employees, residents, visitors, physical assets, and the organization. This position partners closely with facility leadership and executive departments to identify hazards, reduce workplace injuries, strengthen regulatory compliance, manage organizational risk, and promote a proactive culture of safety.

The position provides leadership for the organization's OSHA compliance, workers' compensation program, injury and illness prevention efforts, safety committees, incident investigations, safety education, risk assessments, and corrective action processes. The position analyzes injury, claims, and safety data to identify trends and develop strategies that reduce frequency and severity of workplace incidents and associated costs.

This position supports multiple facilities and requires approximately 10-15% travel throughout Colorado.


DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Develops, implements, and oversees the organization's comprehensive workplace safety, occupational risk, and loss prevention strategy across multiple skilled nursing and long-term care facilities.

  • Establishes policies, procedures, standards, and programs that promote a strong and consistent culture of safety throughout the organization.

  • Conducts and oversees facility risk assessments and safety audits to identify hazards, areas of exposure, and opportunities for improvement.

  • Develops annual and long-term risk reduction initiatives based on injury trends, workers' compensation experience, regulatory requirements, facility assessments, and organizational priorities.

  • Partners with facility Administrators, Directors of Nursing, Human Resources, Operations, and other leaders to implement corrective action plans and improve safety performance.

  • Provides leadership, guidance, and support to facility safety committees and ensures appropriate follow-through on identified risks and corrective actions.

  • Advises senior leadership regarding significant workplace safety and risk exposures and recommends appropriate mitigation strategies.

  • OSHA & Regulatory Compliance

  • Leads organizational efforts to maintain compliance with applicable OSHA workplace safety and health requirements and other applicable federal and Colorado requirements.

  • Oversees OSHA recordkeeping practices and works with appropriate stakeholders to support accurate and timely documentation of occupational injuries and illnesses.

  • Supports facilities during OSHA inspections, inquiries, complaints, and other workplace safety matters.

  • Monitors changes to applicable workplace safety requirements and recommends policy, procedure, training, or operational changes as necessary.

  • Ensures safety programs appropriately address hazards relevant to skilled nursing and long-term care environments.

  • Partners with facility and organizational leadership to maintain appropriate programs related to safe patient/resident handling; ergonomics and musculoskeletal injury prevention; slips, trips, and falls; workplace violence prevention; bloodborne pathogen and exposure risks; personal protective equipment; hazard communication; emergency preparedness; and other occupational hazards relevant to healthcare environments.

  • Workers' Compensation & Claims Management

  • Provides strategic oversight of the organization's Colorado workers' compensation program, working with internal stakeholders, insurance carriers, third-party administrators, brokers, legal counsel, and medical providers as appropriate.

  • Monitors workers' compensation claims from initial reporting through resolution and promotes timely communication between the appropriate stakeholders.

  • Reviews workers' compensation data to identify injury patterns, claim trends, high-risk locations, recurring causes, and opportunities for prevention.

  • Monitors claim activity, reserves, costs, and significant developments and communicates material issues to appropriate organizational leadership.

  • Partners with Compliance, Human Resources, Operations, and facility leadership to support effective return-to-work and modified-duty processes.

  • Conducts or coordinates claim reviews with appropriate internal and external partners.

  • Identifies opportunities to reduce claim frequency, severity, lost workdays, and overall organizational risk.

  • Ensures workers' compensation practices align with applicable Colorado requirements.

  • Incident Investigation & Loss Prevention

  • Oversees investigation of significant employee injuries, workplace incidents, safety events, and other identified areas of organizational risk.

  • Leads or facilitates root cause analyses to identify contributing factors and appropriate corrective actions.

  • Ensures corrective actions are assigned, documented, communicated, and monitored for completion.

  • Uses incident and claims data to identify systemic risks rather than addressing events solely on a case-by-case basis.

  • Develops targeted injury-prevention initiatives for facilities or departments demonstrating elevated risk or recurring trends.

  • Partners with operational and clinical leadership to implement sustainable solutions while maintaining resident care and operational effectiveness.

  • Training & Safety Culture

  • Develops and oversees safety education and training programs for employees and leaders.

  • Ensures required workplace safety training appropriately addresses identified hazards and employee exposures.

  • Coaches facility leadership on effective safety practices, accident prevention, incident investigation, and employee engagement.

  • Develops tools, communications, and resources that reinforce accountability for workplace safety at all levels of the organization.

  • Promotes employee participation in hazard identification, incident prevention, and safety improvement initiatives.

  • Data, Reporting & Performance Improvement

  • Develops and monitors key safety and risk indicators across the organization.

  • Analyzes workers' compensation, injury, incident, and safety data to identify emerging risks and opportunities for improvement.

  • Creates reports and presentations for executive and operational leadership highlighting trends, areas of exposure, corrective actions, and recommended strategies.

  • Establishes measurable safety goals and monitors facility and organizational progress.

  • Uses data and industry best practices to drive continuous improvement in workplace safety and injury prevention.

  • Evaluates effectiveness of implemented risk-control measures and adjusts strategies as necessary.

  • Serves as a subject matter resource toFacility and Executive leadership regarding workplace safety, occupational risk, and workers' compensation.

  • Collaborates with insurance brokers, carriers, third-party administrators, legal counsel, consultants, and other external partners as appropriate.

  • Supports insurance and risk management activities as assigned.

  • Maintains confidential information and documentation in accordance with organizational requirements.

  • Travels to facility locations to conduct assessments, investigations, training, leadership meetings, and other risk and safety activities.

  • Performs other duties related to organizational risk and safety as assigned.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES & QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Occupational Safety, Risk Management, Business Administration, Healthcare Administration, Human Resources, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.

  • Progressive experience in workplace safety, risk management, workers' compensation, occupational health, or a related discipline.

  • Demonstrated experience managing or supporting safety and workers' compensation programs across multiple locations.

  • Working knowledge of OSHA workplace safety requirements and injury and illness prevention practices.

  • Knowledge of workers' compensation claims management and injury prevention principles.

  • Experience conducting workplace investigations, root cause analyses, safety assessments, and corrective action planning.

  • Strong analytical skills with demonstrated ability to interpret injury, claims, and safety data and translate findings into actionable recommendations.

  • Strong leadership, interpersonal, and influencing skills with the ability to partner effectively with facility and senior leadership.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex risk and safety matters clearly.

  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities, facilities, and initiatives.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office products, including Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and Outlook.

  • Valid driver's license and ability to travel approximately 10-15% throughout Colorado.

    Preferred

  • Experience in skilled nursing, long-term care, senior living, healthcare, or another multi-site healthcare environment.

  • Experience overseeing safety and workers' compensation programs across a multi-facility organization.

  • Professional safety or risk management certification such as CSP, ASP, ARM, or similar credential.

  • Experience working with insurance carriers, third-party administrators, brokers, legal counsel, and occupational healthcare providers.

  • Experience developing and delivering safety training for both frontline employees and leadership.

  • RN or other healthcare-related license or clinical background is a plus but not required.

BENEFITS

  • Medical insurance
  • Dental insurance
  • Vision care
  • 401k retirement savings plan
  • Paid vacation

title: Instructional Designer - Senior Manager
description:
When you join Verizon

You want more out of a career. A place to share your ideas freely — even if they’re daring or different. Where the true you can learn, grow, and thrive. At Verizon, we power and empower how people live, work and play by connecting them to what brings them joy. We do what we love — driving innovation, creativity, and impact in the world. Our V Team is a community of people who anticipate, lead, and believe that listening is where learning begins. In crisis and in celebration, we come together — lifting our communities and building trust in how we show up, everywhere & always. Want in? Join the #VTeamLife.

What you'll be doing...


Verizon Connect is hiring an Instructional Designer, Senior Manager. This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who is both a learning scientist and a craftsperson. You will be the lead builder of the learning experiences our customers use. You will take a customer problem from first idea to finished experience yourself: the design, the writing, the visuals, the video, the interaction and the measurement. Your work will range from a 30-second in-product walkthrough to a full role-based learning path, and all of it will look and feel like one product. You will be measured on whether customers adopt the product faster and need less help, not on how much content you publish. We move fast. You will deliver a useful version in days, learn from the data and improve it.

Responsibilities will include:


  • Designing and building customer learning across formats, including in-product walkthroughs, short video, interactive simulations, self-paced modules, job aids and materials for live sessions, and choosing the smallest format that solves the problem.
  • Applying learning science and strong design craft together, so every piece is clear, well written, visually sharp, accessible and built for mobile and short attention spans.
  • Working at release speed by prototyping early, using AI and reusable templates to cut production time, and structuring content in modules so it can be updated in hours when the product changes.
  • Learning the product and the customer first-hand by using it yourself, watching customers work and partnering with Product, UX, Support and delivery teams, without waiting on long review cycles.
  • Using product and learning data to see where customers struggle, testing alternatives, and setting the quality standards, templates and practices the rest of the team builds on.


What we’re looking for...


You are a builder with taste. You can explain why a design works using evidence, and you can also make it look and sound good. You would rather ship a strong first version on Thursday than a perfect one next quarter. You cut words, cut steps and cut content that nobody uses. You are as comfortable in a design file or a video timeline as in a learning objective.

You’ll need to have:


  • Bachelor’s degree or four or more years of work experience.
  • Six or more years of relevant experience required, demonstrated through one or a combination of work and/or military experience, or specialized training.
  • Four or more years of relevant work experience designing and building digital learning.
  • Experience designing for customers of a software or technology product.
  • A portfolio of work you built yourself across at least three formats, such as in-product guidance, video, interactive modules and job aids.
  • Hands-on experience with current authoring, video, design and in-product guidance tools, and the ability to learn new ones quickly.
  • Experience applying evidence-based learning design, including managing cognitive load, practice and feedback, and spaced reinforcement.
  • Writing experience, including scripts, interface microcopy and plain-language instructions.
  • Experience building to accessibility standards, including captions, contrast and screen reader support.
  • Experience using data to improve content after launch, such as usage, drop-off and product adoption.
  • Experience delivering on short timelines while handling several projects at once.



Even better if you have one or more of the following:


  • Experience using AI tools in content production, with your own process for checking accuracy and quality.
  • Experience with fleet, telematics, field service or another product that combines software with hardware in the field.
  • Experience designing for frontline or mobile-first users who are not at a desk.
  • A background in UX design, product design, motion graphics or video production.
  • Experience building content that is ready for translation and regional variation.
  • Working knowledge of HTML, CSS or learning data standards such as SCORM and xAPI.
  • Experience running A/B tests on learning or in-product content.
  • Experience creating templates, style guides or design systems that other creators use.
  • Experience mentoring or leading other designers.

If Verizon and this role sound like a fit for you, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every “even better” qualification listed above.

Where you’ll be working

In this hybrid role, you'll have a defined work location that includes working from home and a minimum of three days per week in the office, which will be set by your manager. Employees are responsible for maintaining compliance with hybrid work policies.

Scheduled Weekly Hours

40

Equal Employment Opportunity

Verizon is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to veteran status, disability or other legally protected characteristics.

Benefits and Compensation

Our benefits are designed to help you move forward in your career, and in areas of your life outside of Verizon. From health and wellness benefit options including: medical, dental, vision, short and long term disability, basic life insurance, supplemental life insurance, AD&D insurance, identity theft protection, pet insurance and group home & auto insurance. We also offer a matched 401(k) savings plan, up to 8 company paid holidays per year and up to 6 personal days per year, paid parental leave, adoption assistance and tuition assistance, plus other incentives, we’ve got you covered with our award-winning total rewards package. Depending on the role, employees have the opportunity to receive compensation in the form of premium pay such as overtime, shift differential, holiday pay, allowances, etc. Newly hired employees receive up to 15 days of vacation per year, which grows with additional service. For part-timers, your coverage will vary as you may be eligible for some of these benefits depending on your individual circumstances.

The salary will vary depending on your location and confirmed job-related skills and experience. This is an incentive based position with the potential to earn more. For part-time roles, your compensation will be adjusted to reflect your hours.

title: Strategy & Transformation Manager
description:
About Wavin Orbia Water & Climate Solutions:

What if your work could improve how water moves, how cities adapt, and how buildings perform every day? At Wavin, Orbia’s Water & Climate Solutions business, this is what we do. Count on a warm welcome, where purpose comes to life. Here, we take responsibility for each other and our company, stay brave in pursuing innovation, and embrace diversity in perspectives, skills and talents. We encourage our employees to develop their talents and become the best version of themselves. Working as a strong team, we grow and advance life around the world. You will join an international, professional team and benefit from a competitive compensation package.

As Strategy & Transformation Manager, you will play a key role in helping Orbia Water & Climate Solutions (Wavin) translate strategic priorities into measurable results. Working closely with senior leaders across the business, you will help drive our global transformation agenda by ensuring progress is tracked, decisions are supported by data, and strategic initiatives deliver tangible value.

A core responsibility of the role is to own and continuously develop the performance management framework for our transformation agenda. You will establish and manage KPI tracking, executive reporting, performance reviews, and follow-up actions across multiple workstreams, creating a transparent and fact-based view of performance at country, business unit, and global level.

Beyond transformation performance management, you will support strategic planning and capital investment governance, providing broad exposure to the priorities that shape the future direction of the business.

This role offers a unique opportunity to work across regions, functions, and leadership teams in a highly international environment, combining strategy, transformation, investment governance, and hands-on execution. If you enjoy connecting data, performance, and strategy to create real business impact, this could be the ideal next step in your career.

Practical Information

  • Location: Flexible across Europe (hybrid), with candidates required to be located within commuting distance of a Wavin office.

  • Scope: Global

  • Traveling: Approximately 10% international travel

What You'll Do

Drive Transformation Performance & Governance

  • Transformation KPI Framework – Establish and own the KPI framework for W&CS’s transformation agenda – defining metrics, targets, baselines and calculation standards with each Excellence workstream to ensure performance is measured consistently and comparably.

  • Multi-Level KPI Tracking & Reporting – Track and report KPIs at country, Business Unit and global level, maintaining the quarterly reporting cadence and producing consolidated performance reports and roadmap updates that demonstrate progress against targets.

  • Stakeholder Management & Governance – Work across global functions and regional Business Units to secure timely and accurate KPI inputs, and govern the standards, processes and reporting cadence that keep transformation reporting reliable.

  • Data & Performance Insights – Source, validate, and analyse performance data from multiple systems and regions, transforming data into actionable insights, visualizations, and recommendations that support decision-making and drive continuous improvement.

  • Excellence Team Partnership – Act as the central performance management partner to the Excellence teams (S&OP, Pricing, Sales Excellence, Global Marketing, AI, Customer Service and Portfolio Optimization), agreeing metric definitions, collecting results, and challenging data quality and performance gaps.

Support Strategy & Business Planning

  • Strategic Planning Support – Support the strategic planning cycle by preparing analyses, materials, and inputs that help shape W&CS strategy and translate strategic priorities into measurable objectives and roadmaps.

  • Cross-Functional Alignment – Collaborate with commercial, operational, and functional leaders to align priorities, assumptions, and business objectives, helping ensure strategic initiatives are translated into coordinated action plans.

  • Leadership Team Meeting Preparation – Prepare leadership team materials and supporting analyses, ensuring meetings are supported by accurate, current and decision-ready content.

This is a high-impact, high-visibility role at the intersection of strategy, transformation, and business performance. title: Analyst, Clinical Data Management
description:
Imagine how your ideas and expertise can change a patient’s life. We generate extensive clinical evidence to demonstrate the effectiveness and safety of our innovations and how our products transform patients’ lives. As part of our Clinical Affairs team, you’ll hone your scientific curiosity and passion for evaluating data to increase access to pioneering technologies for patients in need. In close partnership with principal investigators, dedicated medical professionals, patient advocacy groups, and regulatory authorities, you will drive the evidence needed to optimize patient outcomes.

Patients with mitral and tricuspid heart valve disease often have complex conditions with limited treatment options. Our Transcatheter Mitral and Tricuspid Therapies (TMTT) business unit is boldly pursuing an innovative portfolio of technologies to address a patient’s unmet clinical needs. What else we look for (Preferred):

  • Good computer skills in Microsoft Office Suite
  • Good written and verbal communication skills and interpersonal relationship skills
  • Good problem-solving and critical thinking skills

  • Solid knowledge of processes and procedures in clinical data management
  • Solid knowledge of protocols, DMPs, and SAPs
  • Ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment
  • Strict attention to detail

Aligning our overall business objectives with performance, we offer competitive salaries, performance-based incentives, and a wide variety of benefits programs to address the diverse individual needs of our employees and their families.

title: Senior Principal - Strategic Supplier Manager
description:
GSK remains committed to achieving bold commercial ambitions for the future. By 2031, we aim to deliver £40 billion in annual sales, leveraging our existing strong performance momentum to significantly increase our positive impact on the health of billions of patients globally. Our Ahead Together strategy is centred on early intervention to prevent and alter the course of disease, thereby protecting people and supporting healthcare systems.


Our diverse portfolio consists of vaccines, specialty medicines, and general medicines.


Through continuous innovation and a dedicated focus on scientific and technical excellence, we strive to develop and launch new, groundbreaking treatments that address critical health challenges.

Job Purpose


The Strategic Supplier Manager maximises the value DPTF obtains from its strategic technology suppliers and managed service partners. The role manages those relationships, runs the supplier governance and performance review cycle, holds partners to their committed outcomes, and identifies where partner capability can be used more effectively to accelerate delivery and reduce manual effort.


The role carries direct accountability for the relationships in its portfolio. Procurement and Legal own contractual and commercial negotiation, and this role supplies the performance, value and risk evidence behind it; the platform and product domains own the demand for supplier capability. It partners with the Technology Performance Manager where services span internal teams and partner-delivered capability, and with Business Operations and Finance on spend and commercial position.


Key Responsibilities

  • Manage the relationships with DPTF's strategic technology suppliers and managed service partners, acting as the senior point of contact for performance and value.
  • Develop and maintain a supplier strategy for each strategic partner, setting out what GSK expects from the relationship over time in capability, performance, commercial terms and risk, and reviewing it as the partnership evolves.
  • Run the supplier governance cycle, including operational reviews, quarterly business reviews and executive reviews, ensuring each has a clear agenda, a supporting evidence base and agreed actions.
  • Hold suppliers to their committed outcomes, SLAs and OKRs, measured on the same basis as internally delivered work.
  • Drive value realisation from supplier partnerships, tracking what was committed commercially and operationally against what has been delivered.
  • Identify opportunities to use partner capability more effectively, including where suppliers can accelerate delivery, reduce toil or provide capability GSK does not hold internally.
  • Support contract and partnership optimisation led by Procurement, providing the performance and value evidence needed for renewal, renegotiation and consolidation decisions.
  • Work with the Technology Performance Manager to assess end-to-end performance where delivery and service span internal teams and supplier-provided capability.
  • Escalate and resolve supplier performance issues, agreeing remediation plans and holding partners to them through to closure.
  • Maintain visibility of the strategic supplier landscape, including scope, spend, dependency and concentration risk, and coordinate supplier demand across the platform and product domains so that each partner meets one consistent GSK position instead of several.
  • Support Procurement and Legal in commercial and contractual negotiation, supplying the performance, value and risk evidence on which their position is built, and manage supplier risk, compliance and business continuity, including exit and transition arrangements.
  • Use AI and analytics to accelerate supplier performance analysis, spend transparency and review preparation.

Minimum Level of Job-Related Experience Required

  • Overall 15+ Years of exp, typically 8-10 years in strategic supplier or vendor management, commercial management, or technology sourcing and partner governance roles.
  • Experience owning senior relationships with major technology suppliers or managed service providers.
  • Experience running supplier governance cycles, including quarterly business reviews and executive review forums.
  • Proven ability to hold suppliers to contracted outcomes, SLAs and service commitments, including through formal remediation.
  • Experience providing the performance and value evidence used in renewal, renegotiation or consolidation decisions.
  • Experience supporting Procurement and Legal through commercial and contractual negotiation, and managing supplier risk, compliance and business continuity including exit and transition.
  • Familiarity with supplier performance analytics and AI-enabled tooling for spend and performance transparency.

Skills/Background

  • Strong commercial acumen, able to interpret contracts, spend and performance data and identify where value is being lost.
  • Strong relationship management and influencing skills, able to hold a firm position with a supplier while sustaining a productive long-term partnership.
  • Excellent communication skills, able to present supplier performance clearly to executive audiences on both sides of the relationship.
  • Ability to coordinate demand across multiple internal domains into a single consistent position.
  • Well organised, able to run concurrent governance cycles across several major suppliers.

#AGTech


Skills

Agile Methodology, Commercial Management, Cross-Functional Teamwork, Data Analysis, Design Thinking, DevOps, Partnership Management, Prioritization, Product Development Research, Product Roadmapping, Project Management, Return on Investment (ROI), Software Development, Strategic Support, Strategy Deployment, Technology Sourcing, User Experience (UX), User Interface (UI) Design, Vendor Management

Why GSK?

Uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together.

GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. We aim to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade, as a successful, growing company where people can thrive. We get ahead of disease by preventing and treating it with innovation in specialty medicines and vaccines. We focus on four therapeutic areas: respiratory, immunology and inflammation; oncology; HIV; and infectious diseases – to impact health at scale.

People and patients around the world count on the medicines and vaccines we make, so we’re committed to creating an environment where our people can thrive and focus on what matters most. Our culture of being ambitious for patients, accountable for impact and doing the right thing is the foundation for how, together, we deliver for patients, shareholders and our people.

Job Description:

Primary Purpose

The Research Software Engineer provides the technical foundation for two externally funded interdisciplinary research programs in the Wisdom and Culture Lab, Department of Psychology, one examining metacognition and reasoning in advanced artificial intelligence systems and one examining human-artificial intelligence collaboration in expert judgment and forecasting. The position translates scientific requirements into reliable, reproducible research software, enabling the research team to design and conduct large-scale computational and behavioural studies that would not otherwise be feasible, and to release research tools and code alongside publications. The role was created to establish dedicated research-engineering capacity for these two newly funded programs and to build and sustain the shared computational infrastructure on which both depend.

Key Accountabilities

Research software design and development

  • Designs, develops, and maintains research software supporting computational experiments involving contemporary language models
  • Translates experimental specifications from the Principal Investigator and postdoctoral fellows into functioning, testable systems
  • Implements research prototypes and tools that connect artificial intelligence systems with behavioural experiments and research interfaces
  • Selects appropriate languages, libraries, and frameworks for each research application
  • Tests and debugs research software to confirm that it behaves as the research design requires

Model integration and experimental infrastructure

  • Integrates commercial model application programming interfaces and open-weight language models into experimental pipelines
  • Builds reusable infrastructure for model evaluation, data collection, experimentation, and reproducibility
  • Supports model adaptation and computational experimentation as research questions require
  • Administers compute, storage, and cloud or cluster resources used by the research programs
  • Assesses emerging tools and methods in a rapidly changing artificial intelligence ecosystem and advises the research team on their adoption

Reliability, reproducibility, and research data stewardship

  • Monitors technical performance, diagnoses failures, and improves the reliability and scalability of research systems
  • Maintains version control practices and code review standards across the research codebase
  • Establishes and documents reproducible pipelines so that reported results can be regenerated
  • Applies data management, security, and privacy practices appropriate to research data, in accordance with University policy and approved research ethics protocols
  • Maintains technical records sufficient to support replication, audit, and the data-sharing requirements of funders and journals

Collaboration and technical consultation

  • Works with postdoctoral fellows, graduate students, and research assistants to convert research designs into working systems
  • Advises the research team on technical feasibility, effort, and trade-offs at the design stage of studies
  • Coordinates technical work with external collaborators
  • Provides technical guidance and informal training to trainees using the laboratory research infrastructure
  • Participates in research meetings and contributes a technical perspective to research planning

Documentation, dissemination, and other duties

  • Produces and maintains technical documentation for research software, pipelines, and datasets
  • Prepares code and materials for open-source release and for public repositories associated with publications
  • Contributes technical content to manuscripts, preregistrations, technical reports, and grant applications
  • Contributes technical information to reports for funders and research partners
  • Performs other duties in support of the research programs as assigned

Required Qualifications

Education

  • University degree in computer science, software engineering, machine learning, data science, computational cognitive science, or a related field
  • An equivalent combination of education and demonstrated experience building research-quality software systems will be considered
  • A graduate degree in a related discipline is an asset but is not required

Experience

  • Demonstrated experience programming with contemporary large language models, through commercial application programming interfaces and/or open-weight models
  • Experience developing reproducible experimental, evaluation, or data-processing pipelines
  • Experience working in a shared codebase using version control and code review
  • Experience with cloud computing, databases, web applications or research interfaces, experimental platforms, evaluation infrastructure, or model adaptation and post-training is preferred
  • Experience supporting behavioural or human-participant research is an asset

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

  • Advanced Python programming skills; additional languages relevant to research computing are an asset
  • Working knowledge of machine learning tooling and contemporary artificial intelligence research workflows
  • Ability to write maintainable, documented software that other researchers can extend
  • Analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to diagnose failures in unfamiliar systems and third-party services
  • Ability to explain technical constraints and options to collaborators who do not have a software background
  • Ability to organize and prioritize concurrent technical requests arising from two research programs
  • Ability to work with limited supervision in a research environment in which requirements evolve
  • Commitment to research integrity, reproducibility, and appropriate handling of confidential research data

Equity Statement

The University of Waterloo acknowledges that much of our work takes place on the traditional territory of the Neutral, Anishinaabeg, and Haudenosaunee peoples. Our main campus is situated on the Haldimand Tract, the land granted to the Six Nations that includes six miles on each side of the Grand River. Our active work toward reconciliation takes place across our campuses through research, learning, teaching, and community building, and is coordinated within the Office of Indigenous Relations.

The University values the diverse and intersectional identities of its students, faculty, and staff. The University regards equity and diversity as an integral part of academic excellence and is committed to accessibility for all employees. The University of Waterloo seeks applicants who embrace our values of equity, anti-racism and inclusion. As such, we encourage applications from candidates who have been historically disadvantaged and marginalized, including applicants who identify as First Nations, Métis and/or Inuk (Inuit), Black, racialized, a person with a disability, women and/or 2SLGBTQ+.

Positions are open to qualified candidates who are legally entitled to work in Canada.

title: Sr Engineering Manager
location: North Haven, Connecticut, United States of America
description:
We anticipate the application window for this opening will close on - 31 Dec 2026


Careers that change lives start here. Medtronic is a global leader in healthcare technology with a Mission to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life. Our 95,000 employees work across more than 150 countries to put patients first — developing innovative medical technologies that improve the lives of 72+ million patients each year. Your unique talents will help shape the future of healthcare while building a career grounded in purpose, growth, and impact.

A Day in the Life

Medtronic, a global leader in medical technology, services, and solutions, is seeking an accomplished and experienced Quality Engineering Manager to join our innovative team at the North Haven, CT site. This position will oversee the surgical operating unit’s new product development quality team. A primary responsibility within this role is people management, which includes mentoring, developing, and coaching staff to meet or exceed performance expectations and program commitments. The role also involves providing strategic leadership to prioritize departmental initiatives, setting performance goals and targets, conducting performance reviews, and holding one-on-one meetings to support performance management and employee development aligned with departmental objectives.

The preferred candidate will possess extensive leadership experience in Quality New Product Development, including expertise in reliability science, reliability planning and testing, hardware/software risk management, design controls, and regulatory compliance within the medical device industry. The successful applicant must demonstrate strong teamwork abilities, initiative, curiosity, and the capacity for rapid learning. This position is integral to the medical device development process, ensuring patient safety throughout the entire product lifecycle.

Job Description field

Primary Responsibilities

  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of engineering professionals, including performance management, career development, promotion recommendations, and compensation planning.
  • Guide project-level decisions by gathering technical input, evaluating risk, and resolving disagreements between Quality, Research and Development, and other cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Drive quality improvement initiatives and establish consistent risk management and reliability practices across supported programs.
  • Direct and guide employees in the design and development of medical device products or software systems.
  • Develops and improves objectives, policies, processes, and standards to support strategy and drive functional excellence through best practices.
  • Continuously assesses team member deliverables and documentation quality across all phases of product development.
  • Selects, hires, and develops personnel, aligning talent to programs to support efficient operations of the function
  • Collaborates across functions and businesses while balancing divergent objectives to gain cooperation of other parties
  • Management of departmental budget
  • Builds strong cross-functional partnerships and leads the team in developing and maintaining risk management files, including risk management plans and reports, while ensuring regular and effective risk reviews.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree and 7+ years of relevant experience, including 5+ years of managerial experience, OR an advanced degree and 5+ years of relevant experience, including 5+ years of managerial experience.
  • Experience leading and developing technical professionals, including performance management, career development, and resource allocation.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in product risk management, reliability engineering, or quality engineering.
  • Experience working within the medical device industry or another highly regulated industry, such as aerospace.
  • Experience leading cross-functional technical decisions involving Engineering, Quality, or product development stakeholders.
  • Experience supporting New Product Development within the medical device industry.
  • Experience applying product risk management practices throughout the design and development lifecycle.
  • Experience leading reliability engineering activities for complex products or systems.
  • Experience resolving technical or quality disagreements across Research and Development and Quality teams.
  • Experience developing and executing organizational strategy or quality improvement initiatives.
  • Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Six Sigma/DRM Green Belt or equivalent certification, AAMI design control certification is preferred

For Baccalaureate degrees earned outside of the United States, a degree that satisfies the requirements of 8 C.F.R. § 214.2(h)(4)(iii)(A) is required.

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. For Office Roles: While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to be independently mobile. The employee is also required to interact with a computer, and communicate with peers and co-workers. In alignment with our enterprise-wide workforce planning approach, U.S. work authorization sponsorship (H-1B, TN, J, etc.) is offered exclusively for Principal-level roles and above, where specialized expertise aligns with long-term business needs. title: Investigator
description:
Job Description:

Building trusted markets — powered by our people.


At Cboe Global Markets, we inspire our people to solve complex challenges together because what we do matters. We provide the financial infrastructure that powers the global economy. As a leading provider of market infrastructure and tradable products, Cboe delivers cutting-edge trading, clearing and investment solutions to market participants around the world.

We’re building inclusive ways to support professional and personal development while strengthening the trust we’ve earned as a global market leader. Our teams are empowered to share ideas, actively pursue them and bring on a challenge. As champions of internal mobility and access to opportunity, we encourage our people to “go for it” and equip our managers with the training to coach their teams to the next level. Our Associate Resource Groups champion diversity, equity and inclusion, giving employees a safe space to network, share ideas and create opportunities.

Sound like the place for you? Join us!

Our Team:

The Cboe Regulatory Division is responsible for the oversight of the markets for which it has regulatory responsibility and market participants. The Division endeavors to achieve this goal through effective and efficient surveillance, examination, and investigative programs aimed at detecting and disciplining or preventing violative or otherwise inappropriate behavior.


The Division is actively seeking a highly motivated individual to join our options investigations team and perform investigative activities to assist in determinations regarding possible violations of Cboe, Cboe C2, Cboe BZX, and Cboe EDGX Options Exchange (collectively, the “Exchanges”) Rules and other applicable rules and regulations governing Exchange Members and Trading Permit Holders (“TPH”).


Location Overview

Cboe HQ is located in the historic Old Post Office district, it’s a landmark that blends classic architecture with modern amenities. The building features expansive spaces with high ceilings and large windows, offering an abundance of natural light and panoramic views of the city skyline and the Chicago River.

With its prime location in the heart of downtown, the OPO Building provides easy access to major transportation hubs, including Union Station and multiple CTA lines, making it convenient for commuters. The building is home to a variety of amenities, including restaurants, a fitness center, and collaborative workspaces, creating a vibrant and dynamic work environment in one of Chicago's most iconic areas.


PLEASE NOTE: To support strong partnership and team connection, this role follows a four day in office work model.


What You’ll Do:

Options Investigators in the Division are responsible for conducting focused investigations of trading activities on the Exchanges to detect possible violations of Exchange Rules, By-Laws, and interpretations and policies, and the SEC rules and regulations thereunder, or other improper activities.

In this role, you can expect to:

  • Independently manage investigations from inception to conclusion and completing investigation steps in a timely manner that meet expected guidelines
  • Build and maintain a thorough understanding of the Exchanges trading and regulatory environments, as well as the broader securities industry, in areas such as markets, products, relevant rules and regulations, technologies and systems, processes and operational methodologies, and investigative techniques, while contributing to the creation of new investigative processes that address potential regulatory concerns
  • Evaluate and analyze matters to identify potential violations as well as the types of evidence, including data and information, necessary to determine whether the activity in question was violative or otherwise improper via thorough research, collection of evidence and fact-finding
  • Evaluate and analyze evidence to conclude sufficiency with respect to suspected violations through case law and/or precedent to determine whether non-disciplinary or disciplinary actions are warranted. Recommend appropriate disposition to management for review.
  • Prepare investigative reports detailing findings in a clear, cohesive manner supported by factual evidence and analysis. Utilize Division guidelines for style and form; present work that is complete and requires minimal revisions.
  • Assist in taking on-the-record testimonies, as required
  • Present case information to management and Enforcement committees, including formal disciplinary proceedings
  • Professionally interact with internal regulatory staff and external contacts, such as Members, other Self-Regulatory Organizations, and the SEC
  • Collaborate and communicate with cross-functional teams, particularly the Options Surveillance and Enforcement team to enhance or create solutions
  • Actively participate in team projects, discussions and problem solving
  • Actively participate in training/continuing education opportunities and meetings

What You’ll Need:

  • Bachelor's Degree
  • Two years of Industry experience preferred
  • Strong affinity with financial markets
  • Highly self-motivated and driven
  • Excellent communication and teamwork skills
  • Exceptional written, analytical, and research skills
  • Strong organizational and planning skills
  • Must be proficient in MS-Office suite, including Excel
  • Experience in a regulatory, compliance, and/or legal environment is preferred

Benefits and Perks of working for Cboe Global Markets

We value the total wellbeing of our people – including health, financial, personal and social wellness. We believe standard benefits like health insurance and fair pay are a given at any organization. Still, you should know we offer:

  • Fair and competitive salary and incentive compensation packages with an upside for overachievement
  • Generous paid time off, including vacation, personal days, sick days and annual community service days
  • Health, dental and vision benefits, including access to telemedicine and mental health services
  • 2:1 401(k) match, up to 8% match immediately upon hire
  • Discounted Employee Stock Purchase Plan
  • Tax Savings Accounts for health, dependent and transportation
  • Employee referral bonus program
  • Volunteer opportunities to help you give back to your communities

Some of our associates’ favorite benefits and perks include:

  • Complimentary lunch, snacks and coffee in any Cboe office
  • Paid Tuition assistance and education opportunities
  • Generous charitable giving company match
  • Paid parental leave and fertility benefits
  • On-site gyms and discounts to other fitness centers
  • Paid Time Off

We’re reimagining the future of the workplace by focusing on what matters most, our people. Our journey is an inclusive one. We’re investing deeply in leadership programs and career development initiatives that ensure everyone has an equal chance to succeed.


We work with purpose, solving problems with ingenuity, collaboration, and a lot of passion. We’re an engaged and excited team connecting markets across borders and embracing growth in all its forms to achieve incredible outcomes.

title: Associate Director, Service Ops Lead - Talent and L&D
description:
About the Team:

Enterprise Systems is the backbone of GSK’s internal operations in Digital & Tech, enabling GSK Global Functions teams such as Finance, Procurement, HR, Legal, Compliance, WREF, CGA and Corporate Secretariat to run seamlessly. This team designs and delivers cutting-edge digital platforms that power critical processes, ensuring efficiency, compliance, and scalability across the enterprise.

Our HR Digital & Tech team transforms how GSK attracts, develops, and retains talent through innovative technology solutions. From managing global HR platforms to delivering data-driven insights, this function ensures our people have the tools and experiences they need to thrive. Partnering closely with HR business teams, we create solutions that simplify processes, enhance employee engagement, and enable strategic workforce planning. If you’re passionate about technology that empowers people, this is where you can make an impact.

Job Purpose:

The Associate Director, Service Operations Lead – Talent & L&D is responsible for ensuring the stable, compliant, and reliable operation of select systems and platforms within the HR Digital & Tech domain. The role oversees day-to-day platform operations and ensures that processes are followed, risks are managed, and changes are delivered safely. It maintains the operational performance of multiple platforms (e.g. SuccessFactors), ensuring they meet agreed service levels and adhere to security and compliance expectations. The role also provides leadership across operational service teams and partner-delivered support services, ensuring effective service delivery, proactive issue management, continuous improvement, and strong coordination across business, technology, security, infrastructure, product, and vendor teams.

This role operates under GSK's "Performance with Choice" hybrid working approach, typically expecting 2–3 days per week in the office, with the specific pattern agreed between the successful candidate and their manager based on role and team needs.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Provide operational leadership across Talent & Data platforms, ensuring system stability, availability, and adherence to service levels, acting as the primary internal escalation point for product and domain teams on service performance and major incidents.
  • Govern incident, problem, change, configuration, and release processes for domain platforms, ensuring operational compliance with ITSM policies and control frameworks, and defining measurable outcomes for problem management (e.g., RCA closure time, recurrence prevention, defect trend reduction).
  • Define and maintain service readiness and runbook quality standards (e.g. ServiceNow Knowledge), ensuring escalation paths, support tasks, data handling, continuity steps, and deployment impacts are captured and validated before go-live.
  • Create and oversee service plans for new and enhanced products, coordinating with Product Owners, third-party partners, and platform/service teams to define SLAs, performance expectations, and support handover criteria.
  • Monitor platform performance, proactively identifying risks, trends, and recurring issues, and implement improvement actions to strengthen stability and user experience.
  • Coordinate with Platform Owners, engineering squads, solution architects, and service teams to ensure changes, integrations, upgrades, and releases are deployed safely and meet operational readiness standards.
  • Lead operational readiness assessments, ensuring documentation, support models, monitoring coverage, and non-functional controls are in place prior to deployment.
  • Own operational dashboards, KPIs, and reporting for the platforms, ensuring performance, risks, and issues are communicated to senior stakeholders.
  • Oversee root cause analysis for major incidents, ensuring sustainable fixes, clear remediation actions, and preventative measures are identified and delivered.
  • Maintain and continuously improve operational documentation, including runbooks, support procedures, configuration inventories, and architectural operational views.
  • Manage relationships with third-party vendors and managed service providers to ensure high-quality operational support and fulfilment of contractual obligations.
  • Lead, mentor, and coordinate operational support teams and partner resources across areas such as service desk, platform support, infrastructure, cloud services, and application operations, ensuring clear accountability, timely delivery, and effective escalation management.
  • Collaborate with security, risk, compliance, infrastructure, product, and engineering teams to ensure access controls, data handling, cyber security requirements, operational controls, and compliance standards are embedded into day-to-day service operations.
  • Where required, support extended operational coverage, escalation, or on-call arrangements for critical incidents, major releases, or high-priority business events.
  • Lead your team in using approved AI tools to improve productivity and ways of working, role-modelling responsible use and follow GSK’s Responsible AI, privacy and security requirements.

Required Skills & Qualification:

  • 15–19 years of experience in platform operations, system administration, IT service management, or technical delivery within complex enterprise environments, ideally supporting SuccessFactors, Degreed, or similar HR/L&D platforms.
  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Systems Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • Strong knowledge of platform operations, ITSM, cloud technologies, system integrations, monitoring, security, compliance, resilience, and business continuity.

description:
Grounds & Maintenance Officer (Grade 3 ESO)
Full-Time | Permanent | 37.5 hours per week
St Augustine's Parish School, Salisbury
The Opportunity
Looking for a hands-on role where no two days are quite the same and you can see the difference your work makes?
St Augustine's Parish School is seeking a full-time Grounds & Maintenance Officer (Grade 3 ESO) to support the ongoing care and maintenance of our school grounds, buildings and facilities.
From maintaining gardens and outdoor spaces to completing general repairs, identifying maintenance needs and supporting projects across the school, this is a varied and practical role within a welcoming school community.

Maintain school grounds, gardens, lawns and outdoor areas.
Undertake general repairs and routine maintenance of buildings, equipment and facilities.

We're looking for someone who is practical, dependable and proactive, with a willingness to pitch in wherever needed.

Previous experience in grounds, gardening, property maintenance, facilities or a related field.
A broad range of practical maintenance skills.
Good organisational and time-management skills.
An understanding of safe work practices.
The ability to work independently and use initiative.
Good communication skills and a positive, team-focused approach.

title: Executive Leader, AI Workforce Intelligence
description:
Job Description Summary

GE Aerospace is developing a forward-looking AI workforce strategy ensuring the organization is prepared for how work, roles, and skills will evolve in the age of artificial intelligence. With a passion for amplifying what our people do best, unlocking new and higher-value work, and growing the human capabilities that will define the next era of aerospace, GE has created the AI workforce strategy function sitting at the intersection of the CHRO and the Chief Data & AI Officer.

Reporting to the Head of AI Workforce Strategy & Capability, the Executive Leader of AI Workforce Intelligence is responsible for the design, build and delivery of the enterprise workforce inference data that will unlock both the AI workforce strategy and AI capability building (including AI job profile inferences, skills to job inference, skills to people inference, AI fluency inference form AI tool usage/quality of use). This leader will also drive the AI workforce strategy agent architecture – leading the team to build, train, and maintain utility agents, super agents, and orchestration layer which activate the data foundation across agentic monitoring, interpretation and synthesis (internal skills and job trends, external skills and job trends, talent supply, AI projection, AI workforce strategy, AI fluency, SWP supplementation).

Job Description

Leads the establishing of AI workforce intelligence

  • Establish the job and work AI inference foundation at the task level, connected to skills, and overlay the interaction of AI on those skills and tasks
  • Establish the employee capability AI inference foundation, connecting employee profiles with skills, and overlaying the interaction of AI on those skills
  • Architect the capability constellation to create a connected view of jobs, skills, AI projections, and workforce capability to inform effective employee capability growth and meaningful investments in employee development
  • Integrate multi-source indicators of AI fluency hyper personalized to the job and work AI inference foundation
  • Set the enterprise standard for workforce inference, establish the validation approaches, confidence thresholds for the enterprise

Lead the design and implementation of the AI workforce strategy agent architecture

  • Design, train and maintain the utility agents, super agents and orchestration layer spanning internal and external skills and job trends, talent supply, AI projection, AI workforce strategy, AI fluency and workforce-planning supplementation

Enablement of talent strategy

  • Partner with stakeholders representing Future of Work and Capability Building to optimize projections and the utility of the intelligence layer and agents
  • Partner with Talent COE teams to integrate skills into talent systems, career architecture, and internal mobility programs
  • Own the standards, governance model, and operating routines that keep skills data current, usable, and aligned across the talent ecosystem. The role partners closely with People Analytics, HR Technology, and Talent COE leaders to ensure skills are consistently defined, governed, and applied across key talent processes

Preferred work location is Evendale, OH, however, remote employment will also be considered. Ability and willingness to travel at least 25%.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in human resources, organizational psychology, talent development, education, business, technology or a related discipline.
  • 12+ years of experience in HR (e.g., people analytics, talent COEs, workforce strategy, HR technology), business intelligence/analytics, or related fields
  • Experience designing data architecture and enabling intelligence infrastructure
  • Experience with skills taxonomies, skills-based talent models, job architecture, data governance, or adjacent domains
  • Proven ability to translate strategy into practical operating models, governance routines, and implementation plans
  • Strong program and project management capability, including driving cross functional initiatives in complex, matrixed environments
  • Experience working cross-functionally across HR, technology and business leadership to deliver enterprise solutions
  • Strong ability to forge new territories where best practice and playbooks do not exist, and problem solve/solution
  • Ability to develop credible influence as a collaborator with stakeholders
  • Strong executive communicator with experience in moving from data to storytelling
  • Strong systems thinker with the ability to connect underlying strategy, underlying technology and anticipate downstream needs or issues

Preferred

  • Advanced degree in Human Resources, Organizational Development, Business, Industrial/Organizational Psychology, Strategy, or a related field
  • Working knowledge of AI inference and talent intelligence
  • Working knowledge of AI agents and how to apply agentic capabilities to data monitoring, interpretation, and synthesis
  • Experience building or scaling organizational design, organizational effectiveness, strategic workforce planning, or workforce transformation capabilities at enterprise scale
  • Experience operating in complex, matrixed, regulated, or global organizations
  • Experience applying talent intelligence and data based decision-making
  • Deep expertise with measurement strategies, ROI and demonstrating impact.
  • Demonstrated ability to facilitate senior-level decision making, synthesize complex inputs, and build executive-ready narratives that clarify choices, risks, and tradeoffs
  • Knowledge of future-of-work trends, workforce transformation, operating model evolution, skills-based workforce practices, location strategy, and automation or AI enabled workforce implications
  • Strong consulting orientation, systems thinking, business acumen, financial orientation, and ability to simplify complexity for different audiences
  • Demonstrated change leadership experience, including helping leaders build adoption plans for new structures, operating models, workforce strategies, or ways of working

The base pay range for this position is 200,000 - 300,000 annually. The specific pay offered may be influenced by a variety of factors, including the candidate’s experience, education, and skill set. title: Texture Artist Mid/Senior - London
description:
Crafty Apes is a high-end global visual effects company specialising in photoreal VFX. Established in 2011, Crafty Apes operates offices in Canada, the UK, the US, and Australia with employees working remotely across the globe. Our mission is to bring our clients’ visions to life through exceptional visual effects for film, episodic content, and commercials. Let’s just say: we deliver great shots while having fun!
We are seeking a talented and detail-oriented Texture Artist/Look Dev to join our team. This is an exciting opportunity for a Mid to Senior level artist to contribute to our visual effects pipeline, creating high-quality, photo-realistic surface textures that meet the technical and aesthetic standards of our high-end projects.
The Texture Artist /Look Dev will be responsible for creating detailed texture maps for a variety of assets, from characters and complex props to large-scale environments. You will work closely with Art Directors, VFX Supervisors, and the Look Development team to ensure textures are painted, managed, and integrated seamlessly into our production pipeline.
What you would do

Create high-quality, photo-realistic texture maps (diffuse, specular, bump, displacement, etc.) for characters, props, and environments.

Utilise reference photography and digital painting techniques to achieve high levels of surface detail and realism.

Collaborate closely with the Modeler and Look Development departments to ensure UVs are optimised and shaders are set up to showcase your textures effectively.

Actively participate in the review process, taking feedback from Supervisors and Art Directors to iterate on asset quality and realism.

Troubleshoot texture and shading issues, providing creative and technical solutions to production challenges.

Maintain organised project files and naming conventions, adhering to the studio’s pipeline standards.

What you need

3+ years (Mid) 5+ years (Senior) of professional experience as a Texture Artist/Look Dev in a VFX, feature film, or high-end episodic production environment.

Expert proficiency in industry-standard texturing software (e.g., Substance Painter/Designer, Mari, Adobe Photoshop).

A strong understanding of PBR (Physically Based Rendering) workflows and material properties.

Strong artistic eye for colour, detail, surface properties, and weathering.

Excellent communication skills and the ability to work effectively within a collaborative, fast-paced team environment.

How to Apply
If you are a talented Texture Artist looking for a challenging and rewarding opportunity, we want to hear from you.

Please submit your CV/Reel, detailed filmography/project list, and a brief cover letter outlining your relevant experience and career aspirations.

Crafty Apes Australia is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, or disability status.

title: Research Scientist, Atlas Behavior Learning
description:
Are you passionate about using machine learning to drive robot behavior? Curious what you’d be able to accomplish with total access to Boston Dynamics robots? As a Research Scientist on the Atlas Behavior Learning team, you will join a world-class team of engineers and scientists focused on creating groundbreaking mobile manipulation behaviors for humanoids.


We are investing in reinforcement learning (RL) and behavioral cloning (BC) as a key technology for achieving dexterous and robust whole-body manipulation that can be deployed in real-world environments.


In this role, you will be responsible for:

  • Design, train, and deploy state of the art robot learning algorithms to tackle mobile &cz bimanual manipulation tasks
  • Contribute to foundation models shaping the future of humanoid robotics
  • Train control policies using RL to solve dexterous manipulation tasks
  • Distil many different policies using BC and RL with pixel observations
  • Deploying and debugging learned policies on Atlas


We are looking for:

  • MS with 3 years of industry experience or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Robotics, or a related field
  • Extensive Experience training and deploying RL policies for complex behaviors on real robots or simulated characters
  • Excitement for integrating, running, and evaluating their learned policies on the robot
  • Has in-depth knowledge about domain randomization to bridge the sim-2-real gap
  • Strong foundation in Python and modern ML frameworks (e.g., PyTorch and Jax)
  • Experience in algorithm design, debugging, and performance optimization

The ideal candidate has:

  • A PhD or equivalent research experience in reinforcement learning or robotic manipulation
  • Publications at top tier venues including RSS, CoRL, Science Robotics, ICLR, NeuRIPS
  • Familiarity with behavior cloning and has trained a diffusion policy from images
  • Prior experience with student-teacher training workflows

Why join us?

  • Direct access to cutting-edge robots and the infrastructure to run large-scale experiments
  • A collaborative, mission-driven team where your ideas have real impact
  • The chance to help define what’s possible in real-world robotics



The base pay range for this position is between $170,000 to $220,000 annually. Base pay will depend on multiple individualized factors including, but not limited to internal equity, job related knowledge, skills and experience. This range represents a good faith estimate of compensation at the time of posting. Boston Dynamics offers a generous Benefits package including medical, dental vision, 401(k), paid time off and an annual bonus structure. Additional details regarding these benefit plans will be provided if an employee receives an offer for employment.

title: Research Project Manager
description:
At the University of Waterloo, we create and promote a culture where everyone can reach their full potential. As an employee, you get support & opportunities that empower you to advance your career. Explore how we can bring big ideas to life, together. The University is a welcoming workplace for those of all abilities, interests, and expertise. The internal posting deadline for this position is November 26, 2026 at 11:59PM
This position is being offered as a Secondment or contract opportunity.


Term - 2 years

Job Description:

Primary Purpose

The Research Project Manager oversees two externally funded interdisciplinary research programs in the Wisdom and Culture Lab, Department of Psychology. One program studies metacognition and reasoning in advanced AI systems, while the other examines human-AI collaboration in expert judgment and forecasting. The role manages timelines, deliverables, research ethics, participant recruitment, documentation, budgets, research assistant coordination, and partner relationships across both programs. It was created due to the parallel computational and behavioral research streams, multiple institutions, external partners, trainees, and overlapping timelines that require dedicated management.

Key Accountabilities

Project coordination and planning

• Maintains integrated timelines, milestones, and deliverables across both research programs

• Prepares and runs project meetings, records decisions and action items, and follows issues through to resolution

• Anticipates bottlenecks, identifies risks to timelines, and brings forward practical options for resolution

• Coordinates the Principal Investigator, postdoctoral fellows, technical personnel, trainees, and external collaborators against shared deadlines

• Tracks reporting obligations and deliverables owed to funders and research partners

Research operations and compliance

• Coordinates research ethics submissions, amendments, and renewals with the Office of Research Ethics

• Coordinates study launches, participant recruitment, data collection schedules, and participant panel arrangements

• Maintains organized research documentation, including preregistrations, protocols, codebooks, repositories, and datasets

• Monitors adherence to approved protocols, data management plans, and University policy governing research data

• Maintains records required for audit, funder reporting, and data-sharing obligations

Research personnel coordination and training

• Coordinates recruitment, hiring processes, and onboarding for research assistants and co-operative education students with the Principal Investigator and departmental administration

• Assigns and schedules research assistant work, monitors progress, and provides feedback on assigned research tasks

• Trains research assistants on study procedures, documentation standards, and research integrity requirements

• Balances trainee workload and scheduling across concurrent studies and both research programs

• Supports the onboarding of new postdoctoral fellows and technical personnel

Financial and resource administration

• Tracks project expenditures, participant payments, research services, and technical expenses against approved budgets

• Prepares purchase requisitions, reimbursements, and payment documentation and reconciles accounts with departmental and Office of Research staff

• Coordinates procurement of research services, software, computing resources, and participant panels in accordance with University purchasing policy

• Monitors spending across multiple funding sources and reports variances to the Principal Investigator

• Contributes budget and resource information to grant applications and funder reports

Communication, partnerships, and dissemination

• Serves as day-to-day point of contact for external collaborators and research partners, including Defence Research and Development Canada and collaborating institutions

• Coordinates workshops, project meetings, and visits by external partners

• Maintains project documentation and digital presence, including project pages and public repositories

• Supports preparation of manuscripts, technical reports, presentations, and dissemination materials

• Performs other duties in support of the research programs as assigned

*All employees of the University are expected to follow University and departmental health and safety policy, procedures and work practices at all times. Employees are also responsible for the completion of all health and safety training, as assigned. Employees with staff supervision and/or management responsibilities will ensure that assigned staff abide by the above, and actively identify, assess and correct health and safety hazards, as required.

Required Qualifications

Education

• Bachelor's degree in psychology, cognitive science, behavioural science, computer or data science, human-computer interaction, or a related field

• An equivalent combination of education and relevant project-management experience will be considered

• A master's degree in a relevant discipline, or a recognized project management credential, is an asset

Experience

• Demonstrated experience managing several concurrent workstreams and competing deadlines

• Experience preparing or coordinating research ethics submissions

• Experience with participant recruitment, online data collection, and research documentation practices

• Experience coordinating or supervising research assistants or student staff

• Experience tracking research budgets and expenditures is preferred

• Experience working with external research partners or multi-site collaborations is an asset

• Familiarity with University of Waterloo policies and administrative procedures is an asset

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

• Exceptional organizational skills, follow-through, and attention to detail

• Ability to identify problems, propose practical solutions, and act with limited supervision

• Excellent written and verbal communication and documentation skills

• Strong interpersonal judgment when coordinating people with differing expertise, working styles, and priorities

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office and collaborative project-tracking tools

• Working knowledge of research platforms such as Qualtrics, the Open Science Framework, and GitHub is preferred; familiarity with R or Python is an asset

• Ability to maintain confidentiality of research data and personnel information

• Ability to work effectively in a technically sophisticated, rapidly changing research environment


Equity Statement

The University of Waterloo acknowledges that much of our work takes place on the traditional territory of the Neutral, Anishinaabeg, and Haudenosaunee peoples. Our main campus is situated on the Haldimand Tract, the land granted to the Six Nations that includes six miles on each side of the Grand River. Our active work toward reconciliation takes place across our campuses through research, learning, teaching, and community building, and is coordinated within the Office of Indigenous Relations.

The University values the diverse and intersectional identities of its students, faculty, and staff. The University regards equity and diversity as an integral part of academic excellence and is committed to accessibility for all employees. The University of Waterloo seeks applicants who embrace our values of equity, anti-racism and inclusion. As such, we encourage applications from candidates who have been historically disadvantaged and marginalized, including applicants who identify as First Nations, Métis and/or Inuk (Inuit), Black, racialized, a person with a disability, women and/or 2SLGBTQ+.

Positions are open to qualified candidates who are legally entitled to work in Canada.
