title: Lead Eligibility Technician
description:
About Our Job



Lead Eligibility Technician


With competitive pay, great benefits, and endless opportunities, working for the City and County of Denver means seeing yourself working with purpose — for you, and those who benefit from your passion, skills and expertise. Join our diverse, inclusive and talented workforce of more than 11,000 team members who are at the heart of what makes Denver, Denver.


What We Offer

The City and County of Denver offers competitive pay commensurate with education and experience. New hires are typically brought into the organization between $25.30 and $31.63. We also offer generous benefits for full-time employees which include but are not limited to:

  • A guaranteed life-long monthly pension, once vested after 5 years of service
  • 457B Retirement Plan
  • 140 hours of PTO earned within first year + 12 paid holidays, 1 personal holiday, 1 Wellness Day and 1 volunteer day per year
  • Competitive medical, dental and vision plans effective within 1 month of start date

Location & Schedule

The City and County of Denver supports a hybrid workplace model. Employees work where needed, at a job site several days a week and off-site as needed. This position reports to our office A.P. Taylor at 4685 Peoria St in Denver three days a week and telecommutes remotely at a designated workplace within the State of Colorado the remaining days.


Who We Are & What You’ll Do

At Denver Human Services (DHS), we envision a healthy community where people are connected, supported, safe, and well. One in three people in Denver turn to DHS for support at all stages of life. Our employees help children, at-risk adults, families, and individuals navigate social and economic pressures by connecting them to services and experts who support their overall well-being.


The Family and Adult Assistance Division (FAAD) is hiring for an Eligibility Technician Lead who is driven and passionate with a leadership mindset. The Lead Eligibility Technician will encourage, motivate, support and assist various Eligibility Specialists and Technicians in accomplishing division processing and accuracy goals.


Specifically, as a Lead Eligibility Technician you will:

  • Provide coverage for the supervisor as needed
  • Assist with maintaining daily operational standards
  • Be adaptable and flexible with your work schedule
  • Support Eligibility Specialists and technicians on their team and maintain a thorough and updated knowledge of all public assistance programs, including CBMS, SNAP, Medical Assistance, Adult Financial and/or Colorado Works programs
  • Interpret and explain rules and regulations to staff and help manage team workloads and troubleshooting
  • Provide on-the-job training, mentor employees, and collaborate with the training unit on course content, materials, and claims review
  • Contribute to the development of the performance enhancement plan, document performance, provide performance feedback, and furnish information for the formal performance evaluation
  • Assist Eligibility specialists and technicians with processing and determinations of difficult and/or complex cases and act as an arbitrator when problems occur between applicants/clients and employees
  • Assign and distribute work, review work for accuracy and completeness, and return assignments with recommendations for proper completion. Resolve problems encountered during daily operations and determine appropriate solutions
  • Monitor work activity on caseloads to ensure that cases are clearly and thoroughly documented
  • Review, and analyze case records and reports for completeness and accuracy, identify compliance and production problems, recommend and implement process improvements

What You’ll Bring

We value diversity of ethnicity, race, socioeconomic status, sexual identity, gender, religion, language, ability, and experience and exemplify this through the makeup of our team at all levels. You'll be right at home here if you cultivate strong relationships and push yourself, your work, the people around you and Denver to the next level.


Our ideal candidate has some or all the following experience, skills, and characteristics:

  • Extensive Professional experience determining eligibility for Cash Assistance, Adult Financial and/or Colorado Works programs and willing to learn.
  • Strong leadership skills with a commitment to working with intention and sensitivity amongst a diverse demographic of coworkers and clientele
  • Experience demonstrating adaptability as business needs evolve
  • Proven professional experience utilizing Colorado Benefits Management System (CBMS)
  • Proven success in working in a fast-paced and evolving work environment, adhering to quick turnaround times, and executing accurate follow-up and follow-through
  • Dedication to developing and maintaining positive working relationships while encouraging cooperation, pride and commitment to teamwork

Required Minimum Qualifications

Education requirement: Graduation from high school or the possession of a GED, HiSET or TASC Certificate.

Experience Requirement: Three (3) years of experience determining eligibility for a variety of public assistance programs.

Education/Experience Equivalency: Additional appropriate education may be substituted for the minimum experience requirement.

title: Associate Director, Product Owner - SAP HR S4, Strada and Mercans Payroll
description:
Job Purpose:


  • The Associate Director, Product Owner - SAP HR S4, Strada and Mercans Payroll is responsible for maximising the value of their HR Product portfolio by translating business needs into a prioritised backlog and leading delivery across the HR product lifecycle, within strategic and financial guardrails set by the Senior Director, People Services & Reward, and VP HR Digital & Tech. They work closely with business stakeholders to define outcomes and ensure delivered functionality is usable, secure, compliant, supportable, and aligned to product strategy. The SAP HR S4 Payroll Product Owner guides delivery and operational support teams to ensure requirements are clear, value-driven, and data-informed, while overseeing iterative delivery that improves product performance, adoption, and operational effectiveness.

  • This role operates under GSK's "Performance with Choice" hybrid working approach, typically expecting 2–3 days per week in the office, with the specific pattern agreed between the successful candidate and their manager based on role and team needs.

Responsibilities:

  • Serve as the functional and technical SME for SAP HR S4 Payroll, offering expert guidance on configuration, statutory compliance, and best practice.
  • Partner with business stakeholders to understand functional needs, refine requirements, and define product outcomes that support business priorities, within guardrails set by the Senior Director, People Services & Reward, and VP HR Digital & Tech.
  • Serve as the escalation point for HR Product teams and business users on functional product issues, guiding decisions within agreed financial, risk, and architectural guardrails set by the Director, Workday, Payroll & Time Product Manager and VP, HR Digital & Tech.
  • Own and manage the Product backlog (e.g. Jira, ADO etc), ensuring requirements (e.g., epics, features, user stories) are well-defined and supported by minimum data inputs (e.g., cost drivers, user volumes, risk/sensitivity, process impact, dependencies).
  • Make prioritisation decisions for the Product backlog based on value, cost, risk, business continuity, and resource capacity, escalating only where strategic trade-offs are required by the Senior Director, People Services & Reward, and VP HR Digital & Tec.
  • Lead the Product team’s delivery activities, guiding Engineers, Architects, and Testers to ensure solutions are fit-for-purpose, secure, compliant, supportable, and aligned to architectural standards.
  • Drive operational readiness by applying a delivery readiness checklist covering support model requirements, training needs, continuity planning, configuration/runbook documentation, release notes, and user onboarding.
  • Define and maintain the Product performance dashboard, tracking adoption, cycle time/throughput, stability/defects, UX signals (e.g., CSAT, SUS, completion rates), and support effort; use performance insights to drive continuous improvement.
  • Ensure product changes follow required security controls, risk assessments, data handling policies, and regulated change processes, obtaining approvals from relevant SMEs where required.
  • Support Solution Architects to assess design options and manage cross-Product dependencies, contract/interface impacts, and sequencing needs to support interoperability and consistent business outcomes.
  • Contribute to the improvement of delivery practices within the Product, promoting agile (i.e. SaFe, Scrum etc), iterative, value-driven, and data-led ways of working, including meaningful measurement of benefits and operational impact.

Required skills:


  • 15 to 19 years of experience working in product delivery, digital solutions, business systems, or process-led technology roles.
  • In-depth knowledge of SAP payroll software, including configuration, workflows, and business rules, and hands-on configuration across Payroll, Payroll Interface, and related integrations.
  • SAP certification in SAP HCM or Payroll, preferably on S/4HANA, is highly desirable.
  • CSPO, PSPO or SAFe POPM (the SAFe Product Owner/Product Manager certification), ITIL 4 Foundation or similar IT service management certification.
  • Knowledge of functional domains within Global Functions (e.g., HR) and familiarity with the technology platforms that enable them (e.g., SAP HCM/PY on S4 HANA) and legacy ECC.
  • Knowledge of global or multi-country payroll platforms and managed payroll service providers.
  • Familiarity with Strada and/or Mercans is preferred.
  • Understanding of data protection for payroll data that crosses borders, such as GDPR.
  • Awareness of how local statutory and regulatory changes drive technical changes in outsourced payroll services. Understanding of product performance measures and KPIs, with the ability to drive improvements in product adoption, cycle time, stability, support effort, and overall user experience.
  • Strong understanding of payroll processes, local tax regulations, and compliance requirements, including government reporting and statutory payments.
  • Proven experience defining and prioritising functional requirements (e.g., epics, features, user stories) and managing a product backlog.
  • Experience working directly with business stakeholders to translate needs into feasible, value-led technology changes.
  • Demonstrated ability to make prioritisation decisions based on business value, process impact, risk, cost, and technology constraints.
  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in a relevant field (e.g., Computer Science, Information Technology, or Engineering), or equivalent experience.

Preferred skills:


  • Strong communication and influencing skills, able to explain technology constraints clearly and support stakeholders in making informed product decisions.
  • Skilled in coaching and guiding Associate Product Owners and delivery team members to ensure requirements, documentation, and solutions meet business needs and compliance expectations.
  • Able to interpret business processes, user feedback, and operational data to identify opportunities for process simplification, automation, and improved user experience.
  • Comfortable working within structured governance, security, and data protection requirements, ensuring product changes remain controlled, supportable, and compliant.
  • Strong analytical mindset, able to weigh value, risk, complexity, and cost to make prioritisation decisions and sequence backlog items appropriately.
  • Ability to work in a very fast-paced and fluid environment
  • Comfortable with ambiguity and change


Skills

API Integration, Automation, ISO 20022, ITIL Processes, Payroll Interfaces, Root Cause Analysis (RCA), SAP ERP Central Component (SAP ECC), SAP HANA, SAP HCM, SAP Payroll, System Configuration

Why GSK?

title: Associate Director, Product Owner - Compliance
description:
Job Purpose:


The Associate Director, Product Owner - Compliance is responsible for maximising the value of a set of compliance technology products across the Legal, Compliance & WREF domain by translating business needs into a prioritised backlog and leading delivery across the product lifecycle, within strategic and financial guardrails set by the Director, Compliance Product Manager and Senior Director of Legal, Compliance & WREF Digital & Tech. They work closely with business stakeholders to define outcomes and ensure delivered functionality is usable, secure, compliant, supportable, and aligned to product strategy.

The Compliance Product Owner guides Product Analysts and works with delivery teams to ensure requirements are clear, value-driven, and data-informed, while overseeing iterative delivery that improves product performance, adoption, and operational readiness.

This role operates under GSK's "Performance with Choice" hybrid working approach, typically expecting 2–3 days per week in the office, with the specific pattern agreed between the successful candidate and their manager based on role and team needs.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Partner with business stakeholders to understand functional needs, refine requirements, and define product outcomes that support business priorities, within guardrails set by the Director, Compliance Product Manager and Senior Director of Legal, Compliance & WREF Digital & Tech.
  • Own and manage the Product backlog (e.g. Jira, ADO etc), for all Compliance products ensuring requirements (e.g., epics, features, user stories) are well-defined and supported by minimum data inputs (e.g., cost drivers, user volumes, risk/sensitivity, process impact, dependencies).
  • Make prioritisation decisions for the Product backlog based on value, cost, risk, business continuity, and resource capacity, escalating only where strategic trade-offs are required by the Director, Compliance Product Manager
  • Lead the Product team’s delivery activities, guiding Product Analysts and working with Engineers, Architects, and Testers to ensure solutions are fit-for-purpose, secure, compliant, supportable, and aligned to architectural standards.
  • Drive operational readiness by applying a delivery readiness checklist covering support model requirements, training needs, continuity planning, configuration/runbook documentation, release notes, and user onboarding.
  • Define and maintain the Product performance dashboard, tracking adoption, cycle time/throughput, stability/defects, UX signals (e.g., CSAT, SUS, completion rates), and support effort; use performance insights to drive continuous improvement.
  • Ensure product changes follow required the digital & tech management system (DTMS) security controls, risk assessments, data handling policies, and regulated change processes, obtaining approvals from relevant SMEs where required.
  • Support Solution Architects to assess design options and manage cross-Product dependencies, contract/interface impacts, and sequencing needs to support interoperability and consistent business outcomes.
  • Act as an escalation point for the Product team and business users on functional product issues, guiding decisions within agreed financial, risk, and architectural guardrails set by the Director, Compliance Product Manager and Director, Domain Architecture.
  • Contribute to the improvement of delivery practices within the Product, promoting agile (i.e. SaFe, Scrum etc), iterative, value-driven, and data-led ways of working, including meaningful measurement of benefits and operational impact.
  • Support the Director, Compliance Product Manager with the development of bold, data lead roadmaps for the Compliance tech stack and partner to ensure our tech stack is top quartile in this space
  • Be the aligned Tech Business Partner to the Compliance Risk Analytics & Monitoring team – ensuring their data products are best in class and driving a data and insights lead transformation for compliance

Required Skills:

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in a relevant field (e.g., Computer Science, Information Technology, or Engineering), or equivalent experience.
  • Industry certifications highly desirable (e.g. Agile Methodologies, CPM).
  • Knowledge of Compliance domains within large FTSE organisation and familiarity with the technology platforms that enable Risk & Compliance business processes
  • Knowledge of systems/platforms such as OneTrust, ServiceNow, Databricks, Certa, Harvey, Legora
  • Knowledge of deploying agentic capabilities for compliance functions.
  • 15 to 19 years of experience working in product delivery, digital solutions, business systems, or process-led technology roles.
  • Proven experience defining and prioritising functional requirements (e.g., epics, features, user stories) and managing a product backlog.
  • Experience working within Enterprise technology, particularly aligned to the Compliance function
  • Experience working directly with business stakeholders to translate needs into feasible, value-led technology changes.
  • Demonstrated ability to make prioritisation decisions based on business value, process impact, risk, cost, and technology constraints.
  • Experience leading delivery teams or analysts through the product lifecycle, from refinement and design through testing, release, and adoption.
  • Familiarity with enterprise governance requirements such as change control, security, data protection, and regulatory/compliance considerations.
  • Exposure to continuous improvement approaches (e.g., automation, process simplification, user-centred enhancements) that uplift product adoption, stability, or user experience.
  • Experience working within agile delivery environments and using iterative planning, delivery, and release practices.

Preferred Skills:

  • Strong communication and influencing skills, able to explain technology constraints clearly and support stakeholders in making informed product decisions.
  • Skilled in coaching and guiding Product Analysts and delivery team members to ensure requirements, documentation, and solutions meet business needs and compliance expectations.
  • Able to interpret business processes, user feedback, and operational data to identify opportunities for process simplification, automation, and improved user experience.
  • Comfortable working within structured governance, security, and data protection requirements, ensuring product changes remain controlled, supportable, and compliant.
  • Strong analytical mindset, able to weigh value, risk, complexity, and cost to make prioritisation decisions and sequence backlog items appropriately.

title: Team Manager Public Sector
description:
Om rollen

Team Manager-Public Sector har det helhetlige ansvaret for å sikre stabile, effektive og kundeorienterte leveranser til offentlig sektor.

Rollen skal koordinere teamets aktiviteter, sikre kvalitet og fremdrift i leveranser, håndtere risiko og bidra til høy kundetilfredshet gjennom tett oppfølging av kunder, prosjekter, interne ressurser og eksterne partnere.

En vil også ha ansvar for å sikre tilgjengelige og relevante fag- og presalgsressurser i salgs- og anbudsprosesser mot offentlig sektor.

Team Manager-Public Sector skal bidra aktivt i strategisk viktige kunde- og anskaffelsesprosesser. Det forventes å representere SD Worx Public eksternt og delta aktivt i relevante markeds- og kundeaktiviteter, inkludert konferanser, brukerkonferanser, brukerforum, kundearrangementer og større kundeprosesser.

Rollen er sentral for å sikre at SD Worx er en pålitelig og profesjonell leverandør til offentlig sektor, samtidig som leveransene gjennomføres effektivt, med høy kvalitet og i tråd med kundens forventninger.

Stillingen inngår i lederteamet til Operations og rapporterer direkte til Operations Director.

Leveranseansvar

  • Sikre stabile og effektive leveranser til kunder i offentlig sektor.

  • Koordinere leveranser på tvers av teamet og sikre god samhandling mellom interne og eksterne parter.

  • Prioritere oppgaver og aktiviteter basert på risiko, frister, avtalte SLA-er og kundebehov.

  • Iverksette nødvendige tiltak ved risiko, avvik eller leveranseutfordringer.

  • Håndtere og koordinere kritiske avvik frem til løsning.

  • Personalansvar for ansatte i Public-teamet.

Kunde- og samarbeidsansvar

  • Være Single Point of Contact (SPOC) mellom Operations og Salg, og fungere som salgsteamets primære kontaktpunkt.

  • Følge opp eksterne leverandører og tredjepartspartnere i implementerings- og leveranseprosjekter.

  • Etablere, lede og videreutvikle brukerforum for offentlig sektor.

  • Bidra aktivt til høy kundetilfredshet gjennom proaktiv oppfølging og kontinuerlig forbedring.

Prosjekt- og styringsansvar

  • Representere SD Worx i styringsgrupper knyttet til implementeringsprosjekter.

  • Sikre at prosjektleveranser gjennomføres i henhold til avtalt kvalitet, tid og omfang.

  • Rapportere status, risikoer og kritiske forhold til Growth Board.

Kompetanse- og teamansvar

  • Sikre at teamet til enhver tid har riktig kompetanse for å møte kundenes behov og leveransekrav.

  • Identifisere kompetansegap og initiere utviklingstiltak.

  • Bidra til struktur, prioritering og kontinuerlig forbedring av arbeidsprosesser i teamet.

  • Ansvar for å gjennomføre månedlige statusmøter for hele teamet, inkludert salg og Product.

Myndighet og mandat

  • Iverksette tiltak som bidrar til økt kundetilfredshet og forbedret leveransekvalitet.

  • Prioritere ressurser og oppgaver basert på risiko, frister, SLA-forpliktelser og kommersielle forhold.

  • Godkjenne endringsordrer opp til NOK 50 000.

  • Eskalere kritiske saker og foreslå nødvendige korrigerende tiltak.

Personlige egenskaper

Vi ser etter en ressurs som har personlige egenskaper som kombinerer operasjonell gjennomføringsevne, relasjonsbygging, kommersiell forståelse og evnen til å skape struktur i et komplekst leveransemiljø.

Strukturert og planmessig
Setter klare prioriteringer, følger opp avtaler og sikrer fremdrift.

Kundeorientert
Ser saker fra kundens perspektiv og tar eierskap til utfordringer.

Beslutningsdyktig
Handler raskt når situasjonen krever det, uten å miste helhetsbildet.

Samarbeidsorientert og relasjonssterk
Oppfattes som tilgjengelig, løsningsorientert og troverdig.

Tydelig og trygg kommunikator
Gir klare forventninger og skaper forutsigbarhet.

Proaktiv og forbedringsorientert
Ser muligheter for forbedring og omsetter disse til konkrete tiltak.

Robust og løsningsorientert
Fokuserer på løsninger fremfor problemer.

title: Head of Maintenance
description:
We are currently accepting applications for the position of Head of Department Maintenance at Coronet Peak Ski Area. This is a full time, year-round permanent position based in Queenstown.
Reporting to the Ski Area Manager, you will lead the Maintenance team to ensure the ski area assets are compliant, safe and reliable. As part of the Coronet Peak leadership team you will also be responsible for providing operational and strategic support to deliver NZSki's vision statements.
About the role
As Head of Maintenance, you will:

Lead, support and develop a team of approximately 12 tradespeople.
Supervise employees and contractors undertaking maintenance work across the ski area.
Set and maintain high standards for health and safety, regulatory compliance and asset reliability.
Oversee planned, preventative and reactive maintenance activities.
Coordinate maintenance projects, resources, contractors and operational priorities.
Support the safe and reliable operation of passenger ropeways, conveyors, vehicles, buildings and infrastructure.
Work closely with other departments to provide responsive service to internal and external customers.
Contribute operational and strategic expertise as a member of the Coronet Peak leadership team.
Identify practical and innovative ways to improve systems, processes and asset performance.
Support the delivery of NZSki’s vision and wider business objectives.

About you
You will be a practical, organised and solutions focused leader who is comfortable balancing immediate operational demands with long term maintenance planning.
To succeed in this role, you will bring:

A relevant trade, engineering or industry-recognised technical qualification.
Minimum of two year's experience leading and developing a trades-based team.
A strong commitment to health and safety, regulatory compliance and effective risk management.
Sound knowledge of mechanical and electrical engineering principles and practices.
Strong project planning, prioritisation and problem-solving skills.
Clear, confident communication and effective people-management skills.
A collaborative approach and a commitment to delivering excellent service.
Confidence using Microsoft applications for planning, reporting, documentation and administration.
Experience with ski area equipment, passenger ropeways, heavy vehicles or industrial plant would be highly regarded.
A full New Zealand driver licence is required.
A Class 2 licence and Wheels, Tracks and Rollers endorsements would be advantageous.

title: Director of Payer and Government Relations
description:
Ranked one of Tennessee’s top places to work, MHC is a rare and special place where outstanding company culture is intentional. Where clients and associates are treated the same, as equals.


Mental Health Cooperative, Inc. (MHC) was formed in 1993 to serve individuals with severe and persistent mental illness. Since then, we have expanded our services to children and adolescents with severe emotional disorders across Middle and East Tennessee.

Our sole purpose is to support and treat those challenged with serious mental illness and poverty. Although based out of Nashville, we serve several communities across middle and East Tennessee with satellite offices in Antioch, Gallatin, Dickson, Columbia, Cleveland, Murfreesboro, Clarksville, Cookeville, Chattanooga, and Memphis.


If you are interested in joining a team that is caring, collaborative, innovative and energizing this might be a great place for you!

Position Summary

The Director of Payer and Government Relations leads how Mental Health Cooperative (MHC) shows up with the managed care organizations, commercial payers, and state and local government agencies that fund our work. This leader builds trust with decision makers, protects and grows our reimbursement, and makes sure the people we serve are reflected in the policies that shape access to care.


Reporting Structure

The Director of Strategy and Payer Contracts continues to own contract strategy, negotiation support, and related analysis. The Director of Payer and Government Relations owns the relationship and advocacy side: who we meet, what we ask for, and how we follow through. Contract terms and rate positions are coordinated between the two before anything is taken to a payer or agency.


Key Responsibilities

Payer relations

  • Build and maintain executive-level relationships with managed care organizations and commercial payers, with a regular meeting rhythm and clear agendas
  • Track payer performance, quality measures, and value-based arrangements, and prepare MHC leaders for payer meetings with accurate data and a clear ask
  • Identify new payer partnership opportunities that fit our mission and financial goals

Government relations

  • Represent MHC with state Medicaid and behavioral health agencies, local government, and elected officials
  • Monitor legislation, rulemaking, rate changes, and funding opportunities, and tell leadership what each means for our programs and finances
  • Prepare testimony, comment letters, briefings, and talking points for the CEO and other executives
  • Take an active role in associations, coalitions, and workgroups that influence healthcare policy
  • Support grant and contract relationships with government funders in coordination with the Vice President

Internal partnership

  • Work with finance, operations, clinical leadership, and compliance so that what we say externally matches what we can deliver
  • Coordinate with the Director of Strategy and Payer Contracts on contract priorities, negotiation timing, and payer messaging
  • Give regional and program leaders a clear path to raise payer and government concerns
  • Keep a shared calendar of payer and government contacts, commitments, and follow-ups so nothing is dropped when leaders change
  • Maintain confidentiality in all dealings. Work in this role does not require access to client health information, and none should be handled or shared outside approved MHC processes


Qualifications and Competencies

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in health administration, public policy, business, or a related field, or equivalent experience
  • Seven or more years of progressive experience in payer relations, government affairs, contracting, or health policy, with at least three in behavioral health or a Medicaid-funded setting
  • Working knowledge of Medicaid managed care, behavioral health reimbursement, and the state legislative and regulatory process
  • Track record of building productive relationships with payers or government officials and resolving difficult issues
  • Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to brief executives and speak credibly in public settings
  • Comfort reading financial and performance data and turning it into a clear argument
  • Value-based arrangement experience required

Preferred

  • Master's degree in public administration, public health, business, or a related field
  • Experience with value-based payment, quality reporting, and network adequacy requirements
  • Existing relationships with state agencies, managed care organizations, or legislative offices
  • Experience working within a community-based provider organization
  • Experience with Medicaid in more than one state as preferred

What we look for in the person

  • Builds trust through consistency and follows through on every commitment
  • Advocates firmly without damaging the relationship
  • Works as a partner to finance, operations, and clinical teams
  • Understands the people we serve and keeps them at the center of every conversation
  • Exercises sound judgment about what to escalate and when

BENEFITS: Mental Health Cooperative offers a full comprehensive beneﬁt plan for you to participate in. The following products are available:

· Medical Insurance/Prescription Drug Coverage

· Health Savings Account

· Dental Insurance

· Vision Insurance

· Basic Life and AD&D Insurance

· Short- & Long-Term Disability

· Supplemental Life Insurance

· Cancer Insurance

· Accident Insurance

· Critical Illness Insurance

· 403b - Retirement Plan

· Calm App for medication and mental health

· Gym membership discounts

Mental Health Cooperative is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status.

title: Senior Data Scientist
description:
Senior Data Scientist

Our Company

N2IA Technologies is a consulting company specializing in acquisition/contracting support, cost/FinOps, and technology optimization for federal clients. We deliver tailored strategies, robust software solutions, and streamlined operations to help organizations achieve their goals. At N2IA, we are committed to developing innovative financial and compliance-based solutions that address evolving business and regulatory needs. If you are passionate about accounting, financial accuracy, and supporting government programs, N2IA is the place for you.

Position Overview

N2IA Technologies is seeking a Senior Data Scientist to lead advanced analytics and machine learning initiatives supporting federal government programs. This individual will translate complex mission, business, and operational requirements into analytical solutions that improve program performance, support resource planning, and inform decision-making.

The ideal candidate combines strong statistical and programming expertise with experience delivering practical, reliable data science solutions. This role will collaborate with government stakeholders, subject matter experts, data engineers, and developers while providing technical guidance to junior team members.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead data science initiatives from requirements gathering and data exploration through model development, validation, implementation, and monitoring.
  • Collaborate with government stakeholders to define mission and program questions, analytical requirements, performance measures, and expected outcomes.
  • Analyze complex datasets to identify trends, assess program performance, forecast outcomes, and recommend operational improvements.
  • Develop and evaluate statistical and machine learning models for forecasting, classification, anomaly detection, and other customer needs.
  • Establish practices for data preparation, feature engineering, model evaluation, reproducibility, and documentation.
  • Partner with data engineers and developers to integrate analytical solutions into customer systems and operational workflows.
  • Evaluate model limitations, bias, uncertainty, and changes in performance over time.
  • Prepare briefings, visualizations, reports, and technical documentation that communicate findings to government leaders and technical audiences.
  • Review analytical work, mentor junior data scientists, and guide technical decisions.
  • Follow applicable customer requirements for data governance, privacy, security, access controls, and responsible use of data and AI.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Operations Research, Engineering, or a related quantitative field.
  • Seven or more years of progressive experience in data science, statistical analysis, machine learning, or a closely related analytical field.
  • Expert proficiency in Python or R for data analysis and model development, including hands-on experience with relevant statistical and machine learning libraries.
  • Strong SQL skills and hands-on experience extracting, joining, and analyzing data from relational databases.
  • Strong knowledge of statistical methods, including regression, hypothesis testing, experimental design, and interpretation of uncertainty.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and validating predictive models, selecting appropriate evaluation metrics, and addressing overfitting and data leakage.
  • Hands-on experience preparing complex datasets and resolving missing values, inconsistent formats, duplicate records, and other data quality issues.
  • Experience implementing analytical solutions for operational use and collaborating with engineering teams on deployment and monitoring.
  • Strong ability to translate stakeholder requirements into analytical approaches and communicate actionable recommendations to technical and nontechnical audiences.
  • Hands-on experience with version control, reproducible analytical workflows, and technical documentation.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Hands-on experience supporting federal government customers and working with government programs or mission data.
  • Experience working in environments with formal data governance, privacy, security, and documentation requirements.
  • Hands-on experience with cloud analytics or machine learning platforms such as AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, or Databricks.
  • Experience with distributed data processing tools such as Apache Spark or PySpark.
  • Experience with model lifecycle practices, including experiment tracking, model versioning, automated testing, and performance monitoring.
  • Experience applying natural language processing, time-series forecasting, optimization, or generative AI to a defined business or mission need.
  • Experience analyzing acquisition, contracting, financial, cost, or operational data.
  • Experience mentoring analysts or data scientists and leading technical delivery.

N2IA is committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive work environment. We are an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer and encourage applications from all qualified individuals, regardless of gender, race, ethnicity, sexual orientation, disability, or veteran status.

title: Sustainability Science Fellow
description:
What We Can Achieve Together:


The Impact Finance & Markets division at The Nature Conservancy (TNC) provides technical and strategic leadership to create transformational impact with the private sector by translating the value of nature and conservation approaches into actionable, science-based strategies that can help solve societal challenges. The Corporate Engagement Business Unit is one of four units comprising the Impact Finance & Markets division.This two-year Sustainability Science Fellow will be a member of TNC’s Corporate Engagement Science & Standards team. The They will contribute quantitative and data science expertise to help ensure corporate engagements and related conservation strategies are grounded in robust science, transparent methods and assumptions, and clear evidence. Working with senior team members, relationship managers, conservation teams, and external collaborators, the position will conduct applied research, develop and evaluate models, synthesize scientific evidence, and translate results into practical recommendations for private-sector decision-making.


The ideal candidate is a developing applied scientist with strong quantitative, computational, or data science expertise and a rigorous research background. They bring curiosity, sound scientific judgment, a collaborative approach, and the ability to work productively across disciplines, geographies, cultures, and levels of technical expertise.


This position can be based in any location with an establish TNC office. This is a two-year term position with opportunity for extension based on funding and performance.


Please submit applications ASAP because submissions will be closed once sufficient applications are received.


We’re Looking for You:


The Sustainability Science Fellow conducts applied research, analysis, modeling, and synthesis and translation related to critical private sector sustainability challenges, with input from senior staff. They maintain fluency in their primary subject area and relevant specialized methods, support internal and external technical advisory work across multiple projects, and may lead defined components of technical work and the communication of results. Using statistical, computational, spatial, or other quantitative methods, they generate evidence to inform strategy and decision-making, while ensuring analytical rigor through assessment of data quality, uncertainty, methodological documentation, and clear communication of findings.


RESPONSIBILITIES & SCOPE

  • Conduct applied research and develop models, analyses, and decision-support tools.
  • Synthesize scientific evidence and technical guidance to support project and strategy development.
  • Deliver scientific analyses, technical recommendations, and related products to internal and external partners.
  • Support technical advisory activities across multiple projects and initiatives.
  • Contribute to project design, monitoring, evaluation, and reporting.
  • Communicate scientific findings, uncertainty, and limitations to diverse audiences.
  • Investigate emerging topics and develop recommendations for future analysis and action.
  • May lead staff, interns, or volunteers on a project basis.
  • May manage a grant, contract, or request for proposal.
  • Travel may be required.

What You’ll Bring:

  • Master’s degree in a science-related field and at least two years of relevant experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Experience with applied statistics, data science, computational science, spatial science, quantitative modeling, or another related research method.
  • Experience developing, applying, or evaluating quantitative models for research or decision support.
  • Experience manipulating, analyzing, interpreting, and visualizing complex datasets.
  • Experience designing and documenting reproducible analytical workflows and communicating methods, assumptions, uncertainty, and findings.
  • Experience synthesizing scientific literature and technical information and preparing reports or other products that communicate findings.
  • Experience working with cross-functional or interdisciplinary teams and communicating with people from varied technical, geographic, and cultural backgrounds.


Desired Qualifications:

  • PhD degree in a relevant scientific discipline.
  • Record of scientific contribution through publications, technical reports, presentations, datasets, software, or other research products.
  • Experience working with or within private-sector organizations in applied decision-support contexts.
  • Strong written, oral, visual, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Comfort with ambiguity, curiosity, the ability to creatively solve problems and a commitment to scientific integrity and TNC’s mission and values.

Salary Information:


This position may be based in any country where TNC has an established entity, taking into consideration legal restrictions, such as non-national ratios and immigration processing times. For U.S. based applicants only, the starting pay range for this position is generally within the range of $75,000-105,00 for annual base salary and is based on location, qualifications, specific skills, and experience.


This range only applies to candidates whose country of employment is the USA. For all other applicants, pay ranges will be in local currency, the pay range will be based on the local labor market, and not tied to the above pay range. Your geographic location will be confirmed during the recruitment and used to determine your actual pay range. Additionally, for all applicants, actual pay will fall within a range based on a variety of factors including, for example, the candidate’s qualifications, specific skills, and experience.


Who We Are:

The Nature Conservancy’s mission is to protect the lands and waters upon which all life depends. As a science-based organization, we create innovative, on-the-ground solutions to our world’s toughest challenges so that we can create a world in which people and nature thrive. We’re rooted in our mission and guided by our values, which include respect for all people, communities, and cultures. Whether it’s career development, flexible schedules, or a rewarding mission, there’s many reasons to love life inside TNC. Want a better insight to TNC? Check out our TNC Talent playlist on YouTube to hear stories from staff or visit Glassdoor.

One goal is to cultivate an inclusive work environment so that all our colleagues around the globe feel a sense of belonging and that their unique contributions to our mission are valued. In addition to the requirements in our job postings, we recognize that people come with talent and experiences outside of a job and consider each applicant’s unique experience. Please apply – we’d love to hear from you. To quote a popular saying at TNC, “you’ll join for the mission, and stay for the people.”

What We Bring:


Since 1951, TNC has been doing work you can believe in. Through grassroots action, we have grown from a small non-profit into one of the most effective and wide-reaching environmental organizations in the world. Thanks to more than 1 million members, over 400 scientists, and the dedicated efforts of our diverse staff and partners, we impact conservation around the world!

TNC offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package including health care benefits, flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) plan with an 8% employer match, parental leave, accrued paid time off, life insurance, disability coverage, employee assistance program, other life and work well-being benefits. Learn more about our Benefits and Perks here.

We’re proud to offer a flexible work environment that supports of the health and well-being of the people we employ.

Our recruiting process includes a rolling interview process to ensure we engage applicants in a timely manner. This means we may review applications in the order in which they are received. Once a strong candidate pool is identified, the role will be unposted. The timeline may vary depending on the expressed interest in the role, so we highly encourage candidates to apply as soon as possible.

Employees must submit their application by logging into Workday and applying via the Jobs Hub.

The Nature Conservancy is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Our commitment to equal employment opportunity includes the recognition that our conservation mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people of all backgrounds, beliefs, and culture. Recruiting and mentoring staff to create an inclusive organization is a priority, and we encourage applicants from all cultures, races, colors, religions, sexes, national or regional origins, ages, disability status, sexual orientation, gender identity, military, protected veteran status or other status protected by law.


The successful applicant must meet the requirements of The Nature Conservancy's background screening process.

Do you have military experience? Visit our U.S. Military Skills Translator to match your military experience with our current job openings!

TNC is committed to offering accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application process. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please send a note to applyhelp@tnc.org with Request for Accommodation in the subject line.

At Expedia Group, we help travelers explore the world, one journey at a time. As a global travel company powered by passionate people, trusted partnerships, and leading technology, we connect travelers, partners, and advertisers through our consumer brands, B2B network, and travel advertising business.

Join our dynamic Dispute Ops team as a Disputes Investigator I, where you'll play a vital role in protecting our company and customers from fraudulent activity. title: Business Management Analyst
description:
Job Description:

For over 150 years, our dedication to being the Global Hausbank for our clients has been driven by our people – in around 60 countries and across more than 150 nationalities.

Their deep understanding, insights, expertise, and passion help our clients navigate an increasingly complex world – be it in our Corporate Bank, our Private Bank, our Investment Bank or our Asset Management division.

If you are motivated to take the initiative and collaborate with colleagues around the world; if you want to be part of a community where you can grow, both professionally and personally - join our team.

Together we can make a great impact for our clients home and abroad, securing their lasting success and financial security.

The Business Management Analyst supports the effective financial and operational management of the Belgium TDI/COO organization. The role combines financial and budget management, forecasting and management information, resource management, vendor and contract management, business planning, stakeholder coordination and continuous process improvement.

The role analyses financial and operational information evaluates the impact of business and portfolio decisions and provides management with accurate information and forward-looking insights to support planning and decision-making. It also contributes to consistent, reliable, and efficient Business Management processes across the organization.


Responsabilities:

  • Financial and Budget Management:

Manage budgeting, forecasting and financial planning, including monitoring costs, FTEs, actuals and forecast performance.

Analyze financial performance and provide clear insights and recommendations to support management decisions.

  • Management Information and Business Analysis:

Prepare management information, reports, dashboards and KPIs, translating financial and operational data into actionable insights.

Provide recurring and ad-hoc analysis to support business decisions, prioritization and planning.

  • Resource Management: Support resource planning, allocation and monitoring of internal and external resources in line with business priorities and available budget.
  • Vendor and Contract Management:

Support the financial and administrative management of vendors, contracts and external services, including sourcing and pricing activities.

Coordinate invoice follow-up and monitor the financial performance of external resources and services in collaboration with Finance and Procurement.

  • Business Planning and Decision Support: Support business planning and management decisions by assessing the financial and operational impact of priorities, portfolio changes and resource requirements.
  • Process Improvement and Automation: Identify and implement opportunities to simplify, standardize and automate Business Management processes, reporting and forecasting activities.
  • Stakeholder Management: Partner effectively with Finance, Procurement and local, regional and global TDI/COO stakeholders, acting as a key point of contact for assigned Business Management topics.

Skills:

  • Minimum 3 years of relevant experience in Business Management, financial management, controlling or a comparable function, with strong knowledge of budgeting, forecasting, cost management and financial analysis. Experience in technology, financial services, resource management or vendor/contract management is an advantage.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work with financial figures and large data sets and translate complex information into clear, actionable management insights.
  • Strong Excel skills and proficiency with relevant reporting, data analysis and automation tools; good understanding of financial processes and systems.
  • Strong communication, organization and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities and collaborate effectively across functions in a global matrix environment.

title: Advisor – Social Impact (Fixed-Term Parental Leave Cover)
description:
As an Advisor – Social Impact, you’ll help coordinate and deliver a range of programmes, events and initiatives that connect Deloitte with our communities.

A key part of your role will be delivering Deloitte Grow in Auckland and Hamilton. You’ll work directly with secondary school students and teachers, coordinate Deloitte volunteers, and facilitate sessions with rangatahi.

Beyond Grow, you’ll work across our wider social impact programme. That could mean coordinating an event, communicating with schools and community partners, bringing Deloitte people together to support an initiative, preparing an internal story about our work, or helping the team gather information about the impact of our programmes.

It’s a varied role, so you’ll need to be comfortable moving between different audiences and priorities. One day you might be facilitating a session with high school students; the next you could be coordinating an event or working with people from across Deloitte.

Your typical day could include:

  • Facilitating Deloitte Grow sessions with secondary school students in Auckland and Hamilton
  • Coordinating social impact programmes and events, including school-based initiatives and events such as our Tech Week hackathons
  • Building relationships with schools, teachers, community partners and other stakeholders
  • Engaging Deloitte people to participate as coaches, mentors and contributors to our programmes
  • Managing programme logistics, communications, schedules, participation and follow-ups
  • Writing internal communications and stories that help share our programmes and their impact
  • Supporting the team to gather information and coordinate inputs for social impact reporting
  • Working across the wider Corporate Responsibility & Sustainability team to support other programmes and priorities as needed.

Deloitte Grow forms part of our Societal Innovation commitment to positively impact the lives of 25,000 people in Aotearoa New Zealand by 2030 through education, skills development and access to opportunity.

We’re looking for someone who can build strong relationships, stay organised and take ownership of delivering programmes and events.

You might currently work in community engagement, social impact, programme or event delivery, education, learning and development, communications or a similar role.

You’ll bring:

  • Experience coordinating and delivering programmes, events or initiatives
  • Strong facilitation and communication skills, including confidence presenting to or working with groups
  • The ability to build rapport with rangatahi and work effectively with people from different backgrounds
  • Confidence building relationships with external stakeholders and people at different levels within an organisation
  • Strong organisation skills and the ability to manage several priorities, deadlines and stakeholders at once
  • Clear and engaging written communication skills
  • Initiative and sound judgement, with the confidence to take ownership and keep things moving
  • Strong attention to detail, particularly when managing programme logistics and communications
  • An interest in social impact, education, skills development and creating opportunities for rangatahi.

Experience working with schools, rangatahi, community organisations or volunteer programmes would be useful, but isn’t essential.

You’ll be Auckland-based, with your own car and a full drivers license. You will be able to travel to Hamilton as required for programme delivery.

This is ideally a full-time position, although we’re open to someone working four days per week for the right candidate.

Making an impact that matters, together:

Our purpose and values are at the heart of everything we do. Living these values is essential to ensuring everyone feels included at work and able to reach their full potential. For us to succeed and thrive as an organisation, we understand the importance of creating a culture where diverse perspectives matter and where everyone is given an equal opportunity to thrive, grow and make an impact that matters.

To be considered for this role, you must be legally entitled to work in New Zealand. We are reviewing applications on a rolling basis and will review applications as they are received.

Does this sound like the sort of role for you? Then apply now!

Join us. But be you. At Deloitte, you’ll do more than just join something, you’ll add something. You’ve found a place that values your curiosity, passion, and desire to work alongside brilliant people on the things that really matter. There really is only one question: What impact do YOU want to make?

title: Senior Product Owner - CSV
description:
Job Purpose:

The Senior Product Owner - CSV is responsible for leading and managing Computer System Validation (CSV) activities to ensure digital systems are compliant, validated, and fit for purpose throughout their lifecycle. The role works closely with business, quality, validation, and technology teams to translate business and regulatory requirements into compliant solutions, validation strategies, and prioritized deliverables. The role ensures adherence to CSV, Good Practice (GxP), data integrity, security, and regulatory requirements through effective validation planning, risk-based testing, change control, and lifecycle management. It also drives standardization, continuous improvement, and the adoption of AI-enabled and automated validation practices to improve efficiency, quality, and compliance. The Product Owner - CSV is accountable for validation strategy, compliance readiness, and validation lifecycle activities, ensuring systems remain reliable, compliant, and audit-ready while supporting business and operational objectives. The role contributes to product roadmap planning, backlog prioritization, and KPI (Key Performance Indicator) monitoring to drive continuous improvement and effective governance of the CSV/MES (Manufacturing Execution System) product portfolio.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Manage CSV requirements, validation deliverables, and compliance activities for MES systems.
  • Own and manage CSV requirements, validation activities, risk assessments, testing, change controls, and release readiness to ensure 100% compliance with GxP, data integrity, security, and regulatory requirements.
  • Ensure on-time delivery of validation documentation, test evidence, and approvals, maintain systems in a validated and audit-ready state throughout their lifecycle.
  • Drive audit and inspection readiness, minimizing compliance observations and ensuring timely closure of audit findings, deviations, CAPAs (Corrective and Preventive Action), and change controls.
  • Collaborate with business, quality, engineering, and site teams to deliver validated solutions that meet business objectives and regulatory expectations.
  • Contribute to product roadmap planning and backlog prioritization, ensuring delivery aligns with compliance, operational, and business priorities.
  • Monitor and improve key metrics including validation cycle time, compliance status, release readiness, system availability, roadmap delivery, and stakeholder satisfaction.
  • Lead continuous improvement, standardization, and adoption of CSV best practices to increase efficiency, consistency, and compliance across MES platforms.
  • Leverage AI and automation to improve validation efficiency, documentation quality, test execution, and compliance monitoring.
  • Ensure systems remain reliable, compliant, available, and fit for purpose, supporting operational continuity and business performance.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, Information Technology, Engineering, Business, Life Sciences or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.
  • Minimum 2–4 years of experience in CSV, validation, quality, business analysis or technology delivery within regulated manufacturing environments.
  • Experience in managing CSV deliverables, including Validation Plans, Risk Assessments, User Requirements Specifications (URS), Functional Specifications (FS), Design Specifications (DS), Traceability Matrices, Test Protocols (IQ/OQ/PQ/UAT) Installation / Operational / Performance Qualification/User Acceptance Testing, Validation Reports and Change Controls.
  • Experience in translating business and regulatory requirements into compliant, risk-based MES solutions.
  • Experience in collaborating with Quality, Validation, Engineering, IT and business teams to maintain validated and audit-ready systems.
  • Experience in GxP, data integrity, security and regulatory requirements, including use of AI and automation tools to support validation activities, documentation, testing and compliance monitoring.
  • Experience in working with enterprise MES platforms in GxP-regulated pharmaceutical manufacturing environments.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in communication, facilitation and stakeholder management, including engaging business, quality, IT and validation stakeholders.
  • Experience in facilitating requirements gathering, backlog prioritisation and solution reviews with stakeholders.
  • Experience in applying analytical decision-making to balance business value, compliance, risk and operational impact.
  • Experience in translating business and validation requirements into product priorities and validated solutions.
  • Experience in MES, CSV, data integrity, security and GxP compliance requirements.
  • Experience in maintaining documentation, traceability and lifecycle management records.
  • Experience in working across cross-functional, global and vendor teams in a collaborative way.
  • Experience in delivering solutions that meet compliance, user and business requirements.

title: Arbetsledare för fastighets - och skadejour
description:
Vi söker en trygg, engagerad och affärsmässig ledare som vill utveckla människor, bygga starka team och driva våra spännande projekt framåt.

Är du en ledare som får människor att växa, skapar engagemang och får en grupp att arbeta tillsammans mot gemensamma mål? Har du dokumenterad erfarenhet av att leda andra och vet vad som krävs för att skapa en välfungerande verksamhet med både nöjda medarbetare och god lönsamhet?

Då kan du vara den arbetsledare vi söker till Ocab!

Vi söker framför allt en stark ledarprofil. För oss är ditt ledarskap avgörande. Du är en person som är lyhörd, omtänksam och tydlig, men som också har förmågan att fatta beslut, ställa krav och driva arbetet framåt. Du förstår att framgång skapas tillsammans och att ett bra resultat börjar med engagerade och motiverade medarbetare. Du ska vara prestigelös och själv kunna åka ut och hantera skador om situationen kräver.

Din roll hos oss

Som arbetsledare på Ocab får du en central roll i att leda, utveckla och driva vår verksamhet inom jourteamet i Malmö och Helsingborg.

Du ansvarar för att planera, leda, fördela och följa upp arbetet i teamet samt säkerställa att vår fastighetsjour och akuta skadeserviceprojekt genomförs med hög kvalitet, god effektivitet och lönsamhet.

En viktig del av ditt uppdrag är att skapa ett starkt team där medarbetarna känner delaktighet, tar ansvar och arbetar tillsammans mot gemensamma mål. Du bygger förtroende genom att vara närvarande, lyhörd och tydlig i ditt ledarskap. Du ser individen, men har alltid gruppens och verksamhetens bästa i fokus.

Du har också ett affärsmässigt ansvar och behöver förstå sambandet mellan planering, resursanvändning, kvalitet, kundnöjdhet och lönsamhet.

I rollen ingår bland annat att:

  • Leda, motivera och utveckla medarbetarna samt skapa en positiv och prestationsinriktad arbetsgrupp.

  • Planera, fördela och följa upp det dagliga arbetet och säkerställa rätt resurser på rätt plats.

  • Säkerställa arbetsgruppens samlade kompetens och arbeta med rekrytering, bemanning och utveckling.

  • Driva projekt från planering till genomförande och avslut med fokus på kvalitet, effektivitet och lönsamhet.

  • Skapa goda kundrelationer och ansvara för kontakten med fastighetsägare, försäkringsbolag och andra samarbetspartners.

  • Säkerställa hög kvalitet i skadebesiktningar, kalkyler, rapportering och dokumentation.

  • Hantera både planerade uppdrag och akuta situationer där förmågan att prioritera och fatta beslut är avgörande.

  • Vid behov vara operativ och arbeta ute på fältet tillsammans med medarbetarna.

Du leder en verksamhet där förutsättningarna snabbt kan förändras. Därför behöver du vara flexibel, lösningsorienterad och trygg i att hantera såväl människor som situationer under press.

Vem är du?

Vi söker dig som har dokumenterad erfarenhet av att leda och arbetsleda operativ personal, exempelvis tekniker, hantverkare eller andra yrkesgrupper i en praktisk verksamhet. Du är van att planera, fördela och följa upp arbetet, skapa engagemang i gruppen och få medarbetarna att arbeta tillsammans mot gemensamma mål.

Du har en god förståelse för vad som skapar fungerande team och vet att ett starkt ledarskap handlar om mer än att fördela arbetsuppgifter. Du får människor med dig, skapar tydlighet och bygger en kultur där alla bidrar och tar ansvar.

För att lyckas i rollen ska du vara lösningsorienterad, verksamhetsnära och lyhörd ledare med god människokännedom. Du är prestigelös och har lätt för att samarbeta med olika typer av människor, samtidigt som du är handlingskraftig, tydlig med förväntningar och vågar ta tag i utmaningar när det behövs.

Du har ett naturligt driv, är strukturerad och har förmågan att lyfta blicken och se helheten. Du förstår vikten av att balansera medarbetarnas förutsättningar med kundernas behov och verksamhetens ekonomiska mål.

Vi värdesätter särskilt att du:

  • Har dokumenterad erfarenhet av att leda andra i en praktisk och tjänstedriven verksamhet.

  • Är en trygg, lyhörd och tydlig ledare som skapar förtroende och engagemang.

  • Har förmåga att få människor att samarbeta och arbeta mot gemensamma mål.

  • Är lösningsorienterad, handlingskraftig och tvekar inte att själv åka ut och arbeta om situationen kräver det.

  • Har ett affärsmässigt tänk och förståelse för ekonomi, effektivitet och lönsamhet.

  • Är van att ta ansvar, fatta beslut och prioritera även i pressade situationer.

  • Har god kommunikationsförmåga och kan skapa bra relationer med både medarbetare och kunder.

Kvalifikationer

  • Dokumenterad erfarenhet av att leda andra, gärna med personalansvar.

  • Erfarenhet av beredskapsverksamhet eller arbete i verksamhet med varierande och akuta uppdrag.

  • Självgående och ansvarstagande med god administrativ förmåga.

  • Flytande svenska i tal och skrift.

  • God datorvana.

  • B-körkort.

Det är meriterande om du har erfarenhet från bevakning, säkerhet, blåljusverksamhet eller annan personalintensiv verksamhet där snabba beslut, tydligt ledarskap och förmågan att hantera oförutsedda situationer är en naturlig del av arbetet.

Kunskap i MEPS eller liknande rapporterings- och kalkylsystem är också meriterande.

Vi erbjuder dig

Hos Ocab får du en utvecklande och varierande ledarroll med stort ansvar och möjlighet att påverka både människor och verksamhetens utveckling.

Du blir en viktig del av ett engagerat team och får arbeta i en organisation med korta beslutsvägar, öppen företagskultur och stora möjligheter att utvecklas. Vi tror på att ge våra ledare förutsättningar att lyckas och vill att du ska kunna växa tillsammans med oss.

Du får ett omväxlande arbete där du kombinerar ledarskap, affärsmässighet och operativ verksamhet. Ingen dag är den andra lik och du får möjlighet att göra verklig skillnad – både för dina medarbetare och för våra kunder.

Är du vår nästa ledare?

Vi vill komma i kontakt med dig som har ett genuint intresse för ledarskap och som vill vara med och utveckla både människor och verksamhet.

Berätta i ditt personliga brev om dina erfarenheter som ledare, hur du arbetar för att skapa starka team och vad du anser kännetecknar ett riktigt bra ledarskap. Vi är särskilt intresserade av konkreta exempel på hur du har utvecklat medarbetare, skapat engagemang och bidragit till goda resultat.

Bifoga ditt CV samt eventuella intyg och betyg.

Övrig information

title: Invasive Species Intern
description:
What We Can Achieve Together:


We are hiring two (2,) full-time (40 hrs/week) Invasives Species Interns to work at our Bluestem Prairie Preserve in Glyndon, MN. These are seasonal positions with an anticipated start date of May 17, 2027 and an end date of August 13, 2027.


As an Invasive Species Intern, you will work in the Agassiz Beach Ridges and Sheyenne Delta Landscapes in the Northern Tallgrass Prairie Ecoregion (western Minnesota and eastern North Dakota, respectively) as part of a crew managing prairie and oak savannah tracts. You will maintain preserve areas frequented by the visiting public and perform duties such as vegetation management (herbicide applications, brush removal, tree removal, mowing, biological control, etc.), equipment and tool maintenance and organization, hand collecting native prairie seed, firebreak installation, boundary posting, fencing, prairie restorations, and assist with prescribed fires. You may also implement duties on partner lands such as the Minnesota DNR, USFS, and USFWS-owned properties.


You will primarily focus on treating and removing invasive plant species through the vegetation management techniques listed above. As part of TNC’s commitment to ongoing professional development, you will also help with a wide range of stewardship activities including but not limited to equipment maintenance and organization, prescribed fire, hand collecting native prairie seed, fencing and boundary posting. You will be expected to work independently and in a team environment to help plan and direct preserve work groups. You will regularly work with a 2-5 person crew. This position may require considerable physical exertion and/or muscular strain.


Housing and basic utilities are provided at TNC’s Bluestem Prairie to the employee upon signing and agreeing to housing terms. The value of the housing will be considered taxable income vs charged rent.


We’re Looking for You:


Are you looking for the opportunity to expand your experience in natural resource management? The Nature Conservancy is dedicated to managing our preserves and collaborating with conservation partners to make landscape-level impacts. We are looking for someone who is passionate, motivated, and willing to learn. Come join TNC and apply today!



What You’ll Bring:

  • High school diploma or GED and 6 months of related experience
  • Experience operating various types of equipment in a safe and efficient manner (e.g. lawn mower, chainsaw, UTV, ATV or OHV, two-way radio, or similar equipment).
  • Must be able to obtain related licenses or certifications as required. (e.g. First Aid, CPR, herbicide or pesticide application).


Desired Qualifications

  • Must have valid driver’s license and good driving record and able to obtain a DOT Health card.
  • Experience operating various types of equipment in a safe and efficient manner (e.g. Lawn mower, chainsaw, UTV, ATV or OHV, two-way radio, or similar equipment).
  • Ability and willingness to follow instructions from colleagues.

This position requires a valid driver's license and compliance with TNC’s Auto Safety Program. Employees may not drive Conservancy-owned/leased vehicles, rental cars, or personal vehicles on behalf of the Conservancy if considered "high risk drivers." To learn more about the Auto Safety Program, visit the Auto Safety information page. Employment in this position will be contingent upon completion of a Vehicle Use Agreement, which may include a review of the prospective employee's motor vehicle record.

Salary Information:


The starting pay range for a candidate selected for this position is generally within the range of $16.00 – 17.00/hour. This range only applies to candidates whose country of employment is the USA. Where a successful candidate’s actual pay will fall within this range will be based on a variety of factors, including, for example, the candidate's location, qualifications, specific skills, and experience. Please note countries outside the USA would have a different pay range in the local currency based on the local labor market, and not tied to USA pay or ranges. Your geographic location will be confirmed during the recruitment.

Who We Are:

The Nature Conservancy’s mission is to protect the lands and waters upon which all life depends. As a science-based organization, we create innovative, on-the-ground solutions to our world’s toughest challenges so that we can create a world in which people and nature thrive. We’re rooted in our mission and guided by our values, which include respect for all people, communities, and cultures. Whether it’s career development, flexible schedules, or a rewarding mission, there’s many reasons to love life inside TNC. Want a better insight to TNC? Check out our TNC Talent playlist on YouTube to hear stories from staff or visit Glassdoor.

One goal is to cultivate an inclusive work environment so that all our colleagues around the globe feel a sense of belonging and that their unique contributions to our mission are valued. In addition to the requirements in our job postings, we recognize that people come with talent and experiences outside of a job and consider each applicant’s unique experience. Please apply – we’d love to hear from you. To quote a popular saying at TNC, “you’ll join for the mission, and stay for the people.”

What We Bring:


Since 1951, TNC has been doing work you can believe in. Through grassroots action, we have grown from a small non-profit into one of the most effective and wide-reaching environmental organizations in the world. Thanks to more than 1 million members, over 400 scientists, and the dedicated efforts of our diverse staff and partners, we impact conservation around the world!

TNC offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package including health care benefits, flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) plan with an 8% employer match, parental leave, accrued paid time off, life insurance, disability coverage, employee assistance program, other life and work well-being benefits. Learn more about our Benefits and Perks here.

We’re proud to offer a flexible work environment that supports of the health and well-being of the people we employ.

Our recruiting process includes a rolling interview process to ensure we engage applicants in a timely manner. This means we may review applications in the order in which they are received. Once a strong candidate pool is identified, the role will be unposted. The timeline may vary depending on the expressed interest in the role, so we highly encourage candidates to apply as soon as possible.

The Nature Conservancy is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Our commitment to equal employment opportunity includes the recognition that our conservation mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people of all backgrounds, beliefs, and culture. Recruiting and mentoring staff to create an inclusive organization is a priority, and we encourage applicants from all cultures, races, colors, religions, sexes, national or regional origins, ages, disability status, sexual orientation, gender identity, military, protected veteran status or other status protected by law.

The successful applicant must meet the requirements of The Nature Conservancy's background screening process.

Do you have military experience? Visit our U.S. Military Skills Translator to match your military experience with our current job openings!

TNC is committed to offering accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application process. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please send a note to applyhelp@tnc.org with Request for Accommodation in the subject line.

title: Timvikarier sökes till kvinna utanför Kalix
description:
På Inre Kraft arbetar vi tillsammans för alla människors rätt till att leva livet fullt ut. Nu söker vi ytterligare en kollega till vårt team, är det du?

OM TJÄNSTEN

Vi på Inre Kraft söker dig som vill arbeta som personlig assistent åt vår kund i Storön, Kalix. Vi söker just nu 2st personer som kan jobba som timvikarier vid behov.

Arbetstiderna är följande:

  • Kl. 07.30-15.30

  • Kl. 14.00-21.00

Tillträde sker enligt överenskommelse där vi gärna ser att du kan påbörja introduktion omgående.

OM KUNDEN

Kunden är en kvinna i 70-årsåldern som är intresserad av att gå på stan, hantverk och trädgård. Vår kund behöver din hjälp som assistent i sin vardag då hon drabbades av en stroke för ett antal år sedan.

Arbetsuppgifterna inkluderar:

  • Stöd vid dagliga rutiner, som förekommande hushållssysslor

  • Förflyttningar, hjälp vid personlig hygien, av- och påklädning och viss träning

Kunden använder sig av manuell rullstol.

ÄR DU DEN VI SÖKER?

Vi söker dig som brinner för arbete med människor och kan analysera andra individers behov. Vidare bör du vara lyhörd, initiativtagande, lösningsfokuserad samt engagerad. Stor vikt läggs vid personlig lämplighet.

Om du känner att detta stämmer in på dig, kan du vara den vi söker!

KRAV

  • Körkort och tillgång till egen bil

  • Tåla pälsdjur då kunden har hund

MERITER

  • Erfarenhet av personlig assistans/annat vårdarbete

  • Erfarenhet av stroke

  • Vårdutbildning eller motsvarande

  • Tåla pälsdjur

Sysselsättningsgrad: 2 st timvikarier vid behov

Lön: Vi tillämpar individuell lönesättning. Övriga ersättningar i enlighet med kollektivavtal.

Din ansökan kommer att läsas av medarbetare på Inre Kraft, kund och anhörig.
Urvalet sker löpande och tjänsten kan komma att tillsättas innan sista ansökningsdagen.


Varmt välkommen med din ansökan!

För anställning hos oss på Inre Kraft behöver du ha ett BankID och godkänner att använda ditt BankID i tjänsten. En förutsättning för att påbörja en anställning hos oss är att du som söker kan uppvisa giltig ID-handling och/eller lämna in personbevis samt eventuella dokument som styrker rätten till arbete i Sverige. Personbevis kan du enkelt ladda ner på Skatteverkets hemsida. För att kunna jobba som personlig assistent behöver du vara minst 18 år.

Jobba hos oss på Inre Kraft AB

Inre Kraft är ett familjärt assistansbolag med huvudsaklig verksamhet i Norrbotten och Västerbotten. Vår målsättning är att tillgodose varje kunds individuella och unika behov av personlig assistans, där det är kunden som berättar hur verksamheten ska bedrivas. Våra ledord är trygghet, stabilitet och familjär känsla. Våra kundservicemedarbetare är tillgängliga över telefon årets alla dagar mellan kl 06.00-22.00. Vi har anordnar återkommande kostnadsfria aktiviteter för våra kunder och för dig som medarbetare. Vi är mån om dig som anställd och våra kunder, och strävar efter att skapa en arbetsplats där alla trivs och utvecklas.

Förmåner för dig som anställd hos Inre Kraft

Som anställd personlig assistent hos oss omfattas du av kollektivavtal och avtalspension. Du är försäkrad under arbetstid och till/från arbetet om något oförutsett skulle inträffa. Vi erbjuder friskvårdsbidrag till våra anställda.

Delning av ansökningar inom Team Olivia

För att ge dig bästa möjligheterna att hitta rätt tjänst kan din ansökan komma att delas med våra systerbolag inom Team Olivia, om din profil matchar en ledig tjänst där. Självklart sker detta endast med ditt godkännande, vilket du anger i samband med din ansökan.

För dig med anställningsstöd

Om du har rätt till anställningsstöd tar vi hänsyn till detta vid en eventuell anställning. Att ange denna information i din ansökan är helt frivilligt - alternativt kan du välja att informera oss vid en eventuell intervju. Vi ser detta som en möjlighet att tillsammans skapa en bra lösning för dig som medarbetare.
