title: Associate Director, Product Owner - Legal Ops
description:
Job Purpose:


The Associate Director, Product Owner - Legal Ops is responsible for maximising the value of the Legal Operations product group across the Legal, Compliance & WREF domain by translating business needs into a prioritised backlog and leading delivery across the product lifecycle, within strategic and financial guardrails set by the Dir, Legal Product Manager and Senior Director of Legal, Compliance & WREF Digital & Tech. They work closely with business stakeholders to define outcomes and ensure delivered functionality is usable, secure, compliant, supportable, and aligned to product strategy. The Legal Operations Product Owner guides Product Analysts and works with delivery teams to ensure requirements are clear, value-driven, and data-informed, while overseeing iterative delivery that improves product performance, adoption, and operational readiness. The role is accountable for ensuring Products in the Legal Ops domain have bold, data powered roadmaps.


This role operates under GSK's "Performance with Choice" hybrid working approach, typically expecting 2–3 days per week in the office, with the specific pattern agreed between the successful candidate and their manager based on role and team needs.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Partner with business stakeholders to understand functional needs, refine requirements, and define product outcomes that support business priorities, within guardrails set by the Dir, Legal Product Manager and Senior Director of Legal, Compliance & WREF Digital & Tech.
  • Own and manage the Product backlog (e.g. Jira, ADO etc) for all Legal Ops products ensuring requirements (e.g., epics, features, user stories) are well-defined and supported by minimum data inputs (e.g., cost drivers, user volumes, risk/sensitivity, process impact, dependencies).
  • Make prioritisation decisions for the Product backlog based on value, cost, risk, business continuity, and resource capacity, escalating only where strategic trade-offs are required by the Dir, Legal Product Manager and Senior Director of Legal, Compliance & WREF Digital & Tech.
  • Lead the Product team’s delivery activities, guiding Product Analysts and working with Engineers, Architects, and Testers to ensure solutions are fit-for-purpose, secure, compliant, supportable, and aligned to architectural standards.
  • Drive operational readiness by applying a delivery readiness checklist covering support model requirements, training needs, continuity planning, configuration/runbook documentation, release notes, and user onboarding.
  • Define and maintain the Product performance dashboard, tracking adoption, cycle time/throughput, stability/defects, UX signals (e.g., CSAT, SUS, completion rates), and support effort; use performance insights to drive continuous improvement.
  • Ensure product changes follow required digital & tech governance, in line with our digital & tech management system (DTMS), security controls, risk assessments, data handling policies, and change processes, obtaining approvals from relevant SMEs where required.
  • Support Solution Architects to assess design options and manage cross-Product dependencies, contract/interface impacts, and sequencing needs to support interoperability and consistent business outcomes.
  • Act as an escalation point for the Product team and business users on functional product issues, guiding decisions within agreed financial, risk, and architectural guardrails set by the Dir, Legal Product Manager and Dir, Domain Architecture.
  • Contribute to the improvement of delivery practices within the Product, promoting agile (i.e. SaFe, Scrum etc), iterative, value-driven, and data-led ways of working, including meaningful measurement of benefits and operational impact.
  • Support the Director, Legal Product Manager in ensuring the technology stack in Legal Ops is top quartile and driving business value
  • Partner with Legal business stakeholders on the roadmap and vision for the products in this domain – including for Legal document management, Legal matter management, eBilling, Contract Lifecycle management and Legal AI products/LLMs being explored as part of Legal & Compliance Digital Transformation.

Required Skills:

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in a relevant field (e.g., Computer Science, Information Technology, or Engineering), or equivalent experience.
  • Industry certifications highly desirable (e.g. Agile Methodologies, CPM).
  • 15 to 19 years of experience working in product delivery, digital solutions, business systems, or process-led technology roles.
  • Proven experience defining and prioritising functional requirements (e.g., epics, features, user stories) and managing a product backlog.
  • Experience working within Enterprise Technology, Product and Service Management, Legal technologies
  • Knowledge of Legal Operations technologies such as legal document management, legal matter management, eBilling, contract lifecycle management, legal AI platforms.
  • Knowledge of systems such as NetDocs, Ascent, Ironclad, Persuit, Harvey, Legora, Vincent is extremely advantageous.
  • Understanding of product performance measures and KPIs, with the ability to drive improvements in product adoption, cycle time, stability, support effort, and overall user experience.
  • Experience working directly with business stakeholders to translate needs into feasible, value-led technology changes including being strong at communicating technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders and confidence working with lawyers at varying levels of seniority
  • Demonstrated ability to make prioritisation decisions based on business value, process impact, risk, cost, and technology constraints.
  • Experience leading delivery teams or analysts through the product lifecycle, from refinement and design through testing, release, and adoption.
  • Familiarity with enterprise governance requirements such as change control, security, data protection, and regulatory/compliance considerations.
  • Exposure to continuous improvement approaches (e.g., automation, process simplification, user-centred enhancements) that uplift product adoption, stability, or user experience.
  • Experience working within agile delivery environments and using iterative planning, delivery, and release practices.

Preferred Skills:

  • Strong communication and influencing skills, able to explain technology constraints clearly and support stakeholders in making informed product decisions.
  • Skilled in coaching and guiding Product Analysts and delivery team members to ensure requirements, documentation, and solutions meet business needs and compliance expectations.
  • Able to interpret business processes, user feedback, and operational data to identify opportunities for process simplification, automation, and improved user experience.
  • Comfortable working within structured governance, security, and data protection requirements, ensuring product changes remain controlled, supportable, and compliant.
  • Strong analytical mindset, able to weigh value, risk, complexity, and cost to make prioritisation decisions and sequence backlog items appropriately.


Skills

Agile Methodology, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Automation, Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM), Legal Operations, Legal Technology, Product Delivery, Product Management, Product Strategies, Requirements Gathering, Stakeholder Management

Uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together.

By joining this team, you’ll help shape systems that support thousands of employees worldwide, driving innovation and reliability in the tools that keep GSK moving forward.

Job Purpose:

The Director, Product Manager - Legal leads a group of Legal Technology Products – spanning Legal Operations and Intellectual Property (IP) within the Legal, Compliance & WREF Digital & Tech Domain, ensuring they deliver measurable value, support business processes, and are continuously improved. They work closely with the SD, Legal, Compliance & WREF Digital & Tech to translate functional goals into product roadmaps and provide direction to Product Owners on prioritisation, delivery focus, and product performance. The Director, Legal Product Manager ensures that Legal & Compliance products are usable, compliant, secure, and efficient to operate, while fostering a culture of agile delivery, value realisation, and continuous improvement across their Product group.

This role operates under GSK's "Performance with Choice" hybrid working approach, typically expecting 2–3 days per week in the office, with the specific pattern agreed between the successful candidate and their manager based on role and team needs.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Translate functional strategies provided by the SD, Legal, Compliance & WREF Digital & Tech into actionable product roadmaps and delivery priorities across the Legal product group – covering Legal Operations and Intellectual Property as well as the Legal AI Platform products.
  • Provide leadership, direction and coaching to Product Owners, ensuring requirements are well-defined, business cases for investment are robust, backlogs are prioritised to support business goals, architectural guidance, compliance needs, data-driven decisions, FinOps considerations, and domain ecosystem dependencies through cross-functional partnering.
  • Partner with business stakeholders to understand pain points, process challenges, and improvement needs, shaping product enhancements and technology-enabled opportunities.
  • Oversee delivery execution across the Legal product group, ensuring the quality, usability, stability, and supportability of released features and services.
  • Promote agile and iterative delivery practices (e.g. SaFe, Scrum), supporting incremental value release, transparency of priorities, and improved collaboration with business users. Being comfortable providing product leadership to multiple delivery initiatives at one time.
  • Act as the escalation point for critical product performance, delivery issues, and dependency conflicts, addressing risks and facilitating decisions.
  • Champion the adoption of user-centred improvements, Legal business process optimisation, and automation/AI opportunities that reduce cycle time and enhance user experience.
  • Ensure effective, defensible, risk, security, and compliance management (e.g. ISO controls, GDPR, legal privilege, Information governance requirements) across the Legal product group, embedding relevant controls in partnership with Security, Risk, Legal and Compliance SMEs.
  • Support Solution Architects in shaping cross-product and cross-platform solutions, ensuring Product Owners manage dependencies to deliver integrated outcomes.
  • Track and report performance against agreed KPIs for the Legal product group, driving continuous improvement activities to maximise value for the Legal, Compliance & WREF Digital & Tech Domain.
  • Provide financial oversight of the Legal product group, including product budgets and internal/external team resourcing costs, to inform strategic decision‑making and ensure alignment with GSK’s financial objectives.
  • Lead Innovation agenda across the Legal & IP products ensuring we are running a top quartile technology stack. Includes staying abreast of advancements of the Legal technology ecosystem
  • Ensure investment requests in Legal technology follow the Legal & Compliance Tech & AI board governance, and partner with business leaders to develop robust plans and robust designs as part of approval processes.
  • Champion the use of AI, automation and technology in the Legal & Compliance function
  • Lead your team in using approved AI tools to improve productivity and ways of working, role-modelling responsible use and follow GSK’s Responsible AI, privacy and security requirements.

Required Skills & Qualification:

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in a relevant field (e.g., Computer Science, Information Technology, or Engineering), or equivalent experience
  • Extensive experience 18+ years overseeing end-to-end product delivery, including prioritisation, backlog management, solution design support, testing oversight, and value-focused release planning – with clear focus on Legal Tech
  • Proven track record in overseeing the definition and execution of Legal technology systems in a company of similar size and scale to GSK, realising tangible benefits for the Business.
  • Deep experience in concurrently overseeing multiple Product teams across the full delivery lifecycle, from requirements elicitation through to release.
  • Proficient in conveying complex technology ideas to non-conversant audiences.
  • Very strong analytical and problem-solving skills for developing Product use cases and determining their associated value.
  • Highly experienced team leader that can effectively manage small to medium IT delivery teams.
  • Very strong communication skills and ability to influence senior stakeholders, aligning on competing priorities and guiding Business teams on the feasibility of requests vs. technology constraints.
  • Industry certifications highly desirable (e.g. Agile Methodologies, CPM).

Preferred Skills:

  • Strong communication and influencing skills, able to guide prioritisation decisions, resolve delivery conflicts, and align multiple stakeholders around shared product outcomes.
  • Skilled in coaching and developing Product Owners, fostering a culture of user-centred design, value-based delivery, and continuous improvement.
  • Able to interpret business processes, regulatory needs, and operational insights to identify optimisation and automation opportunities that enhance product performance and user experience.
  • Comfortable working within structured governance, security, and compliance constraints, ensuring product changes are well controlled, supportable, and aligned to organisational standards.


Skills

Artificial Intelligence (AI), Automation, Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM), Digital Transformation, Generative AI, Information Governance, Intellectual Property, Legal Technology, Product Management Leadership

title: Prescribed Fire Land Management Technician
description:
What We Can Achieve Together:


We are hiring three (3,) full-time (40 hrs/week) Prescribed Fire & Land Management Technicians to work at our Bluestem Prairie Preserve in Glyndon, MN. These are seasonal positions anticipated to start March 29, 2027 and end on November 5, 2027.

As a Prescribed Fire and Land Management Technician, you will maintain preserve areas frequented by the visiting public - the Agassiz Beach Ridges and Sheyenne Delta Landscapes in the Northern Tallgrass Prairie Ecoregion (western Minnesota and eastern North Dakota, respectively.) Although not responsible for supervising staff, you may help plan and direct preserve work groups, including staff or volunteers, and will work as part of a crew. You will help manage prairie and oak savannah tracts as well as be responsible for preparation and implementation of prescribed fire at various nature preserves in these landscapes.


Technician duties will include vegetation and exotic species monitoring, management, and removal (herbicide applications, brush removal, tree removal, mowing, biological control, etc.), equipment and tool maintenance and organization, hand collecting native prairie seed, firebreak installation, boundary posting, fencing, prairie restorations, and assist with prescribed fires. You may also implement duties on partner lands such as the Minnesota DNR, USFS, and USFWS-owned properties.


You will also participate in prescribed fire operations which include ignition, control, mop-up, suppression, monitoring, and other tasks as assigned. They will participate in preparing fire lines, maintaining equipment, post-burn monitoring and other tasks. As part of the Technician’s ongoing professional development, they will be responsible for keeping abreast of new burn techniques and equipment to enhance skills and maintain/grow professional fire certification credentials.

Housing and basic utilities are provided at TNC’s Bluestem Prairie to the employee upon signing and agreeing to housing terms. The value of the housing will be considered taxable income vs charged rent.

Transportation from The Nature Conservancy office to the various preserves will also be provided.

This position occasionally requires irregular hours, travel on short notice and the ability to work weekends during the fire season. May work in variable weather conditions, at remote locations, on difficult and hazardous terrain, and under physically demanding circumstances (requires considerable physical exertion and/or muscular strain.)


We’re Looking for You:


Are you looking for a career to help people and nature? Guided by science, TNC creates innovative, on-the-ground solutions to our world’s toughest challenges so that people and nature can thrive together. We’re looking for someone who thrives and enjoys the outdoors and a team player. Your journey with us means continuous growth. Master new techniques and equipment to level up your skills and certifications. Plus, you'll build strong relationships within the conservation team and local areas where we operate. Come join TNC and apply today!


What You’ll Bring:

  • High school diploma or GED and 1 year of training in a science-related field or related experience in land management.
  • Experience recognizing plant and animal species.
  • Experience operating various types of equipment in a safe and efficient manner (e.g. Lawn mower, chainsaw, UTV, ATV or OHV, two-way radio, or similar equipment).
  • Experience working in a team environment.
  • Must be qualified, or able to become qualified, as a Fire Fighter Type 2 (FFT2), including Introduction to ICS (I-100), Human Factors on the Fire line (L-180), Introduction to Wild Land Fire Behavior (S-190), Firefighting Training (S-130), and one training burn serving under the supervision of a qualified FFT2. (TNC can help with FFT2 training once offered the position. See http://www.tncfiremanual.org/firefighter.html)
  • Must achieve physical fitness standard as determined by local Fire Program Manager and the TNC Fire Manual.
  • Must have a valid driver’s license.
  • Must be able to obtain related licenses or certifications as required. (e.g. First Aid, CPR, etc.)



Desired Qualifications

  • 1 - 2 years’ experience in land management or related field.
  • Experience working with or knowledge of natural systems.
  • Ability to follow instructions from colleagues/coworkers/team members.
  • PC and/or mobile device familiarity, including database knowledge or understanding.

This position requires a valid driver's license and compliance with TNC’s Auto Safety Program. Employees may not drive Conservancy-owned/leased vehicles, rental cars, or personal vehicles on behalf of the Conservancy if considered "high risk drivers." To learn more about the Auto Safety Program, visit the Auto Safety information page. Employment in this position will be contingent upon completion of a Vehicle Use Agreement, which may include a review of the prospective employee's motor vehicle record.

Salary Information:


The starting pay range for a candidate selected for this position is generally within the range of $18.60 – 19.65. This range only applies to candidates whose country of employment is the USA. Where a successful candidate’s actual pay will fall within this range will be based on a variety of factors, including, for example, the candidate's location, qualifications, specific skills, and experience. Please note countries outside the USA would have a different pay range in the local currency based on the local labor market, and not tied to USA pay or ranges. Your geographic location will be confirmed during the recruitment.

Who We Are:

The Nature Conservancy’s mission is to protect the lands and waters upon which all life depends. As a science-based organization, we create innovative, on-the-ground solutions to our world’s toughest challenges so that we can create a world in which people and nature thrive. We’re rooted in our mission and guided by our values, which include respect for all people, communities, and cultures. Whether it’s career development, flexible schedules, or a rewarding mission, there’s many reasons to love life inside TNC. Want a better insight to TNC? Check out our TNC Talent playlist on YouTube to hear stories from staff or visit Glassdoor.

One goal is to cultivate an inclusive work environment so that all our colleagues around the globe feel a sense of belonging and that their unique contributions to our mission are valued. In addition to the requirements in our job postings, we recognize that people come with talent and experiences outside of a job and consider each applicant’s unique experience. Please apply – we’d love to hear from you. To quote a popular saying at TNC, “you’ll join for the mission, and stay for the people.”

What We Bring:


Since 1951, TNC has been doing work you can believe in. Through grassroots action, we have grown from a small non-profit into one of the most effective and wide-reaching environmental organizations in the world. Thanks to more than 1 million members, over 400 scientists, and the dedicated efforts of our diverse staff and partners, we impact conservation around the world!

TNC offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package including health care benefits, flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) plan with an 8% employer match, parental leave, accrued paid time off, life insurance, disability coverage, employee assistance program, other life and work well-being benefits. Learn more about our Benefits and Perks here.

We’re proud to offer a flexible work environment that supports of the health and well-being of the people we employ.

Our recruiting process includes a rolling interview process to ensure we engage applicants in a timely manner. This means we may review applications in the order in which they are received. Once a strong candidate pool is identified, the role will be unposted. The timeline may vary depending on the expressed interest in the role, so we highly encourage candidates to apply as soon as possible.

The Nature Conservancy is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Our commitment to equal employment opportunity includes the recognition that our conservation mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people of all backgrounds, beliefs, and culture. Recruiting and mentoring staff to create an inclusive organization is a priority, and we encourage applicants from all cultures, races, colors, religions, sexes, national or regional origins, ages, disability status, sexual orientation, gender identity, military, protected veteran status or other status protected by law.

The successful applicant must meet the requirements of The Nature Conservancy's background screening process.

Do you have military experience? Visit our U.S. Military Skills Translator to match your military experience with our current job openings!

TNC is committed to offering accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application process. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please send a note to applyhelp@tnc.org with Request for Accommodation in the subject line.

title: Software Engineer
description:
About Pulse


Pulse is an AI transformation and custom development firm based in Indianapolis. We work with mid-market companies, usually 50 to 200+ employees, in manufacturing, financial services, healthcare, nonprofits, and government contracting, plus a few enterprise clients.


Most of these companies haven't started with AI because they think they need perfect data and perfectly run operations first. They don't, and our job is to prove it quickly. A lot of our work starts with a 2-Day AI POC: our engineers sit with a client team, learn how the work actually gets done, and ship a working tool while the strategy work is still happening. 98% of our clients renew.

The Role


You'll own client projects from the first conversation to production. That means finding where AI actually saves time or opens up new revenue, deciding the technical plan, building the whole system, and improving it after it goes live. You'll run multiple projects at a time and work within a very flat organizational structure.


This is a software engineering job first. The model is usually the easy part. What makes a project work is everything around it: clean data models, integrations that don't fall over, tests, monitoring, and code another engineer can pick up. We need people who've built and run real systems, and who now use LLMs as one more tool in that work.


Most projects start with a process someone has run the same way for years. You'll map it step by step until every step is simple, figure out which steps AI can take over, build it, keep a person in the loop where mistakes are expensive, and remove that check once the system has earned trust. A project is done when real hours come off someone's workload.


What You'll Do


  • Learn a client's process fast, onsite or remote, often in hours instead of weeks
  • Decide where AI helps and where it doesn't, and explain that call to a CEO and to their IT lead
  • Build the full system: LLM workflows, agents, integrations with the client's ERP, CRM, email, and files, and the interface people use every day
  • Write evals so you know when outputs are good enough to trust
  • Ship to production and keep improving it once real users are on it
  • Help run 2-Day AI POCs, where the goal is a working tool by the end of day two
  • Leave something behind on every project (skills, MCP connectors, eval sets, templates) so the next one starts ahead


What You Won't Do Here


  • Sit through three hours of status meetings every Monday
  • Wait six weeks for a code review
  • Watch your work die in a change management committee
  • Babysit a single legacy system for two years
  • Write specs for someone else to build


What We're Looking For


  • At least 5 years of professional software engineering experience. This is a hard minimum. We want software engineers who can scale with AI, not prompters who pretend to be software engineers.
  • You've owned production systems: designed them, shipped them, been on the hook when they broke, and fixed them
  • Strong fundamentals in system design, data modeling, testing, and debugging
  • Deep experience in Python or TypeScript (ideally both), building and consuming APIs, and working with relational databases like Postgres
  • Comfortable deploying and running software in the cloud, including CI/CD, logging, and monitoring
  • You've built something on top of LLMs that real people use, and you know the ways it breaks
  • Hands-on experience with Claude Code, MCP servers, or agent frameworks
  • You can explain a technical decision to a CEO in plain English and to an engineer in full detail
  • You like being in front of clients. A big part of this job is listening.
  • You'll tell a client something won't work before you build it anyway


Nice to Have


  • Integrations with ERPs (Odoo, NetSuite), CRMs (HubSpot), or accounting tools (QuickBooks)
  • Consulting, agency, or founder experience
  • Background in manufacturing, healthcare, or financial services


What You'll Learn Here


  • How to structure work so agents can do it reliably
  • Context engineering, meaning how to give a model the right information at the right moment
  • How to evaluate outputs and decide where people stay in control
  • How to scope work, build a roadmap, and run a client relationship yourself


How We Work


Our values are Unwavering Integrity, Trailblazing Creativity, and Speed as Superpower. In practice:


  • We tell clients the truth, including when the answer is "don't use AI for this"
  • We try things that haven't been done in a client's industry yet
  • We price work off roadmaps instead of hours, so nobody is rewarded for stretching a project out. If it can ship in 3 months instead of 6, it ships in 3.
  • We keep the team small on purpose. You'll own more, see more of the business, and your work will be visible to clients and leadership.


What We Offer


  • Competitive base salary, commensurate with experience
  • Equity in Pulse
  • Health, dental, vision
  • PTO we actually want you to take
  • A real desk in a real office with people who make you better
  • Direct access to founders. Sean (CEO) and Jake (COO) are in the trenches with you, not behind a calendar wall.


Details


  • Location: Onsite at our office, 350 Massachusetts Ave #256, Indianapolis, IN 46204
  • Travel: This position will require travel to client sites

title: Senior Manager, Workday Reporting & Analytics
description:
Job Description Summary

Job Description

While we prefer this role to be based in our St. Petersburg, FL office with a hybrid work arrangement, we are open to considering qualified candidates for a remote workstyle based on experience and alignment with business needs


Please note: This role is not eligible for Work Visa sponsorship, either currently or in the future.


The Senior Manager, Workday Reporting & Analytics is responsible for leading the operational execution, governance, quality assurance, and continuous improvement of Workday reporting across Raymond James. This role serves as the primary owner for Workday reporting operations, including report nomenclature, metadata standards, report intake and prioritization, quality controls, administration, and ongoing maintenance of reporting content.


This role manages a team of 2 to 3 individual contributors and ensures the team delivers accurate, consistent and well-governed reporting solutions that support HR leaders, business stakeholders, and enterprise workforce decision-making. The Senior Manager partners closely with HR COEs, Technology, HRIS, business leaders and People Analytics stakeholders to translate business needs into scalable reporting solutions, improve report usability and strengthen confidence in Workday data and reporting outputs.



The role requires deep Workday reporting expertise, strong operational discipline, sound judgment, and the ability to simplify complex data and reporting concepts for a broad range of audiences. The Senior Manager will lead reporting governance, documentation, report lifecycle management, quality assurance, issue resolution, team development and stakeholder engagement across HR reporting operations.


Responsibilities:


  • Own the day-to-day operations of Workday reporting, including report intake, prioritization, assignment, quality review, administration, case management and ongoing maintenance
  • Lead and manage a team of 2 to 3 individual contributors responsible for Workday reporting, analytics support, report administration and content governance
  • Establish and maintain Workday report nomenclature, metadata standards, naming conventions, report descriptions, ownership documentation and lifecycle controls
  • Govern and administer reporting content within the People Analytics Marketplace/Hub, ensuring content is accurate, current, well-organized and easy for stakeholders to understand
  • Build, test, maintain and optimize advanced Workday reports, including Matrix Reports, Composite Reports, calculated fields, dashboards, discovery boards and scorecards
  • Lead quality assurance activities for new and existing Workday reporting solutions, including validation, peer review, user acceptance support and production monitoring
  • Develop and maintain documentation, data dictionaries, report inventories, user guidance and governance materials to support consistent reporting practices
  • Partner with HR, HR Technology, HRIS, Payroll, Finance, Compensation, Talent, HR Business Partners and business stakeholders to understand reporting needs and translate requirements into scalable reporting solutions
  • Elicit complex business requirements using interviews, document analysis, workshops and workflow analysis to define reporting needs, intended users and business outcomes
  • Set and lead execution of the Workday reporting plan, including strategies and templates to present HR data in a meaningful, consistent and actionable way
  • Ensure Workday reporting aligns with HR data governance, privacy, compliance and security expectations, including appropriate access, usage and handling of sensitive employee data
  • Troubleshoot reporting, data and system issues, taking ownership through resolution and engaging cross-functional partners as needed
  • Identify opportunities to optimize reporting processes, reduce duplication, improve report usability and strengthen trust in HR data
  • Provide coaching, feedback and development support to team members, including prioritization guidance, performance management and capability building
  • Communicate reporting insights, risks, operational updates and recommendations clearly to HR leaders and business stakeholders
  • Support ongoing and ad hoc HR reporting requests in a high-volume, fast-paced environment while balancing operational needs, governance standards and stakeholder expectations
  • Promote reporting best practices and provide informal training or coaching to stakeholders and team members on Workday reporting, data interpretation and reporting standards

Technical Skills:


  • Advanced Workday reporting experience, including Workday Report Writer, Matrix Reports, Composite Reports, calculated fields, dashboards, discovery boards and scorecards
  • Strong understanding of Workday HCM data structures, business objects, security considerations and reporting dependencies
  • Experience with report governance, report lifecycle management, metadata management, naming standards and documentation
  • Experience with Workday Prism, data models or related analytics tools preferred
  • Proficiency with Excel and data validation techniques
  • Experience with data visualization tools such as Tableau, Qlik, ThoughtSpot or similar platforms preferred
  • Ability to review, validate and improve reports created by others for accuracy, usability and alignment to business purpose

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:


  • Strong understanding of HR data, workforce analytics, Workday reporting and HR business processes
  • Ability to manage complexity, evaluate ambiguous information and define practical solutions
  • Strong planning, organizing and prioritization skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
  • Demonstrated ability to build effective teams, set clear expectations and hold team members accountable for delivery and quality
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to translate complex reporting and data concepts into clear, practical business language
  • Sound judgment and decision quality, including knowing when to resolve issues independently and when to escalate
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy, consistency and governance
  • Ability to optimize work processes and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, usability and stakeholder experience
  • Demonstrated customer-service orientation and ability to build trusted relationships with HR and business stakeholders
  • Ability to lead through change, support adoption of new reporting standards and reinforce consistent reporting practices across HR

Education and Experience:


  • Bachelor’s degree required, preferably in Business Administration, Computer and Information Science, Accounting, Human Resources, Analytics, Data Science or a related field
  • 10 to 15 years of general experience in data, analytics, reporting, HR systems, business intelligence or related disciplines preferred
  • 3 to 6 years of managerial experience preferred, including experience leading direct reports or cross-functional reporting resources
  • Significant hands-on experience with Workday reporting required
  • Experience leading reporting governance, report operations, data quality or analytics administration within HR or a similarly complex function preferred

Education

Bachelor’s - Completed (Required)

Work Experience

General Experience - 6 to 10 years, Manager Experience - None

Certifications

RPT provides services to individuals impacted by a variety of behavioral health (addiction/substance abuse and mental health) issues, recognizing that the individuals we serve often times have experienced trauma that affects their development and adjustment. RPT demonstrates a warm and welcoming empathic, hopeful attitude, conveying a philosophy of dual recovery. RPT will be trained in trauma-informed care and will work to help provide services in an environment that is sensitive and responsive which will prevent victimization, abuse, or trauma as a result of the care received.   • Participates in Team Meetings, shift information exchanges, daily cottage briefings and has input in the evaluation and treatment plan progress of each resident.

title: Associate Director, Data, Knowledge & Agentic AI Engineering
description:
About the Role

GSK R&D and Digital & Tech's collective goal is to deliver GSK impact, including the acceleration of the discovery and development of medicines and vaccines to patients. The Labs and CMC Tech function is central to this mission, driving the reimagining and business transformation of our global laboratory and CMC processes. We are actively transitioning from managing raw scientific data to generating structural scientific knowledge—the foundation for how R&D will discover future medicines in a technology-enabled ecosystem.

The Labs CMC Data, Agentic and Knowledge Engineering (DAKE) group architects the data, agentic and knowledge foundations upon which critical R&D processes and scientific workflows depend. Crucially, our operating model relies on a hybrid workforce: AI agents function as "digital workers" to execute hands-on engineering tasks. They generate pipelines, test and deploy them, monitor them in production and remediate failures.

Reporting into the Director of Data, Knowledge and Agentic AI Engineering, the Associate Director, Data, Knowledge & Agentic AI Engineering, leads the design of production data systems for a team and its domains within Labs & CMC. The role defines the architectural, quality, and governance standards the team and its digital workers apply, leads the team's AI-grade data infrastructure, and mentors junior and mid-level engineers.

Why This Role Exists


  • Production System Leadership: Leads the design of production data systems for a Labs & CMC team and its domains, including pipelines that serve multiple downstream consumers and the AI-grade infrastructure beneath them incorporating existing standards and approaches.
  • Defining the Hybrid Workflow: Defines how the team works with digital workers through the architectural standards, quality checks and review patterns their work must meet within our operating model.
  • Capability Mentorship: Improves and implements our engineering standards with respect to code, documentation and governance, and advances mentoring of junior and mid-level engineers.

Key Responsibilities

Domain-Level Data and Agentic Engineering

  • Design and build production data pipelines for your specific Labs and CMC domain, serving multiple downstream scientific consumers.
  • Implement, enforce and extend our team's patterns for agent-generated work, defining exactly what digital workers build and remediate autonomously versus what requires human review within your domain.
  • Integrate digital workers into your team's specific orchestration and observability workflows, applying clear guardrails, tool designs, and human-in-the-loop controls.
  • Lead the response to significant data quality incidents within your team's purview, from initial detection through to permanent resolution.

Context & Semantics Layer

  • Set the context standards for the team's Labs & CMC domains: how definitions, contracts, classification and lineage are captured in the governed context layer, so humans and digital workers can rely on them.
  • Actively contribute to the broader Labs and CMC context layer by feeding your team's hands-on operational experience upward to evolve the platform.

Data Quality & Governance

  • Execute data quality and governance standards for your team's domains, encoding them directly into the context layer so both humans and digital workers apply them by default.
  • Lead local data quality initiatives to achieve measurable outcomes, such as reduced error rates, improved audit readiness, and better downstream AI performance.

AI Data Infrastructure & Lifecycle

  • Extend our AI-grade data infrastructure for your team's specific AI system needs, including novel retrieval architectures, improved real-time data flows, and smart evaluation datasets.
  • Manage the data lifecycle for AI systems within your domain, including versioning, drift monitoring, and the governance of AI artefacts.

Platform Engineering & Mentorship

  • Design cloud data infrastructure for your team's domains, improve our Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and its deployment reliability.
  • Build shared platform components used by multiple engineers and digital workers to reduce setup time for new Labs and CMC data projects.
  • Set and enforce the code and documentation quality standards for your team, written explicitly for a hybrid workforce of humans and digital workers
  • Mentor junior and mid-level engineers through pairing, code review, and direct feedback to visibly improve their capability and independence.

Basic Qualifications

  • 8+ years of data engineering experience, including significant time leading the design and operation of complex production data systems.
  • Deep expertise with modern warehouses or lakehouses, orchestration and transformation frameworks, and batch and streaming architectures.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and operating AI agents or substantial LLM-powered tools inside data engineering workflows, including tool design, evaluation, observability and human-in-the-loop controls.
  • Experience leading the design of AI-grade data infrastructure for production AI systems, including evaluation datasets, retrieval architectures and real-time data flows.
  • Experience leading data lifecycle management for AI systems, including versioning, drift monitoring and governance of AI artefacts.
  • A track record of defining data quality and governance standards for a team or domain that others adopted, with measurable outcomes.
  • Experience leading cloud data infrastructure design with infrastructure as code.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Technical lead for one or more data platforms or significant domains, from first build through to scale.
  • Experience with catalogue, metadata, semantic or lineage infrastructure that AI systems consume.
  • Experience working within highly regulated industries, such as life sciences, where strict data integrity and auditability are non-negotiable mandates.

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Data Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

#AGTech

#GSK-LI



Skills

Computer Programming, Data Analysis, Data Architecture Development, Databricks Unified Data Analytics Platform, Data Engineering, Data Governance, Data Ingestion, Data Integration, Data Migrations, Data Modeling, Data Transformation, ETL Development, Performance Optimizations, Performance Tuning, Structured Query Language (SQL)

Why GSK?

Uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together.

GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. We aim to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade, as a successful, growing company where people can thrive. We get ahead of disease by preventing and treating it with innovation in specialty medicines and vaccines. We focus on four therapeutic areas: respiratory, immunology and inflammation; oncology; HIV; and infectious diseases – to impact health at scale.

People and patients around the world count on the medicines and vaccines we make, so we’re committed to creating an environment where our people can thrive and focus on what matters most. Our culture of being ambitious for patients, accountable for impact and doing the right thing is the foundation for how, together, we deliver for patients, shareholders and our people.

title: Regional Service Manager Outsourcing Services - regio Noord
description:
Bij SD Worx werk je in een omgeving waar collegialiteit, vertrouwen en zingeving centraal staan.
Je krijgt ruimte om te groeien, met opleidingen en doorgroeikansen die passen bij jouw ambities.
We geloven in hybride werken en denken mee over wat jij nodig hebt om je goed te voelen — op én naast het werk.
Meer dan een loonstrookje? Absoluut!
Hier bouw je aan een carrière die ertoe doet.

Wat doen we?

De unit outsourcing treedt op als externe personeelsdienst voor klanten. Dit kan zowel op tijdelijke basis wanneer klanten door onvoorziene omstandigheden extra hulp nodig hebben, maar ook structureel, wanneer klanten verkiezen om hun personeelsadministratie, inclusief de loonvoorbereiding en loonberekening aan SD Worx uit te besteden. Met haar modulair aanbod neemt deze dienst gericht taken van klanten over en voert deze zo performant en kostenefficiënt mogelijk uit, ter plaatse bij de klanten of vanuit onze kantoren.

Voor deze unit zoeken we een inspirerende people manager met een passie voor HR, dienstverlening en commerciële groei. Je combineert leiderschap met ondernemerschap en bouwt samen met je team aan duurzame klantrelaties en een sterke dienstverlening.

Hoe ziet jouw dag eruit?

  • Je inspireert, coacht en ontwikkelt een team van payroll advisors. Je creëert een omgeving waarin medewerkers kunnen groeien, eigenaarschap opnemen en samen excellente resultaten neerzetten.

  • Je bent verantwoordelijk voor het implementeren van changeprojecten in je team in functie van implementatie van nieuwe systemen, tools en processen. Optimalisatie en efficiëntie staan bij ons voorop.

  • Je werkt nauw samen met teamleaders, regionale directeurs en andere stakeholders om de groei van de regio te ondersteunen, klantrelaties te versterken en commerciële opportuniteiten te benutten.

  • Je bewaakt de kwaliteit, efficiëntie en continuïteit van de dienstverlening en zorgt samen met je team voor een uitstekende klantbeleving.

  • Je volgt de nieuwste ontwikkelingen binnen de payroll (markt) en loonadministratie op de voet.

  • Je bouwt je netwerk verder uit, zowel intern als extern.

  • Je zorgt voor een optimale inzet van medewerkers, waarbij talenten en expertise maximaal aansluiten bij de behoeften van de klant.

  • Je detecteert marktnoden bij klanten en vertaalt deze naar de oplossingen die SD Worx aanbiedt. Zo help je klanten hun organisatie verder te versterken en bouw je duurzame partnerships uit.

  • Je volgt binnenkomende leads op met het oog op groei van de unit.

  • Je bewaakt de financiële gezondheid van je regio, met aandacht voor facturatie, omzetontwikkeling en openstaande vorderingen.

Wat verwachten we van jou?

  • Je bent een sterke people manager die medewerkers inspireert, coacht en laat groeien. Je bouwt aan een performante en betrokken teamcultuur.

  • Je bent communicatief sterk. Naast het dagelijks aansturen van je medewerkers ga je op een constructieve manier in gesprek met klanten over onze dienstverlening.

  • Je neemt initiatief, denkt ondernemend en voelt je comfortabel in een omgeving waar autonomie, verantwoordelijkheid en resultaatgerichtheid centraal staan.

  • Je komt terecht in een dynamische wereld waarbij verandering een constante is, kortom: een snel veranderende wereld is voor jou de ideale omgeving. Je haalt veel voldoening om deze verandering eigen te maken met je team.

  • Je ontwikkelt commerciële opportuniteiten binnen je regio door klantbehoeften, marktontwikkelingen en leads actief op te volgen. Je bouwt duurzame klantrelaties uit en positioneert SD Worx als strategische HR-partner met oplossingen die bijdragen aan groei en toegevoegde waarde.

  • Je begrijpt de uitdagingen van kmo's en middelgrote ondernemingen en kan hun behoeften vertalen naar oplossingen met toegevoegde waarde.

Samen met de andere Regional Service Managers draag je actief bij aan nationale strategische initiatieven en vertaalt deze naar concrete acties binnen je regio. Je speelt een voortrekkersrol in transformatietrajecten rond digitalisering, AI, flexibele workforce, hybride rollen en samenwerking over teams heen.

Je volgt de prestaties van je regio nauwgezet op aan de hand van duidelijke KPI’s rond klanttevredenheid, groei, omzet, rendabiliteit, personeelsbezetting en operationele efficiëntie. Op basis van deze inzichten stuur je gericht bij en realiseer je duurzame resultaten.

title: Director, Data, Knowledge & Agentic AI Engineering
description:
About the Role

GSK R&D and Digital & Tech’s collective goal is to deliver GSK impact, including the acceleration the discovery and development of medicines and vaccines to patients. R&D Digital & Tech are the key Tech partner to support the R&D Ambition of bringing more medicines and vaccines to our projected 2.5 billion Patients and support our scientists by supercharging R&D with Data.

The Labs and CMC Tech function is central to this mission, driving the reimagining and business transformation of our global laboratory and CMC processes. We are actively transitioning from managing raw scientific data to generating structural scientific knowledge—the foundation for how R&D will discover future medicines in a technology-enabled ecosystem. This role operates within a highly complex, end-to-end R&D environment spanning 17 sites, supporting approximately 5,000 scientists, and requiring the integration of both modern software and legacy systems.

The Labs CMC Data, Agentic & Knowledge Engineering (DAKE) group architects the data, agentic and knowledge foundations upon which critical R&D processes and scientific workflows depend. Our engineers are responsible for designing pipelines, modeling complex data, building multi-agent systems, and shipping trusted, reliable infrastructure from end to end.

Crucially, our operating model relies on a hybrid workforce, AI agents function as "digital workers" to execute hands-on engineering tasks. These agents autonomously generate, test, deploy, and monitor pipelines in production, while also remediating failures. The human engineers in our organization are responsible for designing the overarching systems, guardrails, and environments in which these digital workers operate.

The Director, Data, Knowledge & Agentic AI Engineering is accountable for leading and evolving this integrated team of human engineers and digital workers. You will surface data, knowledge, and agents to champion an "Agent-first, Prediction-first" architecture and deliver transformative solutions across the business.


Why This Role Exists

  • Strategic Engineering Leadership: This role advances the overarching engineering direction for data, knowledge, and agentic architecture, championing and embedding agent-driven practices across multiple technical teams.
  • Defining the Digital Worker Ecosystem: Role is to advance the operational ecosystem for our AI agents. You will define the rigorous standards, frameworks, system contracts, and safety guardrails that empower "digital workers" to build and operate data pipelines securely, consistently, and at enterprise scale.
  • Organizational Force Multiplier: This role exists to serve as a critical force multiplier across the Labs and CMC function. By actively mentoring senior and staff engineers, you will directly shape the overarching engineering culture and elevate technical standards across the organization

Key Responsibilities

Context & Semantics Layer Development

  • Unified Context Product: Lead the implementation and evolution of the Labs and CMC context layer as a foundational product. Unify knowledge, data, vocabularies, and ontologies into a single layer that is seamlessly queried by humans and multi-agent systems at runtime to underpin business processes and scientific workflows.
  • Core Dependencies & Protocols: Build the foundational capabilities this layer relies on, including configuration-first engineering, zero-touch deployment frameworks, cataloging, and AI-assisted metadata enrichment. Ensure secure agent access and routing across sources via standard protocols like A2A and MCP.

Agent-Operated Data Engineering Ecosystem

  • Digital Worker Frameworks: Enhance the existing architectural standards and shared frameworks that digital workers use to autonomously generate, test, deploy, and monitor data, knowledge, and agentic engineering pipelines.
  • Operational Governance: Establish the operating model for agent-generated work by clearly defining which tasks are autonomous, which require human approval, how quality is evaluated, and how incidents escalate.
  • Complex Incident Remediation: Lead the resolution of complex incidents that fall outside the remediation capabilities of digital workers, driving them from initial detection through to permanent resolution.

AI Data Infrastructure & Lifecycle Strategy

  • Infrastructure Strategy: Extend the overarching cloud native AI data infrastructure strategy for Labs and CMC, encompassing data and knowledge engineering, vector and retrieval architectures, streaming data flows, and evaluation data design.
  • Shared Production Components: Extend and maintain scalable, shared infrastructure components that support multiple AI initiatives in a production environment.

Governance, Quality & Responsible AI

  • Encoded Governance Controls: Advance and enforce responsible data governance standards for Labs and CMC, incorporating rigorous controls for privacy, consent, PII, auditability, and bias. Encode these standards directly into the context layer so they are applied by default by both humans and digital workers.
  • Lineage & Quality Outcomes: Drive data and knowledge quality and lineage at scale across multiple domains, focusing on measurable improvements in error rates, downstream AI performance, and audit readiness.

Platform Operations & Infrastructure as Code (IaC)

  • Platform-as-Product: Embrace a platform-as-product mindset leveraging GSK-approved data platforms and comprehensive infrastructure as code to ensure new data and AI projects can launch quickly and consistently.
  • Component Ownership: Contribute to and leverage shared platform components essential for AI initiatives, and take ultimate ownership of their reliability, performance, cost-efficiency, and security in production.

Technical Standards & Engineering Leadership

  • Hybrid Workforce Standards: Advance comprehensive engineering standards for code, documentation, and review that are designed to be followed equally by human engineers and digital workers, driving their adoption across the organization.
  • Capability Building: Mentor and develop senior engineers toward greater architectural independence. Partner collaboratively with forward-deployed engineers (FDEs), ML engineers, platform teams, and domain experts to define and deliver the exact requirements for production AI systems.

Basic Qualification

  • 10+ years of advanced data and knowledge engineering experience, with a significant portion dedicated to defining the architecture for production AI or ML systems operating at high scale and complexity.
  • Deep, hands-on expertise in building resilient AI data infrastructure, encompassing data products, knowledge stores, feature stores, vector databases, retrieval architectures, streaming data flows, and rigorous evaluation datasets.
  • Proven experience constructing the metadata, context, and semantic infrastructure consumed by AI systems—including knowledge graphs, ontologies, catalogs, and business glossaries—and exposing these resources to agents via protocols such as MCP.
  • Demonstrated ability to design and operate multi-agent systems, AI agents, or LLM-powered systems embedded within data workflows, including the implementation of evaluation frameworks, safety guardrails, and human-in-the-loop controls.
  • A strong track record of establishing and enforcing data quality, lineage, and governance standards specifically tailored for AI pipelines. This includes robust management of privacy, consent, PII, and auditability adopted across multiple data domains.
  • Expert command of enterprise cloud data platforms and Infrastructure as Code (IaC), coupled with a history of setting high-level engineering standards that other teams successfully adopted.

Preferred Qualification

  • Senior Leadership History: Prior experience operating at a Staff, Principal, or equivalent technical leadership level within an organization managing a non-trivial data engineering function dedicated to AI.
  • Regulated Environments: Experience working within highly regulated industries, such as life sciences, where strict data integrity and auditability are non-negotiable mandates.

Education

  • Bachelor's or master’s degree in computer science, Data Engineering, or a closely related technical field.

#AGTech

#GSK-LI



Skills

Computer Programming, Data Analysis, Data Architecture Development, Databricks Unified Data Analytics Platform, Data Engineering, Data Governance, Data Ingestion, Data Integration, Data Migrations, Data Modeling, Data Transformation, ETL Development, Performance Tuning, Structured Query Language (SQL)

Why GSK?

Uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together.

GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. We aim to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade, as a successful, growing company where people can thrive. We get ahead of disease by preventing and treating it with innovation in specialty medicines and vaccines. We focus on four therapeutic areas: respiratory, immunology and inflammation; oncology; HIV; and infectious diseases – to impact health at scale.

People and patients around the world count on the medicines and vaccines we make, so we’re committed to creating an environment where our people can thrive and focus on what matters most. Our culture of being ambitious for patients, accountable for impact and doing the right thing is the foundation for how, together, we deliver for patients, shareholders and our people.

title: Preserve Management Assistant
description:
What We Can Achieve Together:


We are hiring two (2) Preserve Management Assistants to work out of our Tallgrass Aspen Parklands (TAP) office in Karlstad, MN. This is a seasonal, full-time (40 hours/week) position with an anticipated start date of April 5, 2027 and end of October 22, 2027.

The Tallgrass Aspen Parklands landscape contains over 300,000 acres of conservation land, including almost 16,000 acres of land directly managed by TNC. It hosts a number of charismatic species, including elk, bear, wolves and others. As our Preserve Management Assistant, you will work closely with partners in land management, including the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources and the U.S. Fish and Wildlife service. You will assist in all aspects of prairie management, including:

  • Prescribed fire.
  • Invasive species removal using herbicides and other methods.
  • Prairie restorations, including seed collection, planting, and maintenance.
  • Data collection and monitoring.
  • Maintenance of preserve facilities and equipment.

Wildland fire is a major part of land management in the TAP, so you will gain experience operating equipment and working with large interagency teams.

Shared, dorm style housing and basic utilities are provided by TNC at no cost to the employee upon signing and agreeing to housing terms, and the employee must live in the provided housing to meet the needs and nature of the position and to maximize the effectiveness of the crew.


Some overtime may be expected. You will work outdoors in variable weather conditions, in remote locations, at times on difficult and uneven terrain, and under physically demanding circumstances.



We’re Looking for You:


Guided by science, TNC creates innovative, on-the-ground solutions to our world’s toughest challenges so that people and nature can thrive together. This position is a great introduction to a conservation career focused on land management. You can expect to gain experience in prairie conservation and restoration techniques in the context of large intact natural areas. So, if you’re looking for a career to help people and nature, and enjoy working outdoors, we invite you to apply today!


What You’ll Bring:

  • High school diploma or GED and 1 year’s training in science-related field or related experience in land management.
  • Experience recognizing plant and animal species.
  • Experience operating various types of equipment in a safe and efficient manner (e.g. 4x4 trucks, trailers, chainsaws, UTVs, ATVs or OHVs, tractors, two-way radios, or similar equipment).
  • Experience working in a team environment.
  • Experience working independently
  • Must be able to obtain related licenses or certifications as required. (e.g. First Aid, CPR, herbicide application, basic federal firefighting certifications).
  • Must be able to pass a fitness test (walk 2 miles, with a 25 lb. load within 30 minutes)
  • Must have a valid driver’s license

This position requires a valid driver's license and compliance with TNC’s Auto Safety Program. Employees may not drive Conservancy-owned/leased vehicles, rental cars, or personal vehicles on behalf of the Conservancy if considered "high risk drivers." To learn more about the Auto Safety Program, visit the Auto Safety information page. Employment in this position will be contingent upon completion of a Vehicle Use Agreement, which may include a review of the prospective employee's motor vehicle record.

Salary Information:

The starting pay range for a candidate selected for this position is generally within the range of $18.60 – 19.65/hour. This range only applies to candidates whose country of employment is the USA. Where a successful candidate’s actual pay will fall within this range will be based on a variety of factors, including, for example, the candidate's location, qualifications, specific skills, and experience. Please note countries outside the USA would have a different pay range in the local currency based on the local labor market, and not tied to USA pay or ranges. Your geographic location will be confirmed during the recruitment.


Who We Are:

The Nature Conservancy’s mission is to protect the lands and waters upon which all life depends. As a science-based organization, we create innovative, on-the-ground solutions to our world’s toughest challenges so that we can create a world in which people and nature thrive. We’re rooted in our mission and guided by our values, which include respect for all people, communities, and cultures. Whether it’s career development, flexible schedules, or a rewarding mission, there’s many reasons to love life inside TNC. Want a better insight to TNC? Check out our TNC Talent playlist on YouTube to hear stories from staff or visit Glassdoor.

One goal is to cultivate an inclusive work environment so that all our colleagues around the globe feel a sense of belonging and that their unique contributions to our mission are valued. In addition to the requirements in our job postings, we recognize that people come with talent and experiences outside of a job and consider each applicant’s unique experience. Please apply – we’d love to hear from you. To quote a popular saying at TNC, “you’ll join for the mission, and stay for the people.”

What We Bring:


Since 1951, TNC has been doing work you can believe in. Through grassroots action, we have grown from a small non-profit into one of the most effective and wide-reaching environmental organizations in the world. Thanks to more than 1 million members, over 400 scientists, and the dedicated efforts of our diverse staff and partners, we impact conservation around the world!

TNC offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package including health care benefits, flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) plan with an 8% employer match, parental leave, accrued paid time off, life insurance, disability coverage, employee assistance program, other life and work well-being benefits. Learn more about our Benefits and Perks here.

We’re proud to offer a flexible work environment that supports of the health and well-being of the people we employ.

Our recruiting process includes a rolling interview process to ensure we engage applicants in a timely manner. This means we may review applications in the order in which they are received. Once a strong candidate pool is identified, the role will be unposted. The timeline may vary depending on the expressed interest in the role, so we highly encourage candidates to apply as soon as possible.

The Nature Conservancy is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Our commitment to equal employment opportunity includes the recognition that our conservation mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people of all backgrounds, beliefs, and culture. Recruiting and mentoring staff to create an inclusive organization is a priority, and we encourage applicants from all cultures, races, colors, religions, sexes, national or regional origins, ages, disability status, sexual orientation, gender identity, military, protected veteran status or other status protected by law.

The successful applicant must meet the requirements of The Nature Conservancy's background screening process.

Do you have military experience? Visit our U.S. Military Skills Translator to match your military experience with our current job openings!

TNC is committed to offering accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application process. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please send a note to applyhelp@tnc.org with Request for Accommodation in the subject line.

title: Sr. Field Performance Coordinator
description:

We train you to work across different teams—from qualifying homes for solar, to installing, to inspecting the final work, and servicing existing systems. Responsibilities

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for assigned service partners or branch

  • Work to pursue and achieve tactical or strategic objectives pertaining to the overall vision and assist in the execution of work necessary to meet short term objectives

  • Lead selected program based projects that require cross-functional engagement with key staff across the organization and external stakeholders

  • Launch initiatives that increase revenue or decrease operations costs by strategically analyzing, defining and implementing key projects

  • Drive expanded business opportunities, programmatic growth and innovation​

  • Complete individual customer projects

  • Resolve field service escalations to resolution

  • Solve escalated tech support questions and provide recommendations on how to mitigate in the future

  • Track and provide feedback loop to Partner or Branch to reduce future escalations

  • Close out escalated tasks as assigned​

  • Review and approve Service Partner and sub-contractor quotes

  • Initiate and close out Insurance claims

  • Oversee service territory set up in Scheduling Software Tool

  • On-boarding of new Partners, Branches and Service Technicians

  • Deliver on-going training to existing Partners, Branches and Service technicians

  • Off-boarding of and continued management of Partners


Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s Degree in a technical area of study or significant related experience or training required

  • Minimum of 1 - 3 years relevant work experience

  • Partner and/or project management experience

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills

  • Excellent organizational skills

  • Proactive, energetic and self-motivated

  • Residential solar experience preferred
